However, this timepiece with a custom turquoise dial holds a special place – it was gifted to Young by his wife, Shelby Young, for his third All-Star appearance in 2024. It also features an inscription that reads “Love, Shelby, Tydus, Teal.” “It says my wife’s name and my son and my daughter’s name. So that one’s very special to me,” Young explained during the podcast. For his fourth All-Star, Shelby gifted Young another Rolex classic, the Rolex Datejust Mint Green Jubilee, which WatchGuys listed at US$13,000. Audemars Piguet Royal Oak blue dial Among his several timepieces, Young highlights his Audemars Piguet Royal Oak, which features a blue dial, as the piece that he wears most frequently. “I wear that a lot. That’s one of my favourite watches. I wear it constantly,” he told Altieri. He went on to reveal that he’d acquired the piece after signing his first contract extension. WatchGuys estimates the watch to cost US$50,000. Hublot Classic Fusion black dial (custom case) Young owns more than one wristwatch from Hublot. The NBA star fell in love with the brand after hearing Jay-Z – whose love for the brand is famously documented – name-drop Hublot in a lyric of his 2011 track “Otis” with Kanye West. The Hublot Classic Fusion black dial in his collection features a 42mm dial and a diamond-set titanium bezel. It is estimated to cost US$14,000. Franck Muller Vanguard Moving on to his flashier pieces, Young sported this white Franck Muller Vanguard to Michael Rubin’s all-white party earlier this summer. Originally a women’s watch, the 32mm Vanguard (Ref. V32QZDACE) has a distinct tonneau-shaped case and features diamond embellishments. You can grab yourself a similar model for an estimated US$21,000. Pristine custom made-to-order watches View this post on Instagram A post shared by Pristine Jewelers (@pristine_jewelers) Of his several watches, Young tells Altieri that his favourite is The Azure by Pristine, a custom made-to-order watch from the New York-based Pristine Jewellers that counts the likes of Cardi B, Bad Bunny and Fat Joe as its clients. Covered in icy blue baguette diamonds, the Pristine “Azure” has a hefty price tag of over US$250,000. Young is also the proud owner of a rare Pristine Chandelier Black timepiece, which is covered in black round-cut gems. Only 18 of this model were ever made. Its starting price is estimated to be over US$250,000.

title: Good morning Vietnam: Chinese brokers eye neighbouring springboard for overseas expansion
description: Vietnam is still viewed as a prime location for Chinese companies looking to expand overseas and strengthen trade ties with Southeast Asia.
content: When Wang Junhong was helping Chinese brokerage Guotai Junan International establish a foothold in Vietnam, he had to knock on the door of a familiar Chinese bank. As part of the Hong Kong-based firm’s expansion into Southeast Asia, it had acquired a controlling stake of a small Vietnamese securities company in 2019, but it still needed financing to expand its operation. Wang, now chairman of Guotai Haitong Securities (Vietnam), turned to China Construction Bank’s branch in Ho Chi Minh City, drawing on relationships he had built during his years in the financial industry to secure an early financing arrangement. “Trust was already there,” recalled Wang in a recent interview with South China Morning Post. The bank agreed to provide financing, helping the brokerage get its business moving. It was a modest beginning for a Chinese financial institution venturing into unfamiliar market - and a glimpse into how hard it was for mainland brokerages to open doors across overseas markets in their early years. “Some of our core strengths have to be brought over,” he added, referring to the strong network the company had built with Chinese firms. Guotai Junan International entered Vietnam in 2019, when it acquired about a 51 per cent stake in Vietnam Investment Securities - “a small, locally listed brokerage”. It subsequently increased its holding to about 67 per cent. With several years of development, the Vietnamese operation now ranks in the middle of roughly 80 local brokerages in the country. It had around 70 employees and earned more than HK$10 million (US$1.3 million) annually, having wiped out its accumulated losses, according to Wang. The expansion came as Chinese securities firms were seeking to broaden their overseas presence, with Southeast Asia seen as a major springboard given its proximity to China and close trade ties. China Galaxy Securities began its regional push through a partnership with Malaysia’s CIMB Group in 2017, subsequently taking full ownership of the securities business in 2023. Its international arm, CGS International, has since established a significant presence across the region, ranking among the leading stockbrokers in Malaysia, Singapore, Indonesia and Thailand. Guotai Junan had established operations in Singapore earlier, but Wang said the market’s maturity meant there was less room for rapid expansion in certain areas, including corporate financing. “In a mature market, everything has already been built,” Wang said, explaining why the firm looked towards developing economies for its next opportunity. For Wang, Vietnam offered something different: a young population, growing consumer demand and a capital market still finding its feet. He sees echoes of China two decades ago in the country’s economic transformation. Young Vietnamese consumers, he observed, were eager to buy homes, cars and smartphones – often willing to borrow to enjoy them sooner. That appetite for consumption, Wang believes, will eventually translate into greater demand for investment and financial services.

title: Meet Wicker star Marli Siu, who was born in Hong Kong
description: The actress, who has won a Bafta Scotland Award, stars alongside Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård and Peter Dinklage in the romantic fantasy.
content: One of the most highly anticipated films of 2026 is Alex Huston Fischer and Eleanor Wilson’s Wicker. Starring Olivia Colman and Alexander Skarsgård, it follows a lonely fisherwoman who commissions a weaver to make her a husband out of wicker, only for the creation to come to life, sparking an enviable romance. The cast includes Peter Dinklage as the Basket Weaver, Elizabeth Debicki as the Tailor’s Wife and Marli Siu as the Bottle-Washer’s Wife. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Wicker Movie (@wickermovie) Wicker, which is based on the short story The Wicker Husband by Ursula Wills-Jones, premiered at the Sundance Film Festival in January. “I can’t wait for you to see this film, it’s so good,” Siu wrote on her Instagram at the time. The film was released in some US cinemas on Friday, before a wider roll-out later this month. So, what do we know about Marli Siu? What is Marli Siu’s background? Marli Siu was born on March 11, 1993, and grew up on Lamma Island, Hong Kong, according to her IMDb profile. The Guardian reported that her father is Chinese, and her mother is Scottish. She spent the first four years of her life in Hong Kong before moving to Forres, Scotland, where she lived with her mother – whom she described as a “big hippy” – and four sisters. “Hong Kong Island is so different, fast-paced, full of massive buildings. Lamma was a bit more slow-paced. I wish I could go back more,” she told The Guardian. She has fond memories of the city, especially the “little things – the food, the markets, how I was always barefoot, me and my sisters would play outside a lot,” the actress recalled. How did Marli Siu get into acting? During her time in Scotland, Siu took art and dance lessons, per The Guardian. She caught the acting bug at 15 after discovering a local drama group. “I didn’t know it was a job, no one in my family did it,” she mused. During her secondary school years, Siu considered studying art, but grew curious about acting after wandering into the film department during an open day. She eventually studied acting and English at Edinburgh Napier University, started acting in student shorts, and decided to pursue acting as a career. She would travel to London from Scotland by bus for her auditions. Once she started booking roles, she moved to Walthamstow. What roles has Marli Siu played? On stage, Marli Siu is best known for playing Lettie Hempstock in the National Theatre’s 2019 production of The Ocean at the End of the Lane. Her television credits include Dixi, Everything I Know About Love, Alex Rider and Twenty Twenty Six. She won a Bafta Scotland for her performance as Kelly in the 2019 film Run. The 33-year-old also starred in the films Our Ladies (2019) and Apartment 7A (2024) and wrote the 2017 short Isla.

title: Kenya reports second Ebola death, a close relative of first patient
description: The 65-year-old woman began showing symptoms 10 days ago and died while receiving care at an infectious disease unit.
content: Kenya’s health ministry announced the country’s second Ebola death on Friday, saying a 65-year-old woman who was a close relative of the first patient died after developing symptoms while in quarantine. The woman began showing symptoms 10 days ago and began receiving supportive care at an infectious disease unit in the capital, Nairobi. The ministry said medical personnel “did everything possible to save her life”, but she died Friday evening. Her family was notified, and the ministry said it would arrange a safe and dignified burial in consultation with relatives. The remaining seven Ebola patients were receiving treatment at two isolation facilities. No new infections were reported. Kenya announced its first ever Ebola case on October 6 after a 40-year-old Kenyan man who was living in Congo travelled to Kenya via Uganda, arriving on October 3. He was driven by a relative to Nairobi Hospital, where he tested positive for Ebola on October 5 and died the same day. Authorities have identified some 135 contacts of the first patient, placing 118 in quarantine. Eight tested positive while in quarantine, including four health workers and four close family members. The health ministry said some contacts who completed the 21-day quarantine period without developing symptoms would be released starting Saturday. Ebola is highly contagious and spreads through direct contact with the bodily fluids of an infected person, including blood and vomit, or through contact with contaminated materials and surfaces, such as bedding and clothing. Congo is experiencing its deadliest outbreak, with at least 4,000 deaths since May.

title: Trump to cut some Canada tariffs to help Maine lawmaker’s re-election bid
description: Susan Collins one of the most endangered incumbent Senate Republicans in the coming midterms.
content: The Trump administration is expanding tariff exemptions to more Canadian products, a move that may help boost Republican US Senator Susan Collins’ re-election campaign in Maine. Collins announced in a statement on Friday that the exemptions would apply to certain paper, plastic, machinery and seaweed products, saying they would help the state’s rural and coastal economy, including the blueberry, potato, apple and seaweed industries. “Many of our farmers and growers rely on specialised equipment, packaging materials and other products from Canada that are either unavailable from American suppliers or cannot be replaced without incurring significant expense,” she said. Trump will amend the tariffs to add new ones to replace the exclusions so that the overall tariff impact is unchanged, a US official said. A fact sheet released on Friday said tariffs on certain Canadian imports – including plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment and certain packing crates and boxes – would be replaced with duties on “certain valves, carpets, waste products and others”. The changes will take effect on October 30, the fact sheet said. Collins, who is in a competitive re-election race, has touted her ability to secure tariff reductions that affect Maine consumers and businesses. Her office said she had pushed for additional exemptions during conversations with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Democratic Senate candidate Troy Jackson responded on Friday that Collins “wants credit for bringing a cup of water to put out the fire”, arguing that she acted only because she was at risk of losing her seat. “We deserve a Senator who stands up to Trump – not one who rubber-stamps his agenda and begs for relief from the chaos she helped create,” Jackson said on social media. US President Donald Trump previously exempted road salt and other products last month, following a request from Collins, at the same time that he announced a series of retaliatory measures after US-Canada talks had collapsed. Canada also amended its own retaliatory duties to remove seafood products. The latest changes come with US-Canada trade talks at a standstill. There have been no new substantive discussions since negotiations over a tariff deal imploded in August. Collins is among the most endangered incumbent Senate Republicans this November, though Democrats have failed in previous efforts to unseat her. The move comes as national and state-level polls show voters giving Republicans poor marks over their handling of the cost of living and Trump’s war in Iran. Collins has frequently defied polls and adverse political environments to maintain her seat, but she is battling rising prices – including for housing and fuel – that have made life less affordable for many in Maine. Jackson has hammered Collins over the tariffs, arguing she could better leverage her position as chair of the powerful appropriations committee to force Trump to drop them. Collins has sought to distance herself from the president, saying in a recent debate that she was “not exactly his favourite senator”. The Republican senator has taken credit for pushing back on his tariff agenda, including by obtaining the road-salt exemption. That prompted her opponent Jackson to retort on the debate stage that Maine voters “can’t eat road salt”. Beyond raising consumer prices and hurting Maine industries such as farming, the trade fight has damaged tourist destinations like Bar Harbor and Ogunquit, as Canadians angry at the US president refrain from taking their usual holidays to the border state.

title: Macron condemns ‘racist terrorist attack’ after deadly shooting near Paris
description: A gunman firing from his car killed 1 person and wounded 5, including a 12-year-old girl who was shot 8 times.
content: A gunman firing from a car killed one person and wounded five – including a 12-year-old girl shot eight times – in the Paris suburbs on Friday, in what the French president called a “racist terrorist attack”. The man was “firing at random, wanting to cause a bloodbath” as he drove through the working-class town of Trappes southwest of Paris and neighbouring La Verriere, Trappes mayor Ali Rabeh said. Most of the victims were from foreign backgrounds and prosecutors are investigating whether the acts targeted the “real or supposed race, ethnicity, nationality or religion” of the victims. “What happened here today was a racist terrorist attack,” said French President Emmanuel Macron, visiting Trappes later. “This is a turning point because it is the first time there has been a terrorist act aimed at killing our compatriots and our children for the colour of their skin or what their religion is thought to be,” he said. “We must not yield anything to the ideas that are taking root in the Republic that could justify such behaviour.” The 12-year-old girl shot eight times was “seriously wounded” but in a stable condition, the mayor of La Verriere, Nicolas Dainville, said. Police arrested the alleged shooter – a 39-year-old man, according to a source familiar with the case – in nearby Coignieres. Officers found him in possession of a submachine gun and tear-gas grenades, according to a police source. He had also booby-trapped his flat with three gas canisters and electric wires “connected to a timer”, according to anti-terrorism prosecutors. Prosecutors said they had opened an investigation for “murder in connection with a terrorist enterprise”. Rabeh said the man was firing sporadically from his car and that the person killed was “of African origin”. One of the wounded, “in critical condition, is of North African origin”, he added. It was “objectively a racist, probably Islamophobic attack,” the mayor said, calling for national unity as the toll rose from an earlier count of four wounded. Dainville said that two of the wounded in his town – cleaners attending to a school on Friday morning when the shooter got out of his car to open fire – were of African origin. Laurent Nunez, France’s interior minister, travelled to the two affected towns. He called the shooting “clearly a terrorist crime”. A police source said that the man had fired in bursts from his vehicle around 10.30am. Adel, a resident of Trappes, about 20km (13 miles) west of Paris, said his “heart was broken” as he learned the victims might have been targeted for their race. “I’m North African and it’s frightening for everyone who has the same background,” the 50-year-old man said. Samy, another resident, said he had seen a body on the ground from his window. His mother, he said, saw a grey Renault Clio car speeding by and heard “loud bangs”. Writing on social media, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said the case was “very serious” and that “all resources of the security forces and the judiciary are fully mobilised”. Macron earlier in the day said “the nation is standing with” the victims of this “terrible ordeal”. The shooting came with France on edge following last weekend’s riots on the sidelines of mass protests over the cost of living, some of the worst street violence in recent years. More protests are expected this weekend, but police will be out in force after a week of overnight curfews put in place in cities throughout the country.

title: Gunmen kill 7 at Jordan church, king vows retaliation
description: Dozens more were wounded in the rare attack on Christians in the majority Sunni Muslim kingdom.
content: Gunmen killed at least seven people and wounded dozens at a church in southern Jordan on Friday, with the king vowing retaliation for the rare attack on Christians in the majority Sunni Muslim kingdom. Assailants stormed the compound of a Greek Orthodox church in the village of Hammoud in Karak governorate and opened fire, authorities said. The gunmen got out of a vehicle and started shooting during a funeral procession, the public security directorate said in a statement, adding that a hunt was under way for the perpetrators. “The terrorist attack against Karak will be met with the harshest retaliation,” King Abdullah II said in an English-language post on social media. “We will strike with an iron fist against those who dare to threaten our nation.” After authorities gave a death toll of six, Director of Public Security Major General Abdullah Al-Maaytah said it had risen to seven with 34 injured, 27 of whom were still receiving treatment. Images from state broadcaster Al-Mamlaka showed the king visiting Karak on Friday evening after the attack. The royal court also shared a video showing the monarch at a local hospital in military uniform to check on the wounded. “This country is ours and we will not abandon it – we will never abandon it,” an injured man told him. Footage aired by Al-Mamlaka also showed the moment of the attack. Two gunmen are seen dressed in casual clothes and brandishing pistols, with a third carrying a long gun, before they open fire on the church from an entrance on the street and charge forward. “A terrorist group has carried out a horrific act, one that is condemned in every respect, and the security services are working round the clock to track them down,” Interior Minister Mazen Al-Faraya told a press conference. “Jordan has been targeted by a terrorist attack carried out by a group of extremists.” He said the perpetrators had “absolutely no connection whatsoever to human values” and it “only serves to strengthen the Jordanians’ resolve … to combat and fight terrorism in all its forms”. Mohammed Al-Khalayleh, minister of awqaf, Islamic affairs and holy sites, said “the sanctity of places of worship is inviolable and any violation of this is unacceptable on religious, moral and national grounds”, calling national unity “a red line that must not be crossed”. Prime Minister Jafar Hassan ordered a three-day period of national mourning from Friday, with flags to be flown at half mast over government and public institutions. Minister of Government Communications Mohammed Al-Momani said security forces were investigating the attack. A witness told Al-Mamlaka the gunmen fired continuously for five minutes before fleeing the scene. Between 150 and 200 people were in and around the church at the time, the witness said, adding that most of the victims were aged between 50 and 70. Karak is home to a significant Christian community in the Muslim-majority kingdom, where Christians make up between 2 and 3 per cent of the population. The Greek Orthodox Archdiocese in Jordan said that if the attack was aimed at driving out Christians from the holy land, “it will only make us cling to it more firmly and deepen our roots in it”. “We are absolutely certain that Jordanian society will remain impervious to every dark, extremist ideology, and that this criminal act is far removed from – and alien to – the moderate Islam of our country,” it said. Lebanese President Joseph Aoun, the Arab world’s only Christian head of state, called the shooting a “heinous terrorist attack”. He said it “reaffirms once again that terrorism has no religion and no homeland, and its aim is to strike at coexistence and spread strife”, according to a presidency statement. A spokesman for UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres said “an attack not only on a place of worship, but during a funeral procession, is especially heinous”. Greek Prime Minister Kyriakos Mitsotakis also condemned the attack, saying on social media that targeting a place of worship was “an affront to our shared humanity”. Attacks on houses of worship in Jordan are rare. In 2016 an attack in Karak targeted a security centre and police patrols, leaving 10 people dead. The victims included seven security personnel and a female tourist, before four militants who had barricaded themselves inside Karak’s historic castle were killed.

title: Melania Trump brokers ceasefire in Russian-occupied Ukraine city, White House says
description: Food and medical supplies have been scarce for months in Oleshky, and the truce will allow for evacuation and the entry of humanitarian aid.
content: Ukraine’s top negotiator involved in a humanitarian mission led by US first lady Melania Trump has said that a local ceasefire with Russia will start on Tuesday – two days before the mission begins – and last several days. Ukrainian, Russian and US negotiators reached a deal on Friday to provide humanitarian aid in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, in the war-divided region of Kherson in southern Ukraine. Dmytro Lubinets, the Ukrainian ombudsman and his country’s chief negotiator in the talks, said the ceasefire would take effect across the Kherson region and neighbouring areas essential to the operation. He added that the initiative could act as a model for future humanitarian missions. The White House said Melania Trump had initiated discussions after learning about the situation at an event she hosted during last month’s UN General Assembly session. It said she and a representative worked directly with Russian and Ukrainian leadership to define the terms of the ceasefire. Russian officials also confirmed the arrangement. Lubinets earlier on Friday thanked Melania Trump for her involvement and said the deal would be tough to accomplish. He said the agreement called for a ceasefire, followed by the delivery of much-needed humanitarian aid. Lastly, civilians would be allowed to leave Oleshky, he said in a video message posted online. “The operation will be carried out gradually and is extremely challenging to implement,” Lubinets said. UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres welcomed the first lady’s announcement. Through spokesman Stephane Dujarric, Guterres said he hoped the local pause in fighting could become a step towards “an immediate, full and unconditional ceasefire” leading to “a comprehensive, just and lasting peace in Ukraine in line with international law”. Lubinets said the operation would involve removing mines on the way to Oleshky before the physical delivery of humanitarian aid and the arranging of evacuations. He gave no further details on how the ceasefire or the aid mission would be monitored or implemented, citing the sensitivity of the negotiations. He declined to comment when asked if Melania Trump would travel to Ukraine but described her involvement as invaluable. “When Melania Trump learned about the situation in Oleshky, the negotiation process began under her coordination,” he said. “For several weeks, we discussed many questions, initiatives and ideas. We established new approaches, mechanisms and tools to do everything possible to help civilians in Oleshky survive.” Russia’s chief of the general staff, General Valery Gerasimov, said Russian forces “will cease fire on the Kherson axis” starting at 4am on Tuesday in Moscow “in connection with the humanitarian operation near Oleshky”. Russian forces would also carry out “engineering reconnaissance” and ensure “safe movement of the humanitarian convoy” into the city, Gerasimov said. Russia’s human rights ombudswoman, Yana Lantratova, confirmed on Friday that Melania Trump had brokered an agreement on “organising a humanitarian mission” in Oleshky. Lantratova, who said she took part in negotiations, said providing such assistance was Russia’s priority. The first step would be to clarify what people need and organise the delivery of food, medicine, hygiene products and other essentials, Lantratova said in an online statement. Safe passage would be guaranteed for anyone who wanted to leave the combat zone, she said, adding that it would require abiding by the ceasefire and creating safe conditions for humanitarian vehicles. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Moscow was grateful to the first lady. He said Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump had recently discussed the effort. Peskov said “those who want to leave it would be able to do so”. He would not say whether they would be taken to Russia- or Ukraine-held territory. He also demurred when asked how long the evacuation would last, saying only it would most probably take several days. Melania Trump has made helping children in conflict zones one of her signature issues in her husband’s second term. She hosted a UN Security Council meeting on the issue earlier this year, and last year wrote to Putin about efforts to reunite families with children who have been displaced by the war. She has helped reunite nearly three dozen children, according to her senior adviser, Marc Beckman. “What she wants to do is save children, and that’s her focus,” the president said about his wife during a question-and-answer exchange with journalists at the White House. Beckman portrayed the first lady’s work on the ceasefire as an extension of her efforts to help reunite Russian and Ukrainian children with their families after they were separated by Russia’s war against Ukraine. Food and medical supplies have been scarce for months in Oleshky, which sits on the Dnipro River that separates Ukrainian forces from the city’s Russian occupiers. There is no electricity, heat or running water. Roads leading from town are mined and dotted with burned-out cars. Drones buzz overhead. Once a city of about 24,000 residents, Oleshky was captured by Moscow’s forces on the first day of their full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. Its buildings were shelled and burned, and its infrastructure damaged. In June 2023, floodwaters inundated the city after the Kakhovka Dam collapsed due to an explosion that an Associated Press investigation found was probably caused by the Russian military. Hundreds of residents were killed. Those left in the city along Ukraine’s southeastern front face death from hunger or disease as another harsh winter looms. Ukraine has appealed repeatedly for a local ceasefire to organise evacuations. Russia, as the occupying power, is obliged by international law to ensure civilians under its control have what they need to survive.

title: France deploys 70,000 police for new protests as Macron delays Africa trip
description: Massive law enforcement mobilised ahead of Saturday’s demonstrations amid calls online for violence and looting.
content: France will deploy some 70,000 police nationwide as it braces for new protests this weekend after some of the worst urban violence in years erupted on the sidelines of demonstrations a week ago, the government said on Friday. President Emmanuel Macron, who, according to aides, is postponing a visit later this month to Nigeria and Senegal amid the crisis, held a meeting of his defence council of top ministers and officials and was to meet security forces. He was also set to host for the first time representatives of high school pupils, whose protests over conditions at their schools sparked the movement that has broadened into a nationwide show of anger against the government at the rising cost of living. Some 70,000 security personnel will be deployed on Saturday, Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said at a press conference in Paris, warning that calls for violence and looting were circulating on social media. The protests have come at a critical moment for France six months ahead of the election to replace Macron, with a new poll underlining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the front runner and showing her position has been strengthened by the latest events. Adding to tensions, Le Pen is over the weekend due to host her National Rally party congress in Orleans, with thousands of supporters expected but local authorities fearing clashes as opponents head to the city. Nunez was expected to visit the city on Friday to “inspect the security arrangements” at the request of the prime minister’s office, it said. At Macron’s meeting with students, “we will present our demands to him, which remain the same: the state of school infrastructure and an overhaul of the Parcoursup (university admissions) system”, said Nathanael Combary, president of Renouveau Lyceen (High School Renewal). Macron’s government has sought to draw a line between the legitimate demands of protesters and the looting, burning and ransacking that erupted on the sidelines of protests last Saturday. In a judicial response of unprecedented firmness, courts have already sent 217 people, half of them first-time offenders, to prison over the events on Saturday, Justice Minister Gerald Darmanin said. On Thursday, Macron called for “the utmost severity” against “acts of delinquency”, accusing “ultra-left” groups of having sought to “bring down the republic” last weekend. On Saturday, a second round of demonstrations is expected across France. Lyon’s city centre in the southeast will be off-limits to demonstrators this weekend, while in Paris protesters will only be allowed to march a limited route between Bastille and Nation squares. Marylise Leon, the general secretary of the CFDT, one of the nation’s largest trade unions, said the measure would ‌do little to restore calm, adding that it would be better for the government to make concrete proposals to address people’s anger. “It’s counterproductive ⁠because there is a lot of ⁠anger, a lot of anger and a demand to be considered and to be listened to,” she told French broadcaster TF1. “It’s not for the president to decide who can legitimately request to protest.” Authorities in Marseille had also banned protests but announced on Friday that a union-organised demonstration would be allowed on an “exceptional basis” – the only one authorised in the southern Bouches-du-Rhone department. They also reversed a decision to suspend all public transport in the city on Saturday. But in the capital, leading museums including the Louvre will be closed on Saturday while the Art Basel art fair is being cut short. Some 20 per cent more members of the security forces will be deployed this weekend after heavy criticism of the anticipation and intelligence gathering of police last week. “In a country governed by the rule of law, the police have a responsibility both to ensure that protests can take place peacefully and safely and to protect the public from violent disorder,” said Eva Cosse, senior Europe researcher at Human Rights Watch, expressing alarm over reports of children being severely injured by crowd-control weapons. Meanwhile, a deadly shooting in a town outside Paris on Friday was “a racist, probably Islamophobic attack”, the mayor of Trappes said, as authorities moved to investigate the case as a “terrorist” incident. Interior Minister Nunez, visiting the area where at least two victims were of foreign origin, said the gunman, who killed one person and wounded five others, “clearly” committed “a terrorist crime”. The violence has tarnished the image of France ahead of an election that could be a turning point in its modern history, with the government’s debt pile also troubling investors. A new poll by Harris Interactive for M6/RTL made after the violence showed Le Pen soaring ahead on 33-35 per cent in the first round of voting for the presidential election. It predicted that hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon was on course to face her in the run-off, where Le Pen would emerge as an easy winner on some 70 per cent of the vote. Additional reporting by Reuters

title: Asian Para Games: no gold for Hong Kong, but table tennis team keep medals coming
description: Wong Ting-ting leads way with her third medal at Aichi-Nagoya as she partners Ng Mui-wui to doubles silver; badminton also wins bronze.
content: The para table tennis team are quickly becoming the city’s most successful group at the current Asian Para Games at Aichi-Nagoya after taking home a few more medals on Friday. On the penultimate day of the seven-day event, Ng Mui-wui partnered Wong Ting-ting to win the women’s doubles (class 22) silver medal after the pair overcame Chinese Taipei duo Li Jing-shiuan and Lydia Li Yi-ya 3-1 in their final group match. It was Wong’s third medal from the current games after the 23-year-old also took silver in women’s singles (class 11) and a mixed doubles (class 22) bronze medal. With only three teams competing in the round-robin format, Japanese pair Natsuki Wada and Miya Yamaguchi claimed gold on home soil. A second silver medal for Hong Kong was to follow in the women’s doubles (class 14) final when Chiu Kan-shan and Wong Yue-ching lost in straight games, 11-5, 11-8, 11-8, to Chinese pair Huang Wenjuan and Liu Xiaowu. Earlier in the day, Chiu and Wong had beaten Thailand pair 3-1 in the semi-final to ensure they bettered their previous result, a bronze medal in Hangzhou three years ago. Also contested in a round-robin format was the men’s doubles (class 22) event. Hongkongers Wan Wai-lok and Yuen King-shing beat Mohd Hazlin Abdullah and Jennahtul Fahmi Ahmad Jennah of Malaysia 3-2 to claim a bronze medal with two wins and two losses in the five-team group. South Korea took gold ahead of Chinese Taipei. In men’s doubles (class 18), Ho Ka-shing and Wong Chi-yin had to settle for a bronze medal in consecutive games after they lost 3-1 to Chinese pair Lian Hao and Zhao Shuai at Sky Hall Toyota. There was also a bronze medal in para badminton after veteran Chu Man-kai lost 21-8, 21-19 to Lin Naili of China in the men’s singles (SH6) semi-final at Ichinomiya City Municipal Gymnasium. The 36-year-old Chu also finished fourth and fifth in the men’s doubles and mixed doubles, respectively. Heading into the final day of the Games, Hong Kong have won 35 medals – two gold, 12 silver and 21 bronze medals – from five sports.

title: Hong Kong burnishes gold hub credentials with local refineries deal
description: The agreement will see gold refineries localise production in Hong Kong, allowing the city to create a complete gold trading ecosystem.
content: Hong Kong has taken another step towards building itself into an international gold trading hub, after confirming deals that will see gold refineries localise production in the city. The addition of the local refineries will allow Hong Kong to form a complete gold trading ecosystem, boosting belief in the city’s ability to become a trusted global gold vault, according to analysts. “Hong Kong has been substantiating the idea of a global gold hub now that it no longer needs mainland-based refineries to process the precious metal,” said Ding Haifeng, a consultant at Shanghai-based financial advisory firm Integrity. “A marriage between Hong Kong’s financial system and the mainland’s demand for physical gold is highly likely to give birth to a global gold vault, which could become a key market for price setting.” On Thursday, the Office for Attracting Strategic Enterprises (OASES) – a government unit tasked with attracting companies of strategic importance to Hong Kong – signed agreements with Swiss-based Valcambi and Chinese firm Point Gold International to establish local gold refineries in the city. The deals are part of a wider push by Hong Kong to raise its gold storage capacity to more than 2,000 tonnes within three years. The city previously focused on the processing trade – shipping gold materials to the mainland for refining, before re-exporting them – but is now moving into storing finished gold products. The latest deals came just two weeks after Secretary for Financial Services and the Treasury Christopher Hui Ching-yu visited three Swiss refineries, including Valcambi, as Hong Kong courts the world’s leading gold processors. The city ultimately aims to create a broad gold ecosystem that can attract global traders, processors, consumers and even central banks, as it strengthens its capabilities across trading, clearing and storage. In May, Hui said gold could serve as a “potential bridge” between conventional and new forms of finance, as he envisioned more derivative trading, such as tokenised gold trading via the blockchain. In July, Hong Kong’s new gold clearing and settlement system, Precious Metals Central Clearing, began trial operations, with Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu describing the move as a milestone for the city’s gold hub ambitions. New York and London are currently recognised as the world’s leading gold vaults. Over the past decade, China has also been liberalising its gold market in Shanghai, inviting more international investors to buy and sell bullion listed on the Shanghai Gold Exchange. Hong Kong’s push to transform itself into a global gold trading hub also aligns with Beijing’s diversification of its foreign reserves, which has seen it increasingly buy gold, according to analysts. Official data showed that the People’s Bank of China, China’s central bank, increased its bullion holdings for the 23rd consecutive month in September, bringing the total to 77.47 million troy ounces (2,400 tonnes).

title: Inside the red-hot REM hotel in Macau – think revolving beds and dreamlike suites
description: The 149-room REM hotel at City of Dreams Macau is designed to evoke a sense of dreaminess and fantasy.
content: Melco Resorts & Entertainment’s newest hotel, REM, opened this week to complete the ultra-luxury trio at the City of Dreams in Macau. Rebranded from the Countdown Hotel, which was the Hard Rock Hotel before that, the property sits alongside the Zaha Hadid-designed Morpheus and Asian-inspired Nuwa, positioning itself as the most exclusive of the three. REM stands for rapid eye movement, the phase of sleep during which “we have the most vivid dreams”, said Lawrence Ho Yau-lung, chairman and CEO of Melco Resorts & Entertainment, at the grand opening event on October 20. “That is the vibe we are going after.” Much of the property – from its nightclub-like entrance and lobby, to its 149 rooms and suites – is fluorescent red to evoke a surreal sense of dreaminess and fantasy. REM is not a sleep hotel that promotes the quality of slumbering among guests; instead, it creates a private and intimate environment for them to relax in. Matching the overall theme of dreams are names of the different room types, including the Twilight Suite, Luminous Suite, Euphoria Suite, Hypnotic Suite, The Haven and The Lair. The last is the 12,900 square foot (1,200 square metre) penthouse suite on the 30th floor, a bold statement of opulence and indulgence. The Haven, a 3,000 square foot villa-type suite, is another highlight, featuring a hammock-like swing sofa in the main sitting/ living room, and a gimmicky rotating king-size bed that commands an open view of the neighbourhood when facing the floor-to-ceiling windows. It slowly completes two full 360-degree rotations, then stops automatically, so there is no fear of the bed revolving through the night. The mini bar is hidden behind a half revolving circular door. Though the hotel is suitable for families, the decor in some of these rooms suggests a more mature target audience. In The Haven, for instance, a large digital screen shows a young female model clad in leatherwear, moving slowly into different poses. Judging by the celebrities who showed up at the star-studded grand opening red carpet event, which included Chinese singer/actor Jing Boran, Chinese actress Cai Wenjing, Anson Lo from boy group Mirror and Hong Kong singer-songwriter Tyson Yoshi, REM also sets out to appeal to the cooler, trendy crowd. Room availability at REM will be more limited than the other two Melco hotels: Nüwa has around 300 guest rooms and suites and Morpheus 772. Developed by the joint venture Melco Crown Entertainment and opened in June 2009, the City of Dreams remains one of the major tourist destinations on the Cotai strip in Macau. Other than the three contemporary ultra high-end hotels, the complex is also home to Grand Hyatt Macau and the hugely popular live entertainment show House of Dancing Water, which returned in 2025 with an updated version after a five-year hiatus.

title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang brings ‘sovereign AI’ push to Kazakhstan, shrugs off bubble fears
description: Nvidia CEO calls for the Central Asian nation to transform its ‘energy into intelligence’, as he continues global ‘sovereign AI’ crusade.
content: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is pitching the concept of “sovereign AI” in Kazakhstan – part of his global crusade urging nations to build domestic computing infrastructure using the firm’s chips – as the energy-rich nation emerges as a US-China battleground for artificial intelligence. Speaking at a fireside chat in Astana on Friday with Kazakh AI and digital development minister Zhaslan Madiyev, Huang said AI was reshaping every industry in a transformation that “affects every single person and country”. Huang added that Nvidia provided the computing foundation powering AI hubs, which required vast resources, particularly electricity and data. His remarks come as Kazakhstan seeks to leverage its vast energy reserves to become a regional computing hub by building what Huang calls “AI factories”. The country holds an estimated 25.6 billion tonnes of coal reserves – among the world’s largest – according to the US Energy Information Administration. “Because you have so much energy, instead of just exporting energy in the future, you can transform the energy into intelligence and export intelligence,” Huang said. In June, Kazakhstan announced a US$10 billion plan involving Nvidia and American AI infrastructure developer Firebird to build a computing hub in Ekibastuz, a major coal-mining and power-generation centre. The project envisages deploying around 100,000 Nvidia graphics processing units (GPUs), with total power capacity reaching up to 1 gigawatt. Its initial 50-megawatt facility is scheduled to open in June next year, with Madiyev estimating the hub could eventually generate at least US$3 billion in annual computing export revenue. Still, the region’s ambitions face steep structural obstacles. The Washington-based Carnegie Endowment for International Peace warned in April that Central Asia’s digital push could be constrained by unreliable power grids, limited international connectivity and regulatory barriers. Huang, Nvidia’s 63-year-old founder, has spent much of the past year travelling globally as one of AI’s most prominent evangelists. From Europe to Asia, he has urged governments to build sovereign AI infrastructure – using Nvidia’s coveted chips – to keep control over their own data and cultural capabilities. Just two days before his Astana appearance, Huang pressed European nations to build out their domestic AI infrastructure during Nvidia’s GPU Technology Conference in Berlin, where the firm unveiled new modular data-centre technology. However, Huang’s globe-trotting promotional campaign comes amid mounting scepticism over the financial sustainability of the global AI buildout. Ken Griffin, the billionaire founder of hedge fund Citadel, warned on Wednesday that the AI sector was “almost certainly” in a bubble, raising concerns that an eventual oversupply of computing hardware could drive down prices and undermine the financial returns of megaprojects. His comments echoed earlier warnings from Bridgewater Associates founder Ray Dalio, who described the frenzy as a “classic bubble” nearing a potential peak, as well as the Bank of England, which cautioned last month that mounting debt tied to AI infrastructure could amplify losses if profitability expectations faltered. Huang has brushed off bubble concerns, telling US broadcaster CNBC on Thursday that demand for specialist AI cloud providers remained “off the charts”. Instead, he argued that growth was being bottlenecked by a shortage of working capital across the sector. “What’s missing … is the working capital to fuel that growth, because there are so many demands across so many sectors of AI,” Huang said. Kazakhstan’s push into AI also highlights Central Asia’s growing weight in the technology rivalry between Washington and Beijing. Sharing a roughly 1,700km (1,050-mile) border with China, Kazakhstan has played both sides of the divide. In June, Astana joined Pax Silica – a US-led initiative aimed at securing AI supply chains, energy, chips and data centres – before signing on as a founding member of the China-backed World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation the following month. Meanwhile, Chinese tech companies have expanded their own presence across Central Asia, pursuing telecommunications, cloud infrastructure and AI model partnerships in Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan.

title: Coach of China’s women’s football team leaves post eight months before World Cup
description: Ante Milicic, who helped team qualify for next year’s World Cup in Brazil, will depart ‘after friendly communication’, Chinese FA says.
content: Ante Milicic has left his post as coach of China’s national women’s team, the football association said on Friday, eight months before the World Cup. The 52-year-old Australian had been in charge since May 2024 and led the team to the semi-finals of the Women’s Asian Cup in March. That finish earned them a spot at next year’s World Cup in Brazil. Milicic also recently took China to fourth place at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games in Japan after losing 2-0 to North Korea in the semi-finals. “After friendly communication and consultations between both sides and considering Mr Ante Milicic’s family situation, the Chinese Football Association has decided he will no longer serve as head coach,” the Chinese Football Association (CFA) said in a statement. Milicic’s foreign coaching staff will also leave, the CFA said, thanking them for their “hard work”. The CFA did not immediately name a successor but said it would confirm the national team’s coaching set-up based on its upcoming commitments and continue preparations for the qualifiers for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games. A former striker with the national Australian team, Milicic led the Australia women’s team to the round of 16 at the 2019 Fifa Women’s World Cup. He was also assistant coach with the Australia men’s team at two World Cup campaigns and when the Socceroos won the 2015 Asian Cup. According to the CFA website, Milicic led China in 21 international matches after taking charge in May 2024, recording 10 wins, four draws and seven losses – a 48 per cent win rate – with 40 goals scored and 32 conceded. Following Friday’s announcement, the CFA issued a notice opening public applications for the head coach position. According to the announcement, the new manager will be responsible for leading preparations for the 2027 Women’s World Cup and the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, taking charge of squad building, tactical refinement and talent development. However, a tight fixture list means the CFA has to finalise the appointment in a short time frame. The domestic Chinese Women’s Super League season concludes on November 22, after which the national team will immediately assemble for the Yongchuan Four Nations tournament, playing three matches scheduled for November 27, December 1 and December 5.

title: China, Europe should coordinate on carbon pricing, border tax: energy transition expert
description: Adair Turner urges Beijing and Brussels to unite on emission fees as the US pulls back from climate commitments.
content: China and Europe should jointly introduce a system like the Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), a levy on carbon-intensive imports designed to account for the carbon costs domestic producers face, which “applies against the rest of the world,” the co-chair of a global energy transition organisation says. “The biggest single thing which I would love China to do is to say, ‘We want to join with Europe in a climate club’,” said Adair Turner, co-chair of the Energy Transitions Commission, during a panel discussion at the Bund Summit in Shanghai on Thursday. Turner, who is also the former chairman of the UK’s Financial Services Authority, called on the two economies to commit jointly to carbon prices high enough to drive the decarbonisation of heavy industries such as cement and steel. Calls for closer China-Europe climate cooperation have grown louder as the US retreats from international climate efforts under the Donald Trump administration, including its withdrawal from the Paris Agreement. Meanwhile, the European Union’s CBAM entered its definitive phase in January 2026, requiring importers of covered carbon-intensive goods to pay for embedded emissions under the bloc’s carbon pricing system, which has left many Chinese exporters struggling with compliance. “America has made a bet that the future is fossil fuels. It is a really stupid bet, and they’re going to lose,” Turner said, describing the Trump administration as a “disaster” for dealing with global problems related to the commons. “The future is electric. So let’s be clear: China and … Europe are making the right bet, and the US is going to regret the bet it’s now made.” Jeromin Zettelmeyer, the director of Bruegel, also shared similar ideas at the panel, saying that a joint carbon pricing commitment made by the EU and China would create a market so massive that other developing countries could not afford to ignore it. He pointed to the Open Coalition on Compliance Carbon Markets, launched by the EU, China and Brazil, which he described as a multilateral extension of Europe’s CBAM. “In the end, the US will be isolated and be forced to do something. So this is, in my view, the most powerful idea out there,” he said. Meanwhile, Turner said China would need to eventually raise its carbon prices to around US$100 per tonne to fully decarbonise its iron production by 2050 or 2060. China’s national carbon market closed at 96.66 yuan (US$15) per tonne on Thursday, according to data from the Shanghai Environment and Energy Exchange. “China has done a fantastic contribution to the world through the development of clean technologies,” he said. “The biggest thing it could now add to it is to have a serious strategy for decarbonising cement and iron and steel production.”

title: Cambricon’s third quarter profit surges 148% to US$210m amid push to replace Nvidia chips
description: Revenue reached 3.5 billion yuan, up 104.5 per cent from a year ago, beating the 75.8 per cent revenue increase seen in the second quarter.
content: Chinese artificial intelligence chip giant Cambricon Technologies reported a 147.7 per cent surge in third-quarter profit on Friday, as the country’s aggressive push to replace Nvidia chips continues to fuel high growth among local chipmakers. The Shanghai-listed chipmaker generated 1.4 billion yuan (US$210 million) in net profit for the three months ended September 30, up from 566.6 million yuan during the same period last year. Revenue reached 3.5 billion yuan, an increase of 104.5 per cent from a year ago, according to its stock exchange filing. That was faster than the company’s 75.8 per cent revenue increase seen in the second quarter. Cambricon attributed the revenue surge to its continuous market expansion and efforts to “facilitate the implementation of AI applications”. This top-line increase directly drove the year-on-year surge in total profit and net profit, the company said in the filing. Shares of Cambricon closed up 5.5 per cent at 932.2 yuan ahead of the earnings release on Friday. Earlier this week, Hygon Information Technology, another leading domestic AI chipmaker, posted third-quarter revenue of 5.9 billion yuan, an increase of 45.5 per cent year on year. Its net profit for the quarter surged 37.9 per cent year on year to 1 billion yuan. The momentum at Cambricon and Hygon builds on Beijing’s initiative to develop a self-sufficient AI computing ecosystem, as the country accelerates the deployment of AI infrastructure powered by home-grown chips. The two companies – regarded as top-tier players in the domestic AI chip sector – are moving rapidly to fill the market vacuum left by Washington’s export controls that have cut off China’s access to advanced AI accelerators from US chip giants like Nvidia. Analysts said Cambricon’s earnings outlook depended largely on the commercialisation progress of its latest chips, which was in turn affected by supply chain pressures, especially the shortage of high bandwidth memory chips required for AI data centres. “Cambricon delivered [its] MLU692 to a major cloud service provider in Q3 for testing, but we expect most revenue to be recognised in Q4,” Morgan Stanley analysts wrote in a recent research report. “MLU580 shipments also remain limited as higher high bandwidth memory costs pressure unit economics.” The MLU692 is part of Cambricon’s MLU690 chip series, also known as Siyuan 690. The series can outperform Nvidia’s H20 by 50 to 150 per cent when measured in “tokens per second”, a metric that essentially counts how many words or other data AI can process and spit out, according to an earlier Morgan Stanley report. Hygon, meanwhile, faces high expectations for its next-generation central processing unit and its deep computing unit – a type of accelerator card designed specifically for AI. The company said on Thursday that the progress was “on track” with key metrics such as compute density and interconnect bandwidth set to be upgraded, though mass production timelines remained pending.

title: Matthew Cheung 36 holes from history after taking Hong Kong Open lead at halfway point
description: Hongkonger says he will take it ‘shot by shot, hole by hole’ as he leads Fanling field following sensational bogey-free eight-under-par 62.
content: Matthew Cheung rode a wave of emotion and a little bit of luck to take a three-shot lead in the Link Hong Kong Open on Friday, leaving himself 36 holes from making history. Beginning the day two strokes back, Cheung carded a sensational eight-under-par 62 to move to 14 under overall, with Caleb Surratt alone in second on 11 under after also posting a 62. Overnight leaders Anirban Lahiri and Kevin Yuan could not match their first-round fireworks, with the former’s 68 leaving him in a tie for third alongside Jazz Janewattananond and Steve Lewton on 10 under. Yuan’s 71 dropped him back into a large group on seven under. But the day belonged to Cheung, who was four under through five and went bogey-free around Hong Kong Golf Club’s composite course. The closest the Hongkonger came to disaster was at the par-4 15th, when his drive skipped across the ditch splitting the fairway. A birdie duly followed. “I didn’t hit a really great drive, and I was walking up there thinking I’m in the water,” Cheung said. “But I think golf is a law of equals. I hit a great drive down 13 and I was in a divot, so maybe the golf gods gave me one back there, but I’ll take it.” Hong Kong has never had one of its own win one of the game’s most prestigious events, and the halfway lead is as close as any local golfer has ever managed to get to the trophy. There is more at stake than just the title: a place in next year’s Open Championship and Masters is also up for grabs. The pressure to deliver might stifle some, but Cheung said he would be taking it “shot by shot, hole by hole”, and drawing strength from the growing crowds that have followed him around Fanling. “The crowds out there have been phenomenal,” Cheung said. “The support from friends, family and people I don’t know, honestly, has been great as well. And obviously, I’m playing some really good golf, but we’re only halfway through the tournament, so hopefully another two good days, and we’ll see where we are.” He may yet be joined in the fight by Asian Games teammate Taichi Kho, whose four-under 66 took him into a group on five under. Isaac Lam began the day alongside Cheung, but carded a 73 to sit at three under with a large group that includes compatriot Jason Hak Shun-yat. It was a day to forget for Jeffrey Shen Wang-ngai, though. A six-over 76 saw him miss the cut, ending his run as the tournament’s low amateur. That prize is likely to go to Markus Lam, who managed a 67 to make the cut on the number at two under.

title: Prime Video K-drama Love in Disguise: Yim Si-wan, Seol In-ah lead gender-reversal romcom
description: Yim Si-wan stars as a corporate heir suspected of murder, while Seol In-ah plays a female detective who pretends to be his male bodyguard.
content: Lead cast: Yim Si-wan, Seol In-ah, Kim Jung-hyun, Yeonwoo Latest Nielsen rating: 4.7 per cent In the romantic comedy Love in Disguise, Yim Si-wan plays a vain corporate heir suspected of murder who hires a new personal bodyguard, unaware that his protector is actually a female detective in disguise (played by Seol In-ah of Business Proposal). The series marks a return to more conventional K-drama fare for Yim, following his intense roles in the action film Mantis (2025) and the second and third seasons of Netflix’s Squid Game. Yoon Yi-jun (Yim) is an heir to the Taekang Group who boasts both business acumen and a flair for fashion. He is also rather difficult to work for, prone to flinging stacks of reports in the air when they are not to his liking or refusing to drink meticulously prepared tea if the temperature or brewing time is off by a single degree or second. Given Yi-jun’s reputation, when his female secretary dies in mysterious circumstances one evening, fingers understandably point at him. He is rich and powerful enough to be quickly released by the police, but the detectives on his trail refuse to give up so easily, especially the tomboyish officer Kang Jae-hee (Seol), a former special forces operative who is routinely mistaken for a man. Jae-hee’s colleagues attempt to interrogate Yi-jun, only to be castigated by a superior who is all too eager to kowtow to Taekang’s influence. Fortunately, Jae-hee was not present for the interrogation, so when an opportunity arises to infiltrate Yi-jun’s orbit as he begins searching for a new secretary who can double as a bodyguard, she is the perfect candidate. Jae-hee still needs to beat other candidates for the role, which involves impressing the impossibly demanding Yi-jun, who enjoys toying with interviewees. She fails the interview after he goads her into throwing him over her shoulder. Yet, moments later, she saves Yi-jun from a man attempting to avenge the murdered secretary. Jae-hee gets the position, but her ordeal has only just begun as Yi-jun continues to test and needle her on the job. His demanding behaviour gets in the way of her covert investigation, yet the more time this odd couple spends together, the more likely it is for something to brew between them. Meanwhile, the show promises other romantic fireworks through its secondary leads, played by Kim Jung-hyun (Mr. Queen) and former Momoland member Yeonwoo (The Tale of Lady Ok). Kim plays Kim Si-hyun, the legal counsel for Taekang and the only person who does not indulge Yi-jun’s whims. Si-hyun secures Yi-jun’s release from police custody and tries to figure out who the killer is, but that becomes difficult when he is distracted by Lee Hye-jung (Yeonwoo), the secretary of Yoon Tae-sik (Choi Jin-ho), the chairman of Taekang and Yi-jun’s father. Known as the “Taekang Goddess”, Hye-jung routinely turns down lovesick suitors. Si-hyun is among their ranks, but when he meets Hye-jung by chance outside the workplace, their relationship enters a new dimension. Love in Disguise strikes many familiar notes with its gender-bending premise, not only through the tomboyish Jae-hee, who masquerades as a man, but also the effeminate Yi-jun, whose interest in fashion and prickly personality embody traits more commonly associated with female leads in K-dramas. The pair effectively switch traditional gender roles, with Yi-jun as the pampered figure in need of protection from the more masculine Jae-hee. These gender-reversal tropes are a natural fit for the romantic comedy genre, which the show doubles down on through the conventional pairing of secondary leads Si-hyun and Hye-jung. However, Love in Disguise is not content to stop there, as it plays around with a murder investigation – we can be fairly certain that Yi-jun is not the culprit, yet the undiscovered killer is surely in his midst – and also indulges in chaebol (Korean family-run corporation) succession drama involving Yi-jun’s other family members. These two subplots are likely connected, but with so many familiar ingredients competing for attention, Love in Disguise risks losing sight of its main draw – the evolving relationship between Yi-jun and Jae-hee. As is often the case with middle-of-the-road fare, much of the responsibility for carrying the show falls on its leads. Yim is clearly enjoying his turn as the dapper and highfalutin Yi-jun, while Seol is convincing as the gruff and handsome Jae-hee. There is something of a spark between them so far, but the success of the series will largely depend on how that chemistry evolves in the coming episodes. Love in Disguise is streaming on Prime Video.

title: Dongshan Precision retail IPO undersubscribed as Hong Kong mega listing flops: sources
description: Following a nearly 10 per cent slump in the company’s A-share price on Thursday, some institutional investors withdrew large orders.
content: Chinese printed circuit board maker Suzhou Dongshan Precision Manufacturing Co failed to excite retail investors in Hong Kong, making it one of the least popular mega initial public offerings (IPOs) in the city so far this year. Bookbuilding closed as scheduled on Friday, with preliminary figures showing the public offering has been undersubscribed with fewer than 10,000 applicants, according to people familiar with the matter. Dongshan Precision is seeking to raise as much as HK$10.7 billion (US$1.36 billion) at a maximum price of HK$93.80 apiece, with a 10 per cent initial allocation to the public subscription tranche. Following a nearly 10 per cent slump in the company’s A-share price on Thursday, some institutional investors withdrew large orders from the international offering, said the people, who asked not to be identified because the information was confidential. A similar drop occurred in the public offering. Margin orders fell from nearly HK$400 million at Thursday noon to HK$330 million, before recovering slightly to HK$383 million, meaning just 36 per cent of the HK$1.07 billion offered to the public was covered, according to data from several brokerages. The Suzhou-based firm’s A-shares traded in Shenzhen had slumped up to 14 per cent since the launch of its H-share public offering, before rebounding to close at 114.22 yuan per share on Friday, giving it a market capitalisation of 209 billion yuan (US$31.3 billion). Among Hong Kong’s 10 largest IPOs by fundraising volume this year, Dongshan is the only one to see an undersubscribed public tranche, ranking last in the group behind Muyuan Foods Co, which drew 21,268 applicants in February. A total of 20 cornerstone investors agreed to buy US$680 million worth of the shares, accounting for up to 50 per cent of the total funds to be raised, Dongshan said. These investors were given guaranteed share allocations but must hold the stock for at least six months. Dongshan plans to use the proceeds to construct and upgrade facilities, fund potential acquisitions, repay debt and support general working capital. The company expects its shares to start trading in Hong Kong on October 28. UBS, Guotai Haitong Securities, GF Securities and Citic Securities were joint sponsors for the Hong Kong listing, according to its prospectus.

title: Could Europe’s cost-of-living protests sharpen EU-China trade tensions?
description: Unrest over economic hardship could strengthen calls to protect industry and jobs, though direct impact on trade talks is uncertain.
content: As violent protests fuelled partly by the cost-of-living crisis shake parts of Europe, most notably France, analysts say the unrest could add to pressure on European policymakers to take a tougher trade stance towards China. “One could argue that the EU looks weaker, but then one could also argue that there is more of a need to show external strength at a time of such events,” said David Henig, director of the UK Trade Policy Project at the European Centre for International Political Economy. The unrest comes as France faces growing financial pressures. Yields on French 10-year bonds topped 5 per cent for a third consecutive day on Friday as political and social turmoil continued. On Thursday, French President Emmanuel Macron said requests to hold protests submitted by people “with no legitimacy” would be banned in the coming days. Requests filed by unions would be examined under the law, while local authorities would propose alternative routes to keep demonstrations away from city centres, he said. Cui Hongjian, director of the Centre for EU and Regional Development Studies at Beijing Foreign Studies University, said the unrest could reinforce the narrative that Europe’s challenges were mainly the result of external factors, with China’s trade surplus singled out as a major cause. “Politically, they will take a harder line – especially against China economically – to appease their domestic populations, signalling that they are actively working to shield European society from external economic pressure, unfair competition and similar challenges,” Cui said. Public frustration over economic conditions was a major driver of the unrest, Cui said. Addressing those concerns would require substantial government spending, which could prompt European governments to impose higher tariffs on Chinese goods to bolster fiscal revenue, among other measures, Cui added. Governments could also raise investment barriers for Chinese enterprises while demanding that they do more to create local jobs and generate tax revenue, he said. Marc Julienne, director of the Centre for Asian Studies at the French Institute of International Relations, said Chinese exports were highly competitive and could help ease the cost-of-living crisis. But that same competition, he added, threatened European industry and employment and had pushed Brussels to press Beijing more forcefully to rebalance trade. Meanwhile, Peter Chase, senior fellow at the German Marshall Fund, agreed that the protests could strengthen the view among European politicians that trade imbalances with China were contributing to political problems across the continent. Still, the unrest would not necessarily influence the manner in which trade negotiations were held, according to some analysts. Henig of the UK Trade Policy Project said protests within member states were unlikely to directly affect talks with China, which are handled by the European Commission. “Such is the noise around negotiations, but [it] does not usually affect what is happening in the rooms where talks happen,” Henig said. Ignacio Garcia Bercero, a senior fellow at Bruegel and former director at the European Commission’s trade department, said Beijing also had enough understanding of Europe’s political dynamics to “avoid a misjudgment”.

title: How China captured nearly 82% of the world’s new ship orders
description: Ageing crude carriers and higher oil prices are helping to fuel demand for new vessels, according to analysts.
content: China’s shipbuilding sector now leads the world by an overwhelming margin, with the country’s shipyards accounting for 81.8 per cent of global new ship orders in the first nine months of the year, according to official data. Demand was also expected to stay resilient, with elevated crude oil prices helping to support orders for new vessels, analysts said. Total outstanding orders at Chinese shipyards reached 399.13 million deadweight tonnes (dwt) at the end of September, up 64.8 per cent year on year, according to data released on Friday by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. The figure accounted for 72.4 per cent of the global total. Chinese shipyards completed vessels with a combined carrying capacity of 58.05 million dwt during the first three quarters, representing over 63 per cent of the global total. On Friday, state broadcaster China Central Television highlighted the role that extensive domestic supply chains play in supporting the industry’s dominance. Building an ultra-large container ship capable of carrying 24,000 twenty-foot equivalent units – a standard measure of container capacity – required about 50,000 tonnes of steel and millions of components, CCTV reported. A single project could bring together more than 200 suppliers across dozens of industries, including steel, electrical engineering and machinery, according to the report. Analysts said the global shipbuilding market was likely to remain robust, with China expected to continue reaping the largest share of the gains. Return expectations are the key for shipowners placing newbuilding orders Yue Xin, Guotai Haitong Securities Yue Xin, an analyst at Shanghai-based Guotai Haitong Securities, wrote in a September research note that container ships remained the largest vessel category, accounting for 39.8 per cent of the global order book so far this year. However, Yue also flagged a sharp increase in orders for very large crude carriers (VLCCs), with European shipowners leading the trend. Of the 930 VLCCs in the global fleet, 21 per cent were more than 20 years old, Yue wrote. Such vessels were typically scrapped after 20 to 25 years of age, he added. The need to replace ageing tankers was driving replacement orders, while higher crude prices were providing a further boost, according to Yue. “Return expectations are the key for shipowners placing newbuilding orders … Since 2026, geopolitical conflicts have continued to lift crude prices, and the five-year time-charter rate for a VLCC now stands at US$50,000 per day,” Yue wrote. Shipbuilding capacity had also expanded at a relatively “slow” and “restrained” pace, helping to sustain the prolonged boom, he added. Yao Pei, an analyst at Guizhou-based Huachuang Securities, wrote in a research note in mid-October that the boom was poised to continue. Chinese shipyards could further expand their global market share on the back of their competitive strengths, Yao added. China’s shipbuilding sector is also building more green-powered vessels. It secured 74.1 per cent of global orders in the category, according to the ministry’s data, up 5.7 percentage points from the January-June period.

title: All about Tate Madden, who revealed her baby’s gender with fiancé Tyler Cameron on DWTS
description: The couple, who worked together on Going Home with Tyler Cameron, started dating in 2022 … and announced their engagement this August.
content: During his performance for “Dedication Night” on Dancing with the Stars, Tyler Cameron revealed that he and his fiancée Tate Madden are expecting their first child together. View this post on Instagram Cameron and his professional partner, Sharna Burgess, were joined on stage by Madden and the trio performed to Ed Sheeran’s “Supermarket Flowers”. After their routine, Cameron and Madden also had a surprise gender reveal on stage – it’s a baby girl! Later, in an interview with TMZ, Cameron, who rose to fame from his appearance on The Bachelorette, shared that both he and Madden were hoping for a big family and were planning to have more children. Here’s everything you need to know about Tyler Cameron’s fiancée and baby mama, Tate Madden. How long have Tyler Cameron and Tate Madden dated? Cameron and Madden reportedly started dating in 2022, given the photos she has been posting with him on Instagram since. However, when fans were shipping them together, she denied dating him in December 2022 in a tongue-in-cheek manner, saying, “We are not dating … I actually work for Tyler. But he is madly in love with me and asks me to be his girlfriend every day, and I tell him he needs to calm down. It’s inappropriate.” She also revealed in a TikTok video back then that she was going through a break-up with someone she dated for four years. It is true that the two had a business relationship at first, working together on the home remodelling show, Going Home with Tyler Cameron, but everyone else seemed to notice their chemistry. Trading Secrets host Jason Tartick even commented on their Instagram video, “Really wish your show [Going Home] didn’t edit me out saying ‘that’s your wife’ the day I met her on set with you. Just saying.” The couple announced their engagement in August this year with an Instagram reel showing Cameron popping the big question to Madden at the beach. “A moment we will forever cherish. A moment we get to build on for the rest of our lives. The best chapters are in front of us and I can’t wait to do them with you,” Cameron captioned the reel. Who’s in Tate Madden’s family? Madden seems to be one of five siblings in her family. From her Instagram highlight titled “Fam”, it appears she has two sisters, Emme and Grace, and two brothers, Jake and Jackson. Among them, Emme plays volleyball and is a coach for the Northern Kentucky Youth Volleyball Club. Much like Cameron, who moved back to his hometown of Jupiter, Florida, following the unfortunate loss of his mother, Madden also lives in Florida. Additional reporting by Sumnima Kandangwa

title: ‘Running on his hands’: Chinese world record holder wows public with skateboarding skills
description: Xie uses his wheelchair skills to travel, summiting Mount Huangshan 4 times and sharing his journeys online to inspire others with spinal injuries.
content: A man from southeastern China, dubbed the “Wind-Breaking Rider,” has mastered his wheelchair and stunned the internet with his skateboarding skills. Xie Junwu, 55, lives in Nanchang, Jiangxi province. At 19, he fell from a tree, injuring his thoracic spinal cord and leaving him paralysed from the waist down. For the first eight years after his injury, Xie depended entirely on his mother. Confined to his home, he struggled with the loss of his independence. “The pain was secondary,” Xie recalled in a video. “The real tragedy was losing sight of a future.” His mother’s sudden death in 2000 forced a painful turning point. Determined to honour a promise he had made to her, Xie began learning to live independently. Four years later, he found inspiration at a spinal injury meetup in Qingdao, where he saw another participant balance a wheelchair on its rear wheels. Inspired, Xie searched the internet and taught himself advanced wheelchair manoeuvres, from wheelies and stair-climbing to basketball and street dance. The physical toll was severe. Strapped tightly into his chair, Xie endured countless falls, sprains and bruises. His persistence paid off. In May 2012, he set a Guinness World Record by completing a 25.8-kilometre wheelchair wheelie, surpassing the previous record of 19.96 kilometres, held by an American. Xie also turned his wheelchair skills into a way to travel. He has reached the 1,800-metre summit of Mount Huangshan four times, documenting his journeys online to inspire others with spinal injuries. Along the way, he earned 32 marathon finisher medals. Among them, none meant more than the one from the New York City Marathon, where he was cheered on by crowds from around the world. Despite these achievements, Xie was haunted by vivid dreams of roller-skating, a cherished memory from his youth. Last year, determined to put that lingering regret to rest, he customised a skateboard to secure his wheelchair and began practising wheelchair skateboarding. Videos of him carving and drifting through city streets soon went viral. “My hands became my legs, and my wheelchair became my shoes,” Xie once said. Today, with more than 100,000 social media followers, Xie serves as deputy director of the Jiangxi Accessibility Promotion Committee and as a rehabilitation consultant for people with spinal injuries. With his guidance, a fellow patient learned to manage everyday tasks independently, including mopping and grocery shopping, using his wheelchair. Looking ahead, Xie plans to organise China’s first wheelchair skateboarding competition. He hopes it will help people who have been injured in accidents support one another and regain confidence in life. “Fate handed me a wheelchair, but it also gave me a skateboard,” Xie reflected. “Endure the storm, and you will inevitably see the rainbow.” One online observer commented: “As someone learning to skateboard, Xie’s story moved me deeply. There are no born champions, only ordinary people who keep working hard.”

title: Fencing risks global divide as top official fires off world league threats
description: Governing body boss sends letter warning World Fencing League is not official event, hints at potential bans for athletes who take part.
content: Days after the World Fencing League (WFL) said it would start its 2027 season in Hong Kong, the sport’s world governing body has warned athletes and officials against taking part in unauthorised events In an official statement released on Thursday, the International Fencing Federation (FIE) said the league was not an official competition and it had not sanctioned any of its proposed tournaments.
