Here are the key figures and measures in Malaysia’s 2027 budget: – Federal spending will reach 459.8 billion ringgit, compared with a revised 444.1 billion ringgit in 2026, with 376.8 billion ringgit allocated to operating expenditure and 83 billion ringgit to development, mostly in infrastructure. – Apart from federal spending, the budget will be supported by 25 billion ringgit in investment by government-linked investment companies, 11 billion ringgit in public-private investment and 14.2 billion ringgit from federal statutory agencies and companies owned by the finance ministry. – Economic growth is forecast at 4.2 to 5.2 per cent in 2027, against 4.8 to 5.3 per cent this year, supported by domestic demand and exports of semiconductors and products related to artificial intelligence. – Inflation is projected at 1.8 to 2.8 per cent next year, compared with an estimated 1.5 to 2.5 per cent in 2026, as higher energy, food and other input costs continue to feed through to consumer prices. – The deficit is targeted at 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product, down from a revised 3.6 per cent this year, while federal revenue is forecast to rise to 380.8 billion ringgit from 363.6 billion ringgit. – Subsidies and social assistance are budgeted at 72.7 billion ringgit, compared with an estimated 74.5 billion ringgit this year, with fuel subsidies expected to cost about 40 billion ringgit in 2027, unchanged from this year. – Household assistance under the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) cash aid and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) essential-goods programmes will rise to 16 billion ringgit from 15 billion ringgit. STR recipients will each receive up to 150 ringgit a month in SARA support, while Malaysian adults outside STR will receive two 100 ringgit SARA payments. – Personal tax relief will increase from 9,000 ringgit to 12,000 ringgit, while marginal tax rates on annual taxable income of 70,000–100,000 ringgit and 100,000–150,000 ringgit will fall by one percentage point to 18 and 24 per cent, respectively. The rate on income above 1 million ringgit will be set at 30 per cent. – Additional tax deductions will cover children’s tuition, postpartum care and a wider range of expenses for caring for parents and grandparents, while lifestyle relief will extend to AI subscriptions and certain pet vaccination and adoption costs. –The monthly minimum wage will rise from 1,700 ringgit to 2,000 ringgit in June 2027, with micro, small and medium enterprises recording annual sales below 50 million ringgit exempt. The government also plans a 2,500 ringgit monthly wage floor for semi-skilled jobs and graduates. – Some 1.3 million civil servants, including contract staff, will receive a special payment of 1,500 ringgit, while more than 1 million government retirees and military veterans will receive 750 ringgit, ahead of the Muslim festival of Eid al-Fitr and Malaysia’s 70th independence anniversary in August 2027. – Healthcare funding will rise to 47.7 billion ringgit from 46.5 billion ringgit, with more than 9,000 contract doctors to be offered permanent posts in the public sector. An allocation of 200 million ringgit will fund treatment through other hospitals, including greater use of private facilities, to reduce waiting times. – Education spending will rise to nearly 69 billion ringgit from 66.2 billion ringgit, with a separate 19.1 billion ringgit for higher education. School maintenance funding will double to 2 billion ringgit, while annual back-to-school aid will rise from 150 ringgit to 200 ringgit per pupil. – First-homebuyers will receive full stamp-duty exemptions on loan and transfer documents for homes costing up to 500,000 ringgit under agreements signed from 2027 to 2030. For homes priced above 500,000 ringgit and up to 750,000 ringgit, the first 500,000 ringgit will be fully exempt and the balance will receive a 50 per cent exemption. – Defence and internal security will each receive 22 billion ringgit, with 7.1 billion ringgit earmarked for purchasing and maintaining equipment for the armed forces, police and uniformed agencies under the home ministry. – Two Malaysian Borneo states, Sabah and Sarawak, will receive federal allocations of 18.7 billion ringgit and 16.2 billion ringgit, respectively, up from 17.6 billion ringgit and 15.1 billion ringgit, with 3.3 billion ringgit allocated to road projects across the states. – Smaller businesses will receive a one-percentage-point income tax reduction, bringing rates to 12 per cent on the first 150,000 ringgit of taxable income and 16 per cent on the next 450,00 ringgit, while loan facilities and financing guarantees will total 57 billion ringgit, up from 50 billion ringgit.

title: Girl filmed carrying beer bags to be placed in temporary care with siblings
description: Welfare assessments find it unsuitable for them to return home following the arrest of their parents on suspicion of child ill-treatment.
content: A 10-year-old Hong Kong girl filmed carrying heavy bags of beer will be placed in temporary care with her two siblings after welfare assessments found it would “not be suitable” for them to return home following the arrest of their parents on suspicion of ill-treating a child. Secretary for Labour and Welfare Chris Sun Yuk-han said on Friday that the three children were still in hospital for health checks and were expected to be discharged later that day or on Saturday. “Even after the three siblings are discharged from hospital, the Social Welfare Department’s assessment is that it will not be suitable for them to return home immediately,” he said. “We have therefore arranged suitable temporary accommodation for them after their discharge.” Sun added that the siblings might not be able to stay together because of their age differences. He also said authorities would hold a multidisciplinary case conference on child abuse as soon as possible, with social workers, teachers, medical personnel and police taking part. The conference would review the children’s family circumstances, care needs, safety risks and long-term welfare requirements before a plan was drawn up, he said. “The next step depends on the final assessment and recommendations of the multidisciplinary case conference,” Sun said. “If appropriate, one possible direction would be to apply to the court for a care or protection order.” Police arrested the girl’s mother, 32, and stepfather, 38, on Wednesday on suspicion of ill-treatment of a child after the girl was filmed carrying two heavy bags of beer at Fu Tai Estate in Tuen Mun, with her backpack torn and gaping open. The video showed the man, who was with two other children, snatching one of the bags back and calling the girl “useless” when bystanders intervened. The pair were released on bail on Thursday and must report back to police later this month. The girl’s school, Lutheran Tsang Shing Siu Leun School, said on Wednesday that social workers and teachers had provided counselling to the pupil and her family. The Education Bureau said it was “highly concerned” and confirmed that the school had activated its crisis management team. In Hong Kong, the maximum penalty for ill-treatment or neglect of a child or young person is 10 years’ imprisonment upon conviction on indictment, or three years’ imprisonment upon summary conviction.

title: UK’s ex-prince Andrew gets US$399,000 compensation on his mansion lease
description: He was forced to end the lease on ⁠Royal Lodge more than 50 years early, entitling him to compensation.
content: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor, the younger brother ⁠of Britain’s King ⁠Charles, has benefited from £302,000 (US$399,000) in ⁠compensation after he was forced to end his mansion lease early over revelations about his ties to the late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. Last year, Charles stripped Mountbatten-Windsor of his title of prince and forced ‌him out of his Windsor home, as the royal family sought distance from the Epstein scandal. Mountbatten-Windsor was later arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office. He has denied any wrongdoing. Britain’s Crown Estate, which manages King Charles’ public property, said on Friday that Mountbatten-Windsor surrendered the lease on ⁠Royal Lodge more than 50 years early, entitling him to £302,000 in compensation. Under the terms ‌of the lease, Mountbatten-Windsor also paid £1.8 million to fund repairs needed on the property, but the compensation reduced that bill ‌to £1.5 million, the Crown Estate said in a statement. Andrew had already spent £7.5 ⁠million on ⁠refurbishing the 30-room property when he first moved in over 20 years ago. “The lease for Royal ‌Lodge has ended and our focus now is firmly on its future use and the opportunities to ‌generate additional financial ‌value for the nation from its early return,” a spokesperson for The ‌Crown Estate said. British police on Thursday said warrants they secured to search properties linked ⁠to Mountbatten-Windsor had been issued unlawfully and must be quashed, but added that ⁠their investigation following his arrest was ongoing. Mountbatten-Windsor, the second son of the late Queen Elizabeth, has always denied any wrongdoing in relation to Epstein, and ‌said he regrets their ‌friendship. Amid heightened scrutiny of royal finances, a Buckingham Palace source said this week that the former prince had been told that money provided from private funds by the king should not be used to fund his legal challenge.

title: News commentator denies unlawfully revealing police meeting details online
description: Wong Kwok-ngon tells Hong Kong court details of his meeting with national security officers were already public before he discussed them on YouTube.
content: A Hong Kong news commentator accused of violating the national security law has denied exposing police intelligence operations, telling a court that details of his meeting with officers were already public knowledge before he posted them online. Wong Kwok-ngon, 72, who ran a YouTube commentary channel under the pen name Wong On-yin, stood trial at the District Court on Friday. He is the first person in Hong Kong to be prosecuted for allegedly prejudicing an investigation into national security offences by unlawfully disclosing details of a police interview. He was also charged with knowingly publishing seditious publications in connection with videos covering local and international news. In court, Wong questioned why two sergeants from the police force’s National Security Department considered their meeting with him on December 2, 2025, confidential when media outlets had already widely reported that he was under investigation. Wong and other residents had planned to hold a press conference that day about the Wang Fuk Court blaze, which killed 168 people last November. But the event was called off after national security officers invited them to a meeting the same day. Wong posted two videos on his YouTube channel the following day discussing the meeting. Prosecutors said in their opening submission that Wong’s commentary had exceeded the bounds of “fair comment” because he repeatedly portrayed the National Security Department’s operations as a tool of suppression. They said Wong had signed a non-disclosure declaration at the start of the December 2 meeting, agreeing to keep everything discussed confidential. The court heard that Wong, a highly educated former employee of the Independent Commission Against Corruption, told Sergeants Li Pak-him and Wong Ping-kiu that he understood the terms. Li said Wong did not ask any questions about the declaration but asked whether he was under investigation. Sergeant Wong said the purpose of the meeting was to gather intelligence from the commentator, who was not a suspect at the time, and assess whether the planned press conference might pose a national security risk. Both officers testified that they had asked him about the background to the press conference. Li said he had reiterated the confidentiality requirement at the end of the hour-long meeting. Wong asked Li: “I replied to you at the time that it was already in the newspaper that you guys were having a meeting with me, so what exactly do you want me to keep confidential?” The commentator said he had told the officers he intended only to explain legal matters at the press conference and would not disclose any sensitive information that should concern them. Li said he had reiterated that the “entire meeting”, including the fact that it had taken place, should be kept private. He added that he had not expected to have to tell Wong what he could and could not say to his viewers. The trial will continue on Monday, when the court will hear evidence about the allegedly seditious content published on Wong’s channel.

title: Soaring component costs force laptop makers to rethink shift away from China: report
description: The predicted strategic pivot comes as the PC industry braces for subdued consumer demand driven by rising component prices.
content: Notebook manufacturers are being forced to rethink their shift out of China and consider moving production back to the manufacturing hub, as skyrocketing component costs squeeze profit margins, according to market research firm TrendForce. The Taiwan-based firm projected that the share of global notebook production outside mainland China would decline to 21 per cent this year from about 24 per cent in 2025, and drop below 20 per cent in 2027. “This suggests that brands are reassessing the balance between supply-chain diversification and manufacturing efficiency as policy and cost conditions evolve,” TrendForce said in a report released on Thursday. Over the past few years, major laptop vendors have expanded their manufacturing footprints outside China to hedge against trade tariffs and geopolitical friction. US computer giant Dell, for example, set a goal in 2023 to phase out Chinese-made chips by 2024 and move about half its production out of China by 2025, while Apple shifted portions of its device assembly to Vietnam and India. However, unless trade barriers escalate significantly, financial pragmatism was reasserting itself over risk mitigation, according to TrendForce. “If tariff pressures do not intensify further, the factors guiding manufacturing ‘glocalisation’ are likely to shift from minimising policy risks towards production costs, supply-chain completeness and operational efficiency,” the firm said. The predicted strategic pivot comes as the personal computer (PC) industry braces for subdued consumer demand driven by rising component prices. TrendForce estimated that global notebook shipments would fall by a low single digits percentage in 2027. If semiconductor costs kept climbing, however, laptop brands would have little choice but to pass more of those expenses on to buyers, potentially deepening the market contraction to a high single digits decline, the firm said. Core hardware has grown increasingly expensive. TrendForce estimated that central processing units (CPUs), dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and solid-state drives (SSDs) collectively accounted for around 68 per cent of the total bill of materials for a mainstream US$900 laptop in the third quarter. Compounding the pressure, global PC shipments plunged about 20 per cent year on year to 62.7 million units in the third quarter, according to a separate report by research firm IDC on Thursday. Jitesh Ubrani, research director for consumer devices at IDC, attributed the drop to stockpiling by vendors in the first half of the year as they sought to get ahead of memory price hikes. This created an “inventory pull-in earlier in the year”, leaving the third quarter with “little demand to draw on”, IDC said. “Prices will remain elevated,” Ubrani said. “With macro conditions worsening, the risk is that the outlook for the next few quarters gets worse before it gets better.” Industry market shares remained largely intact despite the downturn. China’s Lenovo retained its top spot with a 23.8 per cent global share, despite a 22.6 per cent drop in shipments in the third quarter, IDC data showed. HP held second place with a 16.5 per cent share, hit by a 30.9 per cent decline in shipments. Dell ranked third, with shipments falling 25 per cent during the quarter.

title: EU removes Panama from tax haven blacklist
description: Panama had made progress on sharing tax information and reformed a ‘harmful’ regime of exemptions for foreign-source income.
content: The EU removed Panama from its tax havens blacklist on Friday after the country made progress on sharing tax information and reformed a “harmful” regime of exemptions for foreign-source income. Vietnam was also removed after undertaking a series of reforms. The updated list now contains eight “non-cooperative” jurisdictions: American Samoa, Anguilla, Guam, Palau, Russia, Turks and Caicos Islands, US Virgin Islands and Vanuatu. “This update reflects a positive trend in compliance with international tax good governance standards,” the EU said in a statement. The list was created in 2017 in the wake of a series of scandals, including the so-called Panama Papers that revealed how the world’s wealthy stashed assets in offshore companies, triggering scores of investigations around the globe. Panama had been removed in 2018, before returning to the list in 2020. The EU said Panama had been removed once again in light of a review granted by the OECD Global Forum regarding its “compliance with international standards on the exchange of tax information on request”. It also underlined that Panama “has now reformed its harmful foreign-source income exemption regime”. The leak of 11.5 million files from the law firm Mossack Fonseca in Panama City in 2016 rocked the world, exposing how the rich and famous used offshore accounts to stash hundreds of millions of dollars from tax authorities. The Panama Papers scandal dealt a severe blow to the country’s reputation as an offshore financial hub, prompting it to implement several reforms, including penalising tax evasion. The country had hit out at the EU for keeping it on its tax haven blacklist despite efforts to crack down on tax evasion. The Financial Action Task Force, an intergovernmental organisation that combats money laundering and terrorism financing, removed Panama from its grey list in 2023.

title: China’s funding of global development bodies grows ‘over tenfold’ but now more selective
description: Think tank analysts say fastest growth in funding has been to multilateral development banks assisting low-income countries.
content: China’s funding of global development institutions has grown more than tenfold since 2010, according to a new report that also says the pace of growth has been slowing recently as financing becomes more selective. China’s annual contributions to multilateral development entities rose from just under US$260 million in 2010 to over US$3 billion in 2024, according to a report published by the Washington-based Centre for Global Development think tank on Thursday. “China appears to be more involved in that system than it was a decade ago, but on terms shaped both by Beijing’s own caution and selectivity and by what existing shareholders have been willing to concede,” analysts Beata Cichocka and Ian Mitchell wrote in the report. They said China’s overall growth in funding had slowed in the past five years, with the fastest-growing contributions going towards multilateral development banks providing cheap loans and grants to low-income countries. China pledged US$1.5 billion to the World Bank’s International Development Association in its last replenishment cycle in 2024. That marked a 14 per cent rise over the previous funding round and made Beijing the fund’s fifth-largest donor, despite wider donor retrenchment, the analysts said. Climate finance attributable to China had also risen sharply, growing from US$600 million in 2017 to $5.25 billion last year, equivalent to around 5.4 per cent of total climate finance outflows from multilateral development banks, they said. But while China’s international role has grown, its multilateral contributions are ... low relative to other providers Beata Cichocka and Ian Mitchell, Centre for Global Development Meanwhile, China’s engagement with UN bodies had become more selective, with its assessed contributions – required dues based on the relative size of a country’s economy – now the second largest, but its voluntary contributions ranking only 19th. The report said China’s steepest growth in UN funding over the past decade was to the UN Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East and the World Meteorological Organisation. Four months after the United States withdrew from the World Health Organization, Beijing pledged in May last year to give the WHO an additional US$500 million over the following five years. “China is a net contributor to the multilateral system,” Cichocka and Mitchell said in a separate article published on the think tank’s website on Thursday, noting that China’s borrowing from multilateral development banks had nearly halved between 2021 and 2024. “But while China’s international role has grown, its multilateral contributions are still a very small share of its economy and low relative to other providers,” they added. They said China’s financing was estimated at just 0.01 per cent of its gross national income in 2023, significantly lower than the 0.14 per cent average among Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development members. “This is understandable for a middle-income country,” Cichocka and Mitchell said. “But as China reaches and grows through high-income status, it could comfortably increase its role in many different ways.”

title: Can the Philippines lead Southeast Asia’s fight against child labour?
description: As Manila puts together a new road map to end child labour by 2028, analysts warn policies alone cannot overcome poverty.
content: The Philippines is developing a national road map to combat child labour as part of a broader push across Southeast Asia, where poverty and insecure livelihoods continue to drive children into work despite government efforts to stamp out the practice. But analysts warn that policy commitments alone will not be enough without stronger support for vulnerable families, better access to education and more effective enforcement of child protection laws. On September 23 and 24, government officials, civil society groups and welfare organisations gathered in Manila to help draft the road map and reaffirm their commitment to ending child labour and human trafficking. The move comes a year after the Philippine Department of Labour and Employment expressed its interest in becoming an Alliance 8.7 Pathfinder Country. Alliance 8.7 is a global partnership based on Target 8.7 of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, which calls for immediate and effective measures to eradicate forced labour, modern slavery, human trafficking and the worst forms of child labour. Pathfinder countries are expected to develop and implement improved legislation, national action plans and policies to address the issue. The push to formalise a road map comes against the backdrop of the recent rescue of at least 120 children reportedly forced into labour in the southern Philippine region of Bangsamoro. The children were found working in markets and selling items on the streets, either to meet their daily needs or to supplement their parents’ income, Bangsamoro Labour Minister Muslimin Sema said. The children’s parents and guardians received 15,000 pesos (US$239) each through a rehabilitation programme, Sema said, as part of efforts to return them to schooling. Over the past three years, the programme has helped nearly 4,000 child labourers across Bangsamoro. A regional struggle The challenge facing Manila reflects a wider issue across the Association of Southeast Asian Nations, where poverty, insecure livelihoods and barriers to education leave millions of children vulnerable to exploitation. In April, the Philippine labour department said it had rescued 232,966 children from child labour over the past three years as part of a campaign to eliminate child labour in the country by 2028. According to the department, the number of children engaged in labour fell to 509,000 in 2024, down from 828,000 in 2022. “The decline is meaningful, but the remaining number is large because child labour is rooted in household poverty, insecure rural livelihoods, barriers to schooling and weak protection in informal work – not simply in parents’ choices or a lack of laws,” said Florence Flores-Pasos, an assistant professor at the University of the Philippines Diliman College of Social Work and Community Development. Flores-Pasos said the 509,000 figure came from the Philippine Statistics Authority’s 2024 data and was slightly lower than preliminary estimates of 514,000. Manila’s efforts to eliminate child labour began well before the Trump administration threatened tariffs under Section 301 investigations into forced labour, according to the International Labour Organization (ILO). “The Philippines has been working for many years to eliminate child labour and forced labour,” an ILO representative said, adding that talks about becoming an Alliance 8.7 Pathfinder Country began several years ago, with the organisation providing technical support. “As such, these efforts should be seen as part of a long-term process and commitment,” the UN agency added. The challenges facing the Philippines are reflected elsewhere in Asia, where the worst forms of child labour persist, according to the ILO. These include slavery, commercial sexual exploitation, child trafficking for illicit activities such as the drug trade and hazardous work that threatens physical and mental well-being. Across Southeast Asia, an estimated 5.6 million children are engaged in labour, with 3.7 million working in hazardous conditions, the ILO said. “Child labour in the Philippines is driven by interconnected factors: poverty and insecure livelihoods, barriers to quality education, social norms, climate and other shocks, gaps in social protection and demand for cheap labour,” it said in a statement. “These challenges are compounded by informality and difficulties enforcing protections.” In September, an ILO report on child labour in Myanmar found that economic vulnerability and limited access to education continued to drive children into work, particularly in agricultural and rural communities where children as young as 12 were engaged in hazardous work in construction, agriculture and other trades. The report also found cases of children trapped in armed conflict, illicit activities and commercial sexual exploitation. Enforcement gaps Against this backdrop, Flores-Pasos said the Asean road map provided a clear direction for the Philippines to translate into national programmes and local action. “It is like a shared map for Southeast Asia. Each country still has to identify its own dangerous areas, choose the right routes, and provide the resources needed to reach the destination,” she said. Flores-Pasos added that the regional framework identified human trafficking, commercial sexual exploitation, online exploitation, hazardous work and forced labour as shared concerns, with children in remote areas and informal sectors particularly vulnerable. Across the region, children can be found working in agriculture, plantations, forestry, fishing, domestic work, construction, manufacturing, street vending and mining. While the Asean road map had helped shape policy direction and inter-agency coordination, Flores-Pasos said its impact would depend on execution. “The real test is implementation. A road map will only make a difference if it leads to more support for vulnerable families, better monitoring of informal workplaces, stronger action against traffickers and exploiters and safer access to education for children,” she said. “Its success will depend on how consistently national agencies and local communities put those commitments into practice.”

title: Knee pain and crunching: causes and 3 exercises to ease osteoarthritis of the kneecap
description: Stiff knees could be a sign of osteoarthritis of the kneecap. Here’s what to know about the condition and who is most at risk.
content: Does your knee crunch like a coffee grinder whenever you move it? It could be a sign of patellofemoral osteoarthritis, the breakdown of cartilage on the underside of the patella (kneecap) and groove of the femur (thighbone). “Degenerative changes behind the kneecap are the cause,” says Dr Sven Ostermeier, an orthopaedist based in Freiburg, Germany, adding that the condition should be treated as early as possible or, ideally, prevented in the first place. The kneecap does more than merely protect the knee joint. This disc-shaped bone in front of the knee is important, along with the quadriceps muscle on the front of the thigh, for extending and straightening the leg when you walk or stand, Ostermeier says. Whenever you bend or stretch your leg, the kneecap moves back and forth inside a groove on top of the thighbone. Cartilage helps the bones glide smoothly against each other. When cartilage wears away, the resulting friction can be painful – and even audible. Many people aged 50 or older have patellofemoral osteoarthritis, particularly those who are overweight, obese or in occupations requiring heavy lifting, frequent kneeling or squatting. This subjects knee joints to considerable stress, contributing to cartilage degeneration. Joggers, too, can be affected. The condition makes itself especially felt when descending stairs or inclines, according to Ostermeier. Standing up from a sitting position, kneeling or squatting can be painful as well. Some people with the condition get knee stiffness, and in some cases the knee seems to lock up when they try to move it. If inflammation develops, there may be swelling and warmth in the kneecap region, Ostermeier says. Early treatment is important, he says, to prevent the osteoarthritis from progressing to the entire knee joint. Most cartilage damage behind the kneecap can be treated conservatively. Losing excess body weight often relieves symptoms. Strengthening the quadriceps – by doing knee bends, for instance – can also reduce strain on the knee, and stretching exercises that promote lateral mobility are good for the kneecap, too. But before starting exercises such as these, anyone with knee problems – including acute pain or inflamed joints – should first consult a medical specialist. Doctors can provide advice on pain-relieving medications and further treatment options, such as a cartilage cell transplant or implants. 3 good exercises for your knees: Lie flat on your back with your legs stretched out on the floor. Then lift one leg and draw your foot towards your buttocks. After several seconds, stretch out your leg again. Do this a dozen times with each leg. Sit on a sturdy table and let your legs dangle. This helps to distribute synovial fluid, a lubricant in freely movable joints, over all of the cartilage surface in the knees. The fluid reduces friction and delivers oxygen and nutrients to cartilage, which does not have its own blood supply. Stand on one leg and let the other swing back and forth about 10 times. Do this three times with each leg. It will strengthen your leg muscles and improve balance. At first you may need to rest a hand on the back of a chair for additional support.

title: Saudi Arabia says 3 killed at Riyadh airport as Yemen war expands
description: Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government forces it backs have struggled to contain the Houthis’ advance.
content: Saudi Arabia said on Friday that three people were killed including a pilot, in attacks on Riyadh’s international airport, after Yemen’s Houthis claimed a series of attacks targeting the facility. The conflict between the Houthis and Yemen’s Saudi-backed government has widened, with the Iran-backed fighters repeatedly attacking Saudi targets since they began a lightning offensive just across the border. While seizing large swathes of territory along the Red Sea coast in Yemen, the Houthis have also attacked Saudi transport hubs, oil facilities and other civilian targets in the world’s largest crude exporter. The Saudi civil aviation authority said two attacks on Thursday on the Saudi capital’s airport and a Saudia Airlines plane there “resulted in the martyrdom of three citizens”. The national flag carrier confirmed the death of the plane’s captain, expressing “profound sadness” and citing an “incident” at King Khalid International Airport. Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government forces it backs have struggled to contain the Houthis’ advance, despite a counteroffensive aimed at recapturing territory including the area around the Bab al-Mandab strait that is crucial to global energy flows. But a regional source said on Friday that Riyadh would not bow to the Houthis’ “military blackmail” and would not agree to a truce until the Yemeni government regains all territory it has lost in recent weeks. The attacks forced diplomats stationed in the Saudi capital to shelter in place and international schools to take safety measures, as explosions echoed across the city on Thursday. Numerous flights at Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport were delayed or cancelled, while the airport advised travellers of the “necessity” to contact airlines before their trips. The kingdom’s civil defence agency also said “interception debris” had damaged a kindergarten and a medical complex in Riyadh. It did not say if there were casualties there or provide details of the damage. The Houthis, whose heartlands are among the Zaidi Shia Muslims in the northwest, had already controlled the capital Sanaa and most of Yemen’s major population centres since the start of the war in 2014. Riyadh’s military coalition intervened to support the government the following year. After declaring their counteroffensive against the Houthis, Yemen’s government claimed to have pushed the fighters out of strategic areas on the Red Sea coast and the port city of Mocha. But the Houthis insist they are holding their territory, and military sources from both sides contacted by AFP have not reported any major changes on the ground. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree said the group launched missiles at an airport in Najran and an airbase in Khamis Mushait on Thursday. The Houthis have also warned workers to evacuate Saudi Arabia’s oil facilities, having days before hit a major refinery south of the capital. Admissions by Saudi authorities of civilian targets being hit are relatively rare. There have been few statements on Houthi attacks in recent weeks. Claims by the warring parties have been impossible to independently verify, with the situation moving fast and access for journalists difficult. In Yemen, one of the world’s poorest countries, ordinary civilians are paying the price for the renewed fighting, with more than 200,000 people displaced since July, according to UN data. In Yemen’s Taiz, the Houthis are laying siege to the government-controlled city in the country’s west, depriving residents of their main supply route to the government’s temporary capital in Aden. “There is a crisis in everything: water, gas, vegetables, everything essential”, said Um Rian.

title: Hong Kong outlines new liquidity reforms as US market rally pulls funds away
description: City is pressing ahead with market reforms as a surging US stock market intensifies competition for capital.
content: Hong Kong’s securities watchdog is renewing its push to boost market liquidity, setting out further reforms as emerging markets grapple with capital outflow pressure amid a rally in US equities and a strengthening dollar. Speaking at a conference organised by the Asia Securities Industry & Financial Markets Association (Asifma) on Friday, Julia Leung, CEO of the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC), outlined measures ranging from extended trading hours and shorter settlement cycles to cross-market margining and board lot reform aimed at improving market liquidity and efficiency. “The SFC is working with the HKEX [Hong Kong Exchanges and Clearing] to develop margin offsets across its clearing houses,” Leung said, adding that the move would free up capital for “more productive” uses. Leung also said the HKEX’s clearing house, OTC Clear, would enable same-day settlement for bond deposits and withdrawals later this year, streamlining the process and making non-cash collateral “a more attractive funding pool”. As part of board lot reform, Leung announced the introduction of eight standardised categories. The maximum board lot value would be capped at HK$50,000 (US$6,370), while the minimum would be reduced to HK$1,000. “The aim is to lower entry barriers, broaden participation and make stock trading more accessible,” she said. The measure will take effect in November for existing issuers, having already been implemented for new listings since July. Average daily turnover in Hong Kong’s stock market had exceeded HK$270 billion so far this year, up 160 per cent from 2023, SFC data showed. The increase had been driven partly by mainland Chinese funds flowing into Hong Kong through the Stock Connect and Bond Connect programmes, particularly into technology shares. Hong Kong had also become Asia’s third-largest exchange-traded product (ETP) market by turnover, according to the SFC. Challenges remain, however, as global investors continue to favour US assets. Nasdaq and the S&P 500 hit record highs this week amid enthusiasm for artificial intelligence-related investments, while the Hang Seng Index has fallen about 5.5 per cent this year. Leung also said the HKEX would soon announce a timeline for shortening the market’s settlement cycle to T+1 – allowing trades to be settled one business day after execution – from T+2. “Shortening the cycle reduces various risks, improves capital efficiency and brings Hong Kong more in line with major international markets,” she said. The US adopted T+1 settlement in 2024, while the European Union, UK and Switzerland plan to make the transition in October 2027. Peter Stein, CEO of Asifma, said the association supported the move towards T+1, but had “expressed concerns about the implementation timeline” during the consultation process. Given Hong Kong’s time difference with New York, “you have a narrower window with which to provide the funding to settle trades and do the [foreign exchange] conversions”, he said. Stein added that he welcomed the new measures announced by Leung and viewed them as “a great model for what we’d like to see happen in some other markets”.

title: China’s hotel room rates disappoint during ‘golden week’ despite tourism boom
description: Hotel bookings climbed during the National Day holiday, but stronger supply and cautious spending kept rates in check.
content: Hotel room rates across mainland China fell short of expectations during the National Day “golden week” holiday despite a tourism boom, as company officials and analysts called for stronger asset and revenue management to ease pricing pressure. Hotel tariffs remained largely unchanged from the previous month between October 1 and 7, even as bookings jumped, according to executives at hotel operators and travel agencies. “The days when hotels and resorts could expect a windfall during the week-long holiday are history,” said Li Wenjie, CEO of Shanghai Yaheng International Travel. “Middle-income tourists are no longer willing to spend freely on accommodation.” The subdued performance stood in stark contrast to the surge in room prices seen three years ago after Beijing lifted its zero-Covid-19 policy. During the 2023 National Day holiday, some hotel operators inflated rates to as much as 10 times their average levels. Online travel agency Qunar reported ahead of the holiday that hotel bookings in popular tourist destinations on the mainland had risen about 30 per cent year on year. “New supply, measured corporate travel and outbound tourism are somewhat eroding room rates,” said Zhou Tao, head of hotels and hospitality at JLL in China. “Operators should adopt total-revenue management, price around events and peak periods, and diversify into local, MICE [meetings, incentives, conferences and exhibitions] and extended-stay demand.” Some hotels in China were also burdened by outdated designs that no longer met the needs of today’s travellers, he added. Leading hospitality groups from Hilton to Shangri-La have been doubling down on lifestyle brands over the past two years to cater to mainland tourists’ growing appetite for personalised and culturally immersive experiences, helping support room rates and occupancy. Last year, Shangri-La launched its super-luxury hotel brand, Shangri-La Signatures, in China, combining cultural heritage and nature to attract wealthy tourists with unique experiences. In July, Hilton introduced its Tempo brand to China. Alan Watts, the group’s president for the Asia-Pacific region, said the move would help hotel owners capture growing demand for lifestyle-oriented hospitality through a scalable business model. Last month, Herman Chui, senior director of office, hotel and residence at Hong Kong developer Hang Lung Properties, said modern hotels should offer guests more personalised experiences, from selecting in-room amenities like teapots to allowing them to bring along their pets. “Refurbishment should follow a clear target-segment strategy rather than a generic upgrade, with labour, energy and procurement costs aligned to demand,” Zhou of JLL said. “Professional asset management is required to implement [strategic] repositioning, rebranding and renovation to achieve rejuvenation with better and healthier performance as well as asset value for hotels.” There are signs of hope for the sector. Analysts said events could generate concentrated, date-specific demand from cross-city visitors, giving venue-adjacent hotels greater pricing power. As a prime test case, Shanghai will kick off the 25th China Shanghai International Arts Festival (CSIAF) on October 17 to attract visitors from around the globe. The month-long grand cultural event will feature about 400 programmes and more than 1,100 performances. Highlights include the Shanghai debut of Dance Reflections by Van Cleef & Arpels, appearances by Grammy Award-winning Chinese composer Tan Dun, and the “Focus on Germany” cultural week showcasing German classical arts. “The festival will enable Shanghai to truly earn its status as a premier global destination for the performing arts,” said Li Ming, president of the CSIAF. “It will be a festival filled with top-notch artists and performances.”

title: Meet Halle Berry’s daughter Nahla Aubry, who defended the actress against abuse allegations
description: The Oscar winner was accused of physically abusing her son Maceo by ex-husband Olivier Martinez – here’s how her eldest child responded.
content: Halle Berry’s daughter Nahla Aubry has come to her mother’s defence after the actress was accused of physically abusing her 13-year-old son Maceo by her ex-husband Olivier Martinez. Martinez, who finalised his divorce from Berry in 2023 after an eight-year-long legal battle, filed a temporary restraining order last week against his ex-wife and accused her of choking Maceo. According to court documents obtained by Page Six, Martinez claims that Berry “jumped” on Maceo and “started physically fighting with him”. He alleges that the actress grabbed Maceo by the neck and started choking him while shouting, “Who is dominant now?! Who is dominant?!” The incident in question allegedly took place after Berry called Maceo “stupid” and “such an idiot” for playing video games. Martinez further claims that it was not the first time Berry had been abusive towards Maceo, saying she previously made racially charged statements against their son. But Nahla, Berry’s daughter with ex-boyfriend Gabriel Aubry, reportedly defended her mother as a “loving and devoted parent”. “I have never seen my mom place her hands around Maceo’s neck, put him in a chokehold, restrict his breathing, or engage in any conduct remotely resembling the allegations that have been made against her,” the 18-year-old wrote in a declaration filed in the Los Angeles Superior Court, per Page Six. Nahla said her mother can be “strict when necessary”, but is also “warm, supportive and deeply involved in our lives”. Regarding the accusation against Berry for making racially insensitive comments towards Maceo, Nahla said: “My mom is biracial, I am biracial, and Maceo is biracial. Throughout my life, my mom taught both of us to embrace who we are, appreciate our differences, and respect people from all backgrounds.” Nahla added that she last spoke to her brother on September 29, when Berry drove him to school, and that he sounded happy and “didn’t seem upset about anything”. However, she said she has since refrained from reaching out to Maceo because she is unsure of what is allowed during the ongoing legal proceedings. Here’s everything you need to know about Halle Berry’s teenage daughter, Nahla Aubry. Her parents fought over her custody Nahla Ariela Aubry was born to Halle Berry and Gabriel Aubry in March 2008. Berry met Canadian model Aubry in 2006 at a Versace store opening, per People magazine. They started dating and welcomed Nahla two years later. After their 2010 split, the couple entered a bitter custody battle over Nahla. According to The New Zealand Herald, Berry accused Aubry of an incestuous affair with a family member, claiming he was also abusive towards their daughter and refused to acknowledge her biracial heritage. In 2012, Aubry and Martinez, who was engaged to Berry at the time, were hospitalised after a brawl at the Catwoman actress’ home in California. Berry and Aubry were eventually granted joint custody of Nahla in 2012. She grew up outside the limelight Despite her famous mother, Nahla has had a fairly private upbringing. “I’ve fought really hard to protect their privacy, and I just want them to have their life and have it be theirs,” Berry said of her children on the Today show in 2019. “I just don’t want to plaster them all over the internet. That just doesn’t feel right for me,” the mother of two explained. “They’re gonna do that soon enough. That’s gonna be their life when they grow up, and they will choose when that starts.” Over the years, the Monster’s Ball actress has rarely shared photos or updates of Nahla on social media. One exception was in October 2025, when Berry celebrated her daughter’s early university acceptance on Instagram Stories, writing: “Congratulations to my sweet Angel Nahla for her early college acceptance!” In June, Berry was spotted attending Nahla’s secondary school graduation with her fiancé Van Hunt and was reunited with Nahla’s father, Aubry, per People.

title: Anne Carson wins 2026 Nobel Prize in Literature for ‘reimagining’ classics
description: Most prestigious literature prize awarded to Canadian poet and essayist for genre-defying work that blends verse, prose, dialogue and translation.
content:
This year’s Nobel Prize in Literature has gone to Canada’s Anne Carson, an essayist and classicist who brings a modern twist to mysticism and antiquity in her writings about love, desire and despair.
The 76-year-old won “for her bold and inventive oeuvre that, in playful dialogue with the classical tradition, has created new forms for contemporary literature”, the Swedish Academy said on Thursday.
Carson is widely known for her translations of classical Greek literature – which heavily influence her work – ranging from opera librettos to literary criticism and verse novels, such as Autobiography of Red from 1998.
Her style ⁠is exemplified in Norma Jeane Baker of Troy from 2019, a performance piece which mixes the ‌stories of Helen of Troy in Euripides’ play Helen and Marilyn Monroe.
Ingrid Carlberg, the academy’s permanent secretary, said she had briefly spoken to Carson.
“We didn’t have so much time to speak. All she had time to tell me was that she is for the moment in Iceland, where she’s listening to the wind,” Carlberg said. “She was taken by surprise, but very happy. I could hear that in her voice.”
In an interview with public broadcaster RUV in Iceland, where Carson has lived part of the year since 2008 and has become a citizen, she said of the decision to honour her: “They’re all crazy.”
Asked by RUV on a blustery roadside if she thought the Nobel would change her readership, Carson, holding tightly to her cap so it would not blow away, replied: “I’ll get a sticker on the front of my books.”
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday lauded Carson’s win. Her works featured “wit, imagination and a style entirely her own”, Carney said on social media.
“She has brought ancient stories to new audiences and transformed the way we think about literature,” he said, calling the award “an extraordinary achievement and a proud moment for Canada”.
Carson was born in 1950 in Toronto. She was educated at the University of Toronto and has taught at several universities in North America, including McGill, Michigan, New York and Princeton.
A professor of classics with a background in dead languages, literature, anthropology and history, Carson was described by The New York Times in 2001 as “one of the great pasticheurs”. Her unique contemporary poetry earned her several key literary prizes in the 1990s, including the 1996 Lannan Award and the 1997 Pushcart Prize.
The academy said almost all of Carson’s literary production “has centred upon the intersection between the philologist’s obsession with words and the poet’s desire for new meaning”. It singled out her poem Nox , printed on one continuous sheet of paper in homage to her brother who died in 2000, as “an unforgettable work”.
“Palpable here is a deep sense of loss that works its way up from below. The result is a creation as sculptural as it is literary, an epitaph in the form of a box containing an accordion-fold-out of pictures, letters and other written texts dedicated to her dead brother,” the academy said.
Carson’s wide-ranging influences, from the ancient Greeks to John Keats, Virginia Woolf and Emily Bronte, led “to playful and ironic works that move not only between classical and modern poetry but also between different genres and art forms”, said Anders Olsson, chair of the Nobel Literature Committee.
Carson has said that she considers herself a visual artist as much as a literary one.
“I think of making a poem as making an object. I have always thought of ⁠them more as drawings than as texts, but drawings that are also physically enterable through the fact of language,” she said in an interview with Canada’s CBC Radio One in 2016.
Poetry, she says, may be more attuned to the fast modern-day life than long-form writing.
“I ⁠think it’s probably more useful than prose right now because it’s faster and everybody is in a hurry so basically it’s good because it is brief,” she told the Icelandic broadcaster on Thursday.
Carson had been among the favourites to win this year’s prize, according to bookmakers Ladbrokes, and takes a place beside luminaries such as ‌Alexander Solzhenitsyn, ‌Alice Munro and Ernest Hemingway as a recipient of the award, which often divides opinion among book lovers.
Last year, the academy picked Hungarian writer Laszlo Krasznahorkai.
The academy has been ‌lambasted for ignoring some of the literary titans of the last 120 years such as Leo Tolstoy, Woolf and Jorge Luis ⁠Borges, criticised for snubbing American authors – though it gave the prize to singer-songwriter Bob Dylan in 2016 – and accused of being too ⁠obscure in its choices.
Defenders say the academy has made popular picks, such as Colombia’s Gabriel Garcia Marquez in 1982 and Doris Lessing in 2007, arguing that part of its task is to highlight lesser-known literary traditions and ‌encourage readers to broaden their horizons.
There have been just 19 women laureates out of 122 since the Nobel Literature Prize was first awarded in 1901. The Literature Prize is the fourth award announced each year, following the Nobel Prizes in Medicine, Physics and Chemistry.
The Peace Prize will be announced on Friday in Oslo, the only Nobel award not presented in Stockholm. The week concludes on Monday with the Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences.
Each Nobel Prize this year carries a cash award of 12 million Swedish kronor (about US$1.2 million). The prizes will be formally presented to the winners at a ceremony on December 10, the anniversary of the death of Swedish inventor and Nobel Foundation founder Alfred Nobel (1833–1896).
Reporting by Agence France-Presse, Reuters, Associated Press and dpa

title: Wild card Zheng Qinwen finally wins in straight sets to reach China Open semi-finals
description: World No 54 sends Beijing crowd roaring as she wins for first time in tournament without requiring decider.
content: Home-grown hero Zheng Qinwen pulled out some of her best tennis to beat Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina 6-3, 7-6 at the China Open on Friday and storm into the semi-finals. Zheng, a wild-card entry in Beijing, finally notched her first straight-sets win of this year’s tournament, having needed more than 10 hours on court to get to the quarter-final. The world No 54 sent the crowd roaring as she punched winners down the line, though the seventh-ranked Svitolina came back fighting to force a second-set tiebreak. Zheng double-faulted on the first point but crawled her way out from a 0-2 deficit and fell on her back victorious after winning her second match point. “Truthfully, because I really wanted to grab this win, I was really nervous,” the 24-year-old told the crowd. “I played really aggressive in important moments,” she said, adding that her opponent “raised her level” in a tight second set. Svitolina made just 13 unforced errors over the one-hour-and-47-minute match, but was outgunned by 48 winners from the 2024 Olympic champion. Later on Friday, Poland’s Iga Swiatek, the 2023 title winner in Beijing, was due to play Belgium’s Elise Mertens for the last semi-final spot. The other semi-final will see Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva up against Nikola Bartunkova of the Czech Republic. Andreeva pushed through two tiebreaks to beat compatriot Ekaterina Alexandrova 7-6, 7-6 on Thursday. The 19-year-old fourth seed is now the favourite for the tournament now that a series of upsets have knocked out her more esteemed rivals. The French Open champion dropped just three points to grab a two-game lead but still needed a tiebreak to edge 28th-ranked Alexandrova in the first set. Bartunkova earlier reached her first WTA 1000 semifinal after beating fellow Czech Karolina Muchova 6-3, 6-0. Bartunkova stamped her authority on the quarterfinal by racing to 5-0 against her seventh-seeded opponent. It was the 20-year-old Bartunkova’s third career win against a top 10-ranked opponent.

title: Homebodies Portland tipped to face well-travelled Pacers in 2027 NBA China Games
description: Not known for their overseas reach, the Portland Trail Blazers have been pencilled in to face Indiana Pacers in Macau next year.
content: Chinese basketball fans wanting to catch a glimpse of Yang Hansen in a Portland Trail Blazers uniform might get their wish next year, with the centre’s side reportedly one of the two teams tipped to play in the 2027 NBA China Games in Macau. The Trail Blazers, who opened their pre-season with a 123-118 win over the Golden State Warriors on Thursday, have Chinese centre Yang, all-star point guard Damian Lillard, and former rookie of the year Ja Morant on their roster. A well-placed source told the South China Morning Post that Portland, who lost in the first round of the play-offs to the San Antonio Spurs this summer, could face the Indiana Pacers and their star player, Tyrese Haliburton, at the Venetian Arena in 12 months’ time. Since drafting Chinese international Yang with the No 16 pick last summer, and coupled with the return of the NBA China Games for the first time since 2019, the Trail Blazers have consistently been discussed as a team that could take part in the pre-season friendlies, while the Boston Celtics are another team that has been mentioned a lot. Not well known as a franchise that has waded into the overseas market, the Portland, Oregon, outfit have rarely travelled, playing only a pair of regular season games against the Los Angeles Clippers in Yokohama in 1994. In contrast, the Pacers ran a campaign to find a new Chinese name to replace their long-standing translation when they recently visited the mainland for the NBA Shanghai Basketball Festival in August. Several senior executives with the team believed their existing name “Buxingzhe”, which means “walkers” in Chinese, appeared to be “too slow” for the squad. “We’re anything but walkers … we’re not slow, we’re not losers,” Ted Wu, executive vice-president of basketball operations and assistant general manager of the Pacers, told fans when explaining the decision. “Our play style is the complete opposite of everything the name is about. We move the ball, we play in transition, we have the fastest point guard in the league. This is our play style. And we need a name to reflect that.” The Pacers are no strangers to competing overseas, having played three regular season games in London and Paris in 2017 and 2025. They are also scheduled to play the Denver Nuggets in Mexico City next month. The two-time Eastern Conference champions, who last won in 2025 before Haliburton injured himself in the NBA Finals, also made eight pre-season appearances in Berlin, Seville, Taipei, Beijing, Manila and Mumbai between 1996 and 2019.

title: Navanethem ‘Navi’ Pillay wins 2026 Nobel Peace Prize
description: South African judge Pillay recognised for her efforts to promote peace and international law.
content: Former UN human rights chief Navanethem “Navi” Pillay has won this year’s Nobel Peace Prize. The South Africa-born jurist was recognised for her efforts to promote peace and international law. The announcement was made by the Norwegian Nobel Committee in Oslo on Friday. Pillay joked that she might “share the prize” with US President Donald Trump if people kept applauding her. “If you clap a little bit more I may share this prize with Trump,” Pillay said in a video posted to social media by the Secretary General of Amnesty International, which showed Pillay being applauded in Nuremberg after the announcement of the award. She said that her first reaction to hearing the news was that it must be a joke. “Being a lawyer and a judge, I still want to verify this,” the 85-year-old said, wanting to make sure it was true. Pillay has served as a judge in South Africa, at the International Criminal Tribunal for Rwanda and the International Criminal Court. She was UN High Commissioner for Human Rights from 2008 to 2014. Pillay was chair of the United Nations Commission of Inquiry on ‌the Occupied Palestinian Territory that concluded last year that Israel has committed genocide in ‌Gaza. Israel dismissed ‌the report as “scandalous”. “The last thing I did is the delivery of the report on Gaza, naming what’s happening there as genocide,” she said. “One of the main reactions to that report is paying tribute to me for my courage. And you can imagine how surprised I was, why would you need courage to speak the truth?” she added. Pillay has held states and national leaders accountable and brought hope to victims of violence and conflict, and showed a firm moral ⁠compass in her long career, the Norwegian Nobel Committee said. “A common thread runs from ‌her early work defending Nelson Mandela and others who stood up against apartheid to her service as a ‌judge in some of the key international court cases ⁠of our time,” ⁠the committee said. The Nobel Peace Prize awarded to Pillay is especially important given current attacks on international law, the president of the ICC said on Friday. “At a time of profound challenges to the international legal order and the rule of law, this recognition carries particular significance,” said Tomoko Akane in a statement. The US has vowed to dismantle the ICC “brick-by-brick”, furious at the court issuing arrest warrants for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over the military campaign in Gaza. Washington has sanctioned top ICC officials and has threatened to slap sanctions against the court as a whole, which would cause the institution significant operational difficulties. “This is an important recognition of the vital role that international justice plays as a cornerstone of lasting peace,” said Akane in her statement. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen congratulated Pillay for confronting “some of humanity’s darkest chapters”. “She has looked the brutality of injustice in the eye and never looked away. She is the defender of the persecuted, the vulnerable, the voiceless and the excluded,” von der Leyen wrote on social media. UN Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Turk hailed the award as “a recognition, a reaffirmation that human rights, the rule of law and justice, and accountability are fundamental to everything, to peace, to security, and prosperity”. In 2025, the prize was awarded to Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado. She dedicated her award to Trump and later gave him her medal. Under Nobel rules, however, the prize itself cannot be transferred to another person. Trump – who is waging a war against Iran – has long coveted the prize and repeatedly said he deserves it. The award is worth 12 million Swedish kronor (about US$1.2 million) this year. Laureates in medicine, physics, chemistry and literature have already been announced. The Nobel Prizes were founded by Alfred Nobel (1833-1896), the inventor of dynamite. In his will, he stipulated that the prizes should be awarded to those who, in the previous year, had been of the greatest benefit to humanity in the various prize categories. Peace was the fifth and final prize area that Nobel mentioned in his will. He left no explanation as to why a Norwegian committee should award the prize for peace, while the other four prizes are handled by Swedish committees. The Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Sciences will be announced on Monday.

title: DFI Retail Group says it will continue to invest in Hong Kong supermarkets
description: Owner of Wellcome, Market Place, 3hreesixty and Oliver’s chains operates a network of more than 325 stores.
content: Hong Kong-headquartered DFI Retail Group, which owns and operates the city’s largest supermarket network, says it will continue to invest in new stores even though consumers remain cautious. Darren Chan, the group’s managing director for food in Hong Kong and Macau, said DFI – whose supermarket chains include Wellcome and Market Place in Hong Kong – was also “looking for opportunities to strengthen” its network where there was “clear customer demand and attractive long-term returns”. “We invest in both new stores and our existing stores,” Chan said. “We open stores where they can better serve local communities, while continuing to modernise our existing network to ensure our store remains attractive, convenient and relevant to evolving customer needs.” Wellcome, Market Place, 3hreesixty and Oliver’s operate a network of more than 325 stores serving more than 14 million customers a month. Chan also oversees 3hreesixty, Oliver’s and San Miu, a supermarket chain in Macau. In the first half of the year, DFI’s food division posted 1.4 per cent growth in sales to US$1.14 billion, although same-store sales declined by 0.2 per cent. The group has been employing new strategies to improve sales as more Hong Kong residents travel to Shenzhen for cheaper shopping and dining options. They include broadening the number of countries it imports from to help bring prices down. There is no one-size-fits-all approach Darren Chan, DFI Wellcome and Market Place have recently teamed up with CJ Foods, South Korea’s largest food company, to enhance their Korean food offerings, with DFI saying the collaboration is expected to generate more than US$22 million in sales. Meanwhile, Market Place recently launched “Taste of Australia”, a gourmet food fair featuring more than 70 Australian brands and over 200 new products including fresh produce, wines and snacks. Chan said Wellcome’s real estate strategy would continue to feature large and small stores. “There is no one-size-fits-all approach,” he said. “The optimal format depends on factors such as catchment demographics, customer shopping missions and local market opportunities.” Hong Kong’s overall retail sales rose by 8.5 per cent year on year in the first eight months of this year, but stand-alone supermarket sales rose by just 1.4 per cent according to the Census and Statistics Department. Sales of all supermarkets, including those in department stores, rose by 1.5 per cent. Formerly known as Dairy Farm, DFI also owns and operates Mannings, 7-Eleven and Ikea in Hong Kong. It also operates Guardian in Southeast Asia, 7-Eleven in Macau, Guangdong province and Singapore and Ikea in Macau, Taiwan and Indonesia.

title: Russia lifts plague lab-related measures. Should China – and the world – be relieved?
description: Moscow says the incident is over but questions remain among Chinese commenters and others on social media globally.
content: While Russian authorities have denied the death of a woman who worked in a laboratory at an anti-plague institute in Siberia was connected with the pathogen, the incident has sparked global concern – including in China – over a potential spread of the disease and a lack of transparency. US President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that he planned to speak with his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin after it emerged late last week that the 28-year-old female lab technician had been admitted to hospital with severe pneumonia and died. Initial unconfirmed reports linked the death to pneumonic plague – a severe lung infection caused by the bacterium Yersinia pestis – following a laboratory exposure at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East. On Thursday, Igor Kobzev, the governor of Irkutsk, said the region had completed quarantine measures and monitoring of close contacts of the technician, who had a case of “community-acquired pneumonia”. “No health issues related to infectious disease were detected. Laboratory analysis of nearly 5,000 samples revealed no dangerous pathogenic microorganisms,” Kobzev added. He did not indicate the cause of the lab worker’s pneumonia. Experts stressed that even if plague had been involved as initially suspected, the risk of a broader outbreak would have remained low. However, suspicions about the incident have continued to be aired across social media platforms, including in China, even after Russian authorities denied the pathogen’s involvement. Russian consumer and health watchdog Rospotrebnadzor said over the weekend that the worker died of a “pneumonia of unknown aetiology”, according to Russian state news agency Tass. The watchdog said samples taken from the patient found no microorganisms associated with the technician’s professional activities. It has yet to confirm the causative agent behind the pneumonia. Kobzev said the employee “had been vaccinated and possessed immunity against the dangerous pathogens she worked with”. Rospotrebnadzor also said no emergency incidents involving pathogenic microorganisms were identified at the institute, which was founded in 1934 to study the plague and now also works with anthrax and other infectious diseases. Yuen Kwok-Yung, chairman of infectious diseases at the University of Hong Kong’s department of microbiology, noted that there was still little microbiological, epidemiological or clinical information available regarding the incident. Based on a general understanding of infectious diseases, Yuen assessed that as long as the bacterial strain involved was not “bioengineered” to possess multidrug resistance or increased transmissibility, there should be no concerns about any effect on Hong Kong. If the pneumonia was caused by the “natural” Yersinia pestis bacterium – denied by Russian authorities, Yuen noted – the outbreak would be contained if all lab, family and hospital contacts were properly quarantined and given antibiotics, he stressed. “If the contact tracing, isolation of cases and quarantine of contacts are correctly done in this Siberian incident, there should not be any crossover into the Chinese mainland,” Yuen told the South China Morning Post in an email on Thursday. Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, director general of the World Health Organization (WHO), said on Wednesday that the agency had been in touch with Russia, which responded that no case of plague had been reported in the Irkutsk region. According to the WHO chief, the Russian authorities also said they had placed about 200 contacts of the woman in quarantine. Tedros said the agency had requested further information and more detail on what prompted the public health measures as well as the health status of the contacts. “As we don’t yet have the full picture of this event, we are not able to conduct a full risk assessment,” he added. Trump told US broadcaster NBC that he did not believe the incident was the result of biological weapons research. According to several popular bloggers in China, suspicions over the incident and the official narrative may not be unfounded. The concerns over bioweapons stem in part from a Telegram post by Siberian journalist and blogger Pavel Stepanov on October 2, which alleged that the infection potentially involved “military-grade strains”. Stepanov’s post also speculated that the cause of the infection was the pneumonic plague and that the incident had occurred in a laboratory. When asked about the outbreak on Tuesday, Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun said “China and Russia maintain close exchanges and cooperation on the prevention and control of infectious diseases, including plague”. Animals frequently move across the border between Russia and China, with the two countries establishing wildlife corridors to help the movement of species such as the endangered Siberian tiger. According to the WHO, Yersinia pestis – the bacterium behind the infamous Black Death that swept through Europe in the 14th century – naturally occurs in wild animals, typically small mammals like rats, as well as their fleas, in Siberia and much of the world. The form that began the outbreak that caused more than 50 million deaths in Europe was bubonic plague, which came about when the pathogen was transmitted from animals and fleas to humans. Pneumonic plague is an especially contagious form that occurs when the bacteria infect the lungs. This can spread from human to human through respiratory droplets or contact with infected materials and is often fatal if left untreated. However, pneumonic plague can be easily treated using antibiotics if administered early, according to the WHO. Yuen said that since the advent of effective antibiotics along with improved hygiene and sanitation measures against rats and rat fleas, the risk of a plague epidemic or pandemic was “rather low”. Brendan Wren, a professor with the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, told the Science Media Centre that while Yersinia pestis was “fairly transmissible”, it was not as transmissible as Covid-19. In a statement posted by the centre on Monday, Wren said the plague remained endemic across the world. There were around 2,000 cases per year that could be treated with standard antibiotics, he added. Tedros said the Russian side had confirmed that an epidemiological investigation was conducted following the incident. “However, [the] WHO has requested further information on the laboratory tests conducted on the individual who died and the contacts, more detail on what prompted the public health measures, and details about the health status of the contacts,” he said. “Timely, complete and transparent information sharing under the International Health Regulations is essential to clarify conflicting reports and enable an accurate assessment of potential public health risks.” According to Tass, monitoring of the close contacts of the deceased researcher identified two cases of Covid-19 and two of rhinovirus, which causes the common cold. Sign up for free now.

title: Poland’s ‘Bloody Friday’ school threats prompt big police operation
description: Police arrested several teens on Friday, including on who posted a photo of ⁠a knife in a class group chat and threatened other students.
content: Thousands of Polish police officers visited schools nationwide on Friday in an effort to reassure pupils after two teenage stabbing sprees in as many days sparked rumours of a “Bloody Friday” of attacks. Social media in Poland has been filled with talk ‌of a supposed online challenge that could be behind the attacks and which would end with a bloodbath at schools on Friday, but police said their investigations had found no evidence of this. By midday, 24,000 police officers had been deployed to 15,000 schools and 19 young people had been detained, mainly for making threats online, Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said. “There will be no compromise here – the safety of youngsters is the most important thing,” he told a press conference. Education Minister Barbara Nowacka said 59 schools around the country were closed, mainly in the ⁠Mazowsze region where this week’s attacks took place. On Thursday, a 15-year-old former pupil wearing a helmet-mounted camera killed one employee and injured two others at a ‌Polish primary school in Leszczydol-Nowiny, northeast of Warsaw. On Wednesday, a 19-year-old wounded 10 people including himself at another school in Ostroleka, north of the capital. The scale of the police deployment and the school closures underscored the shock caused ‌by two attacks in a country where school stabbings have been very rare, and the speed with which online rumours amplified the ⁠fear. In Ostroleka, schools were operating as normal but attendance was just 25 per cent, the PAP state news agency quoted Mayor Pawel Niewiadomski as saying. In Warsaw, 59-year-old NGO manager and mother-of-four Dorota Czekaj told ‌Reuters the week’s events had left her “simply terrified”. She called for a tough response to online content that could encourage violence. “Unlimited access to all sorts of content, some of it very negative, certainly ‌affects … our ‌brains and contributes to a general social desensitisation in some way,” she said. “And I think we simply have to respond to this more firmly.” Authorities ‌warned people of the risks of online disinformation, with Defence Minister Wladyslaw Kosiniak-Kamysz suggesting Russia could use such events to sow panic. Russia has repeatedly denied attempting ⁠to destabilise Western countries using online disinformation. Polish police made a string of arrests on Friday. These included a 13-year-old from Warsaw who posted a photo of ⁠a knife in a class group chat and threatened other students, a 14-year-old in Warsaw detained on school grounds with a knife and firecrackers, and two 15-year-olds from Pruszkow County just outside the capital who posted a video with threats to kill. Several social media ‌accounts posted pictures on Thursday of a ‌TikTok account which supposedly belonged to the attacker from Leszczydol-Nowiny and featured images taken just before the incident. Reuters was unable to find the account, which appeared to have been taken down. “Officers from the Central Bureau for Combating Cybercrime (CBZC) are aware of the content posted on the TikTok account in question,” CBZC told Reuters by email, adding that the platform was cooperating with the agency. TikTok did not reply to an emailed request for comment.

title: China state funds double down on Hua Hong in legacy chip push
description: State investors increase support for the contract chipmaker and a new Wuxi fab as Beijing strengthens domestic semiconductor supply.
content: Chinese state funds are ramping up support for the country’s second-largest contract chipmaker, pouring billions of yuan into the parent of Hua Hong Grace Semiconductor and a new manufacturing facility to fuel Beijing’s drive for self-reliance in mature-node chips. The capital blitz, spanning Hua Hong’s Shanghai-based parent company and a fabrication plant in Wuxi, highlights how government-coordinated financing is doubling down on domestic foundries, as Washington tightens technology restrictions on China. Registered capital of Hua Hong Group, the Shanghai- and Hong Kong-listed chipmaker’s owner, surged to 19.7 billion yuan (US$2.9 billion) from 13.5 billion yuan, according to a stock exchange filing on Thursday. The 6.2 billion yuan injection was led by Shanghai Guosheng Group, a state-backed investment vehicle. Following the transaction, Guosheng’s direct stake in Hua Hong Group would jump to 41.7 per cent from 15.3 per cent, while its indirect holding would rise to 10.2 per cent from 3.8 per cent. The Shanghai State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission – the local state-assets regulator – also injected 19.7 million yuan, maintaining its role as Hua Hong Group’s ultimate actual controller. Blocked by the US from acquiring the most advanced chipmaking equipment, including extreme ultraviolet lithography systems, Beijing has channelled state funds towards dominating legacy and mature-node semiconductors, generally defined as chips made using 28-nanometre process technology and above. While less sophisticated than cutting-edge artificial intelligence processors, legacy chips remain essential for electric vehicles, industrial automation, Internet of Things devices and consumer electronics. Hua Hong has accelerated investment in its third fab project in Wuxi, in China’s eastern province of Jiangsu. Registered capital at the joint venture managing the fab skyrocketed to US$4.17 billion from 6.68 million yuan (US$998,000) earlier this month – an over 4,000-fold increase – according to Chinese corporate database Tianyancha. The venture has drawn major state investors, including the National Integrated Circuit Industry Investment Fund – known as the “Big Fund” – alongside local government capital. The move follows a fundraising round in September, when Hua Hong invested US$2 billion in the facility. Hua Hong and its Shanghai subsidiary hold a combined 51 per cent controlling stake, with the remaining stake held by state-backed investors. Construction of the facility, known as Fab 9B, began in March. It would focus on specialty technology chips used in power devices, analog chips and embedded storage, according to Hua Hong. Once fully operational, Fab 9B would add 55,000 wafers to Hua Hong’s monthly production capacity, expanding its total Wuxi capacity by roughly 30 per cent. During an earnings call in May, Hua Hong chairman and president Bai Peng said the company “did not see any impact” from US export controls on equipment procurement for the Wuxi project. Hua Hong’s Hong Kong-listed shares fell 1.1 per cent to HK$94.55 on Friday, tracking a broader pullback across Chinese semiconductor stocks.

title: Opinion | US-Japan-Poland strategic triangle can encourage a ‘peaceful war’
description: The catalyst for this new architecture of deterrence in an age of fragmented interdependence lies less in China than in Russia.
