They can prepare in Hong Kong, but they need to compete in 100 matches a year against the toughest competitors from the age of 14 to 18.” Filling the head coach vacancy at the Hong Kong Sports Institute with someone bringing proven international experience with it is also on the cards. However, Cheng is not alone in shouldering the load, as he was supported by a huge team during his second presidential term at the HKCTA. Among them was Ronnie Cheng Kay-yen, a respected headmaster and career educator, who joined the national team set-up as the manager at the start of the year. “We spent a lot of time studying and researching the best tennis nations and working out what is right for Hong Kong. We need to apply global benchmarks and give it a local identity,” Michael Cheng said. “Tennis is a tough sport, and it’s difficult for players to succeed alone. “We need to build a support structure to help them, and when they commit, we have to be there for them.” Ronnie Cheng, who is also the headmaster of Diocesan Boys’ School, added: “I want to reaffirm our commitment to a stronger team bond founded on teamwork, mutual support and shared growth. Every player has an important role to play. “It is by standing together, learning together, and improving together that we will continue to move forward. My job is to build the team for the future.” Wong, who is presently ranked 96th in the world, is 22 years old, and Thompson is 18. Officials believe another 18-year-old, Nicholas Cheng Siu-chi, is “within reach” of the junior slams. Richie Choi Fu-wang, the Orange Bowl boys’ singles runner-up in 2023, is the next in line, having already played a junior under-14 Wimbledon event last year. “We are reviewing and need to study and identify the right ingredients for success and build on them,” Ronnie Cheng said. “Note that all the players who won our recent medals are full-time athletes. Players need to commit and compete with the best. When players commit, we will be there for them.”

title: Meet architect Betty Ng, founder of Hong Kong’s Collective Studio
description: Ng and her two former Harvard classmates spearhead design projects across the region – from auction spaces and boutiques to water depots.
content: Architect Betty Ng founded Collective Studio, a Hong Kong-based firm that also specialises in interior and exhibition design, in 2015. She now oversees the studio’s operations – including teams in Perth, Madrid and London – with her former Harvard University classmates Juan Minguez and Chi Yan Chan. Together they spearhead some of Asia’s most forward-thinking design projects, from the expansive Asia-Pacific headquarters of Christie’s in Hong Kong to the radical, environmentally friendly Ludan Sports Center and Water Depot in Shenzhen. Other notable projects include several outposts for Hong Kong multi-brand boutique Kapok, as well as the sustainable cocktail bar Penicillin. Collective Studio’s nonconformist, avant-garde approach to architecture and design begins with the very foundations of the organisation. In line with its name, it operates as a true collective of architects, designers and creative minds. The firm challenges the status quo in the breadth and depth of its design projects, practising design “as a methodology, instead of a style” as it says on its website. Collective Studio’s projects embrace a progressive approach that goes beyond being client-driven and stylistically impressive to address common real-world issues in design. The Ludan Sports Center and Water Depot, for example, built atop an existing water depot along the Shenzhen River, was designed with both form and function in mind. Its expansive rooftop is not only a public terrace but also a stepped drain collecting water for the park on ground level as well as the water depot itself. There’s also the deceptively simple interior of the 50,000sq ft Christie’s APAC headquarters inside the new Zaha Hadid Architects-designed skyscraper, The Henderson. What at first glance looks like an open floor plan with white walls belies striking technical functionality. Many of the walls are movable to accommodate the needs of the auctioneer and exhibitors. Open workstations in staff areas are designed to foster team collaboration while retractable systems like large-scale sliding LED screens and ceiling-hung drop-down video production cameras allow the gallery spaces to convert easily into an auction room ready for a live broadcast. These projects support Collective Studio’s stated aim of designing spaces “that insist on clarity and function, with beauty as a consequence”. Exploring how great design serves not only the eyes but every aspect of our daily lives continues to drive the firm’s practice. “Living and working across vastly different geographies breeds an instinctual open-mindedness and a recognition that no single question has only one answer,” Ng says. “This is precisely what I want to see reflected in our profession; there may be clear design principles, but there should never be a rigid formula.” “Rules are not to be broken,” Ng concludes. “They are meant to be re-engineered, rewired and penetrated.”

title: Asking for a Friend: Help! How can I discuss my views on my parent’s superstitions?
description: Each week, we respond to a question from our readers and give advice and resources they can turn to.
content:
Do you have a personal question you’ve been too afraid to ask? Whether it is about school, family or your social life, you can share it with us through this form . Don’t worry, you’ll remain anonymous.
My mum is very superstitious about the number four. I recently got into the school basketball team, and my jersey number is four. She wants me to ask my coach for a different number. How can I persuade her that wearing a number four basketball jersey is not a problem?
Congratulations on making the basketball team! This is a significant achievement, and you should be very proud.
Seeking to understand your mother’s perspective rather than reacting with frustration demonstrates empathy that will benefit you both on and off the court.
It is completely understandable why this situation is stressful. After putting so much effort into making the team, the last thing you want is to have an awkward conversation with your coach about changing your jersey number.
Let’s reframe your mother’s concern not as an obstacle, but as a heartfelt expression of her love. In many cultures, the number four is associated with misfortune. When children step onto the sports field, parents often feel a profound lack of control over their safety. For your mother, focusing on the jersey number is likely a tangible way for her to try to protect you from injury.
To effectively handle this situation, avoid debating the logic behind superstitions , as deeply rooted cultural beliefs are not easily changed through argument.
Acknowledge her concerns verbally without directly endorsing the superstition itself. For example, you might say, “Mum, I understand that you want me to be safe, and I really appreciate how much you care about my well-being.”
Next, highlight that the jersey number is assigned by your coach and is not a personal choice. By presenting it as a fixed rule, you can alleviate any pressure associated with the decision.
Additionally, you can offer cognitive reframing by noting that different cultures have superstitions surrounding various numbers, which can help diminish the significance of this particular one.
It is essential to invite her to be part of your athletic journey.
The more she learns about your preparation and the structured nature of the sport, the more secure she will feel.
Finally, provide clear reassurance. Let her know that you will play mindfully and prioritise your safety during every game. Often, parental anxiety decreases significantly when they feel heard and see that their child is prepared.
Wear your jersey with confidence and stay focused on your performance. We wish you the best of luck in your games. You have the maturity to handle both the game and this relationship beautifully.
This question was answered by Tiffany Chiu, a child psychotherapist and play and behavioural therapist at Your Relationship Clinic

title: Flavio Bolsonaro says he would work with China and US as Brazil’s president
description: As leader, Bolsonaro would assume control of an economy that is heavily dependent on China – by far Brazil’s largest trading partner.
content: Flavio Bolsonaro said he would work with the US and China if he becomes Brazil’s president, after a surprise election performance left him poised to join a wave of conservative leaders pushing Latin America closer to Washington. “I’m not going to pick sides,” Bolsonaro said at an event in Brasilia on Thursday. “My side will be the Brazilian people, whether we’re dealing with China, Israel, the Middle East, Argentina or India. It doesn’t matter. That’s how I’m going to govern.” Bolsonaro finished ahead of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva by about two points in Sunday’s first-round election, a result that sparked a surge in Brazilian assets due to investor views that he is more likely to pursue market-friendly financial policies. Bolsonaro would take 52 per cent to Lula’s 48 per cent of valid votes, excluding blank and invalid ballots, in the October 25 run-off, a Datafolha poll released on Thursday evening showed. The survey has a margin of error of plus or minus two percentage points. Bolsonaro outperformed Datafolha’s final poll of the first round by about five points. Victory for Bolsonaro would complete a conservative sweep of South America’s major economies for right-wing allies of US President Donald Trump, who has sought to reassert US influence over a western hemisphere that has moved increasingly closer to China. Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, has pledged to work closely with the Trump administration on trade and crime while outlining plans to join the US-led Shield of the Americas security initiative. He visited Trump at the White House in May. But as president, he would assume control of an economy that is heavily dependent on China. The country is by far Brazil’s largest trading partner and the chief buyer of agricultural exports that form the backbone of Latin America’s largest economy. Chinese companies have also poured money into Brazil’s energy, electric vehicles and manufacturing industries, and large amounts of China-produced consumer goods enter the country every day. Lula has deepened Brazil’s ties to Beijing while also pushing to diversify its trade relationships with other parts of the world. He has had a hot-and-cold relationship with Trump since the US placed tariffs on many Brazilian goods last year as part of an unsuccessful effort to help Jair Bolsonaro avoid conviction on coup attempt charges. Datafolha surveyed 2,520 people from October 6 to 7, according to Folha de S.Paulo. The poll has a margin of error of plus or minus 2 percentage points, a confidence level of 95 per cent and is registered with Brazil’s electoral court.

title: Editorial | Hong Kong businesses must stay agile to attract tourists
description: While visitor numbers were up during the National Day holiday, changing travel and spending patterns mean the city’s businesses must keep adapting or risk losing out.
content: The National Day “golden week” has long been a barometer of Hong Kong’s tourism and business health. While there was a reassuring uptick in visitor numbers and business activity this year, the figures also underscore the more complex and challenging environment facing various sectors. The simultaneous outflow of residents heading north, combined with evolving spending patterns among southbound mainland visitors, continues to put the city’s tourism facilities and business adaptability to a stern test. If the crowds at shopping districts and tourist hotspots are any reference, Hong Kong still appears to have strong appeal in that respect. The city recorded more than 1.42 million mainland visitor arrivals during the seven-day holiday, exceeding the government’s forecast of 1.29 million. Arrival numbers during the first few days were especially remarkable, with 277,304 mainland visitors descending on October 1, up 19.1 per cent from 232,751 on the first day of last year’s holiday. The visitors were not just day trippers. Only 49,798 mainland visitors left the city on the first day, resulting in a net inflow of 227,506. It is also good news that the hotel sector reported bookings of more than 90 per cent on the first day of the holiday and expected overall occupancy to reach about 90 per cent during the break. Hopefully, the longer stays translated into higher spending and benefits for businesses and the economy. A shopping mall in Tsim Sha Tsui said footfall reached a record for a National Day golden week holiday while tourist spending rose by 26 per cent year on year. Another business group said both footfall and turnover at its major shopping malls recorded double-digit year-on-year growth. Indeed, the city continues to attract a wide spectrum of holidaymakers. Some came for the fireworks spectacle, the lantern display and other seasonal attractions; others ventured to the city’s countryside popularised on mainland social media. The influx to these nature hotspots continues to test tourism facilities and their management. Take the popular volcanic rock columns in Sai Kung. While a real-name registration system for crowd control at Po Pin Chau drew some 2,420 bookings on National Day, exceeding the official capacity of 2,000, only 1,160 people showed up, including walk-in registrations. The authorities should review the arrangement to enhance visitors’ convenience and experience. Many Hongkongers also took advantage of the holiday to head north for dining and entertainment. But that did not necessarily mean local restaurants and retailers suffered. Thanks to various discounts and promotions by some 3,800 catering outlets and other sectors, there were crowds and queues across the city. The changing travel and spending patterns mean Hong Kong businesses must continue to adapt or risk losing out. This requires not only adjustment in price and strategy but also quality and variety. This is especially important because the trend is expected to evolve further as cross-border integration intensifies in the coming years. The challenging business environment in recent years has put different sectors through a painful adjustment period. Those that manage to survive stand a better chance of thriving as they enhance their offerings to attract customers from near and far. The “go-north” trend need not be a one-way exodus. If anything, it is more a reminder that it will take greater effort to retain those who are willing to stay and spend when there are good deals. Staging more promotional events and enhancing nightlife options and neighbourhood attractions could help retain domestic spending that might otherwise leak across the border. The authorities are right to strengthen the city’s tourism appeal. In addition to staging more mega-events, the recent “Only in Hong Kong” promotions entice visitors to go beyond the usual attractions and experience what is unique to the city. There were 36.7 million visitors in the first eight months of this year, up 11 per cent from the same period last year. Gone are the days when the city can just sit back and milk the cash cow of tourism with the usual offerings. Amid growing challenges, many local businesses have proved to be resilient and resourceful. They absorb shocks, pivot quickly and capitalise on risks and opportunities. Such qualities must be further strengthened as more testing times lie ahead.

title: Profile | How Cantopop pioneer and avid arts lover Anthony Wong Yiu-ming shaped Hong Kong culture
description: Wong, one-half of Cantopop duo Tat Ming Pair, is a solo artist, label pioneer and a fearless LGBTQ and pro-democracy advocate.
content: This is the 87th instalment in a biweekly series profiling major Hong Kong pop culture figures of recent decades. For Hong Kong’s culture enthusiasts, sitting just a few seats away from Anthony Wong Yiu-ming at an art-house film screening or standing steps from him at an underground gig has long been a serendipitous staple of the city’s arts scene. He is legendary for his ubiquitous presence as an ordinary spectator. Beyond his genuine enthusiasm as a fellow audience member, the 64-year-old Cantopop pioneer has spent decades shaping the city’s pop landscape – as a decorated solo artist, one half of the legendary duo Tat Ming Pair and founder of the record label People Mountain People Sea. Across a four-decade-long career, the singer, songwriter and producer has refused to separate art from social advocacy, using his music to comment on politics, identity and civil liberties. After completing high school, he enrolled in Hong Kong broadcasting channel TVB’s training course in 1981, landing minor acting roles before briefly serving as an assistant director for the show Woman Today in 1983. He also had a short-lived career as a production assistant at an advertising agency until he abruptly quit. “I resigned because the company said I had to work overtime this month and couldn’t take a holiday, but I was going to see Bowie,” Wong recalled in an interview with the now-defunct Music Colony Bi-weekly in 1995, referring to David Bowie’s Serious Moonlight Tour in 1983. The birth of Tat Ming Pair Wong began working as a DJ at Commercial Radio Hong Kong in 1984. His life changed that same year when he responded to a magazine advertisement placed by fellow musician Tats Lau Yee-tat, who was seeking a vocalist for a band. United by their shared interest in electronic music, the duo – billed as Tat Ming Pair – signed with PolyGram Records in 1985. They released their self-titled debut EP in 1986 to critical and commercial success. Tat Ming Pair stood out in the booming Cantopop scene for their distinctive 1980s new wave sound, drawing frequent comparisons to the Pet Shop Boys. With his long hair, Wong’s look further emphasised the duo as an alternative force, contrasting the slick aesthetics of other male pop stars. “When we signed with PolyGram … we didn’t like to hear much of the music in Hong Kong,” Wong told the South China Morning Post in 1996. “So we made our own music to provide an alternative.” Their breakthrough came with their second album, The Story of the Stone (1987). Tracks such as “Angels of the Road” and “Beautiful New World” captured the existential anxieties of Hong Kong youth after the 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration. At the peak of the late-80s “band boom”, Tat Ming Pair occasionally outperformed mainstream rivals, edging out Beyond – arguably the city’s most beloved band – to win gold in the ultimate group category at the 1988 Commercial Radio Ultimate Song Chart Awards. Breaking taboos Tat Ming Pair never shied away from political and social taboos. Their 1988 song “Forbidden Colours” illustrated a romance that must remain in the shadows, serving as both a metaphor for marginalised identities, such as LGBTQ love, and a reflection of the political anxiety surrounding nonconformity. Wong, who realised he was gay during high school, eventually drifted away from his Christian upbringing. Describing his world view as broader than any single dogma, he told HK Magazine in 2006: “If music is my religion, so are film and love. I am a man of many religions.” Tat Ming Pair disbanded in 1991 over differing musical directions, though they would reunite for milestone concerts in the decades that followed. Indeed, it was at the band’s 25th anniversary concert series at the Hong Kong Coliseum in 2012 that Wong publicly came out as gay on stage. Even before then, he never truly saw himself as being “in the closet”, as he had openly written about queer love. While media outlets portrayed his coming out as sensational, Wong had a much more grounded perspective. “I’ve never thought about being a ‘gay icon’ because it’s not important to me,” he told HK Magazine in 2016. “I don’t do what I do to be an icon. As long as I think it’s the right thing to do, I’ll do it,” Wong founded the pro-LGBTQ advocacy group BigLove Alliance in 2013 and led Pink Dot HK as a prominent headliner. Building an indie empire Wong launched a solo career with albums such as Faith, Hope and Love (1992). He collaborated with lyricist Albert Leung Wai-man (better known as Lin Xi or Lam Chik) and produced for others, shaping alternative Cantopop. Wong’s eclectic visual style was partly shaped by his long-standing ties to the avant-garde theatre group Zuni Icosahedron, forging creative partnerships that would heavily influence his musical direction. In 1999, Wong established the independent collective and record label People Mountain People Sea, named after his 1997 cover album of the same title. That allowed Wong and his regular collaborators to make and distribute music without relying on any major record company. Alongside musicians like GayBird (also known as Keith Leung Kei-cheuk), Jason Choi Tak-choi, Yu Yat-yiu and Veronica Lee Duen-han, Wong built a production engine to nurture and launch younger artists, such as the indie-pop acts at17 and PixelToy. People Mountain People Sea also helped shape Hong Kong pop, producing songs for A-list artists such as Faye Wong, Eason Chan Yick-shun and Miriam Yeung Chin-wah. In 2002, Wong put together a joint EP – Cross Over – with Cantopop icon Leslie Cheung Kwok-wing. Extending his commitment to the region’s arts scene, Wong co-founded the non-profit Renaissance Foundation in 2012 to incubate new talent across music, film and literature. Accolades and activism Meanwhile, his work continued to earn top accolades. In January 2019, Tat Ming Pair received the RTHK Golden Needle Award, widely considered Hong Kong music’s highest honour. Just four months later, however, the duo’s music was removed from mainland Chinese streaming sites because of the political nature of their work. Wong had been unable to perform on the mainland since his involvement in Hong Kong’s 2014 Occupy movement, during which he visited protest sites, gave speeches and performed the song “Raise the Umbrella” with singer Denise Ho Wan-see. Though left out of work for months, his support for the pro-democracy camp remained unwavering during the anti-extradition bill protests in 2019. In August 2021, Hong Kong’s Independent Commission Against Corruption arrested Wong, charging him with “corrupt conduct” for singing two songs at a 2018 political campaign rally in support of pro-democracy candidate Au Nok-hin. The charges were dropped in exchange for an 18-month “good behaviour” bind-over order. Wong has since transitioned to international touring and independent releases. In late 2025, he released a song named after Vietnamese-American poet Ocean Vuong’s novel On Earth We’re Briefly Gorgeous (2019), describing it as an elder’s advice to youth navigating displacement. He also co-produced Ho’s latest project, Rive-Sud, Montreal (2026), in which she pays tribute to her immigration experience. Reflecting on his decision to remain in Hong Kong while performing abroad, Wong shared a pragmatic view during a 2024 seminar in Vancouver, Canada: “If you want to continue to find space to survive [in Hong Kong] … be as nimble as a snake and as kind as a dove. If not, how can you live?” While he has thought about leaving, he maintained that his heart remains in the city. “It doesn’t matter where I am now,” he said. “Anywhere is my world.”

title: Central retail shop bought by Swiss heir in ‘rare’ Hong Kong market move
description: Local developer Hip Shing Hong sells ground-floor shop on Arbuthnot Road after holding the property for 55 years.
content: In a rare market move, a long-established local developer sold a Central retail shop that was held for over 50 years to an heir of Swiss underwear maker Triumph, according to data from the Land Registry, a deal analysts have called “highly unusual”. The use of international capital to acquire local retail assets in Hong Kong is uncommon. Triumph International did not immediately respond to a request for comment from the South China Morning Post. The transaction involved a ground-floor shop at Arbuthnot House, 10-12 Arbuthnot Road, Central, with a gross area of about 1,474 square feet. It sold for HK$21.4 million – or HK$14,518 per square foot – late last month, the data showed. The shop is currently leased to the private members’ club Salon No. 10. The original owner was Associated Builders Corporation Limited. According to the Companies Registry, the company’s directors include Fong Fu-wah, Jonathan Fong Tim-fai, Raymond Fong Man-cheong, David Fong Man-hung, and Vincent Fong Tim-ming – all of whom are family members of the late Henry Fong Yun-wah, chairman of the Hong Kong-based developer Hip Shing Hong. The company purchased the shop unit in 1971 for about HK$940,000. Having held the property for 55 years, it realised a paper profit of HK$20.46 million – an increase of nearly 22-fold. Stanley Poon Chi-ming, managing director at Centaline Commercial, stated that Hip Shing Hong had held the property for a long time, using it primarily for rental income, and kept a low profile regarding its sale. “Hip Shing Hong is a long-established local developer; it has primarily focused on rental income and rarely sells properties,” he said. “However, the company has been restructuring its property portfolio and offloading non-core commercial real estate to reduce its holdings.” Centaline Commercial has assisted Hip Shing Hong in selling some of its assets, such as its office space in Mong Kok. Hip Shing Hong’s current strategy focuses on selling off scattered, non-core properties to generate cash for future land acquisitions and development, Poon noted. According to the Land Registry, the new buyer of the retail shop is Aimba Limited. The company’s director is Oliver Michael Spiesshofer, a descendant of Johann Gottfried Spiesshofer – one of the founders of the Swiss-headquartered undergarment group Triumph International – and the current CEO and managing partner of the company. Poon noted that this transaction is “extremely rare”, as foreign capital has historically seldom been used to purchase retail properties, especially street shops, in Hong Kong. “The vast majority of local retail properties are purchased by Hong Kong investors and companies, as locals are more familiar with the market,” he said. “Chinese [investors] have a particular fondness for such properties – adhering to the saying that ‘a single shop can support three generations’.” Edwin Lee, founder and CEO of Bridgeway Prime Shop Fund Management, described the property as an “excellent buy”. The shop features a large floor area and is located in an area with strong purchasing power for high-end consumption near SoHo and Lan Kwai Fong. “The tenant is a private club, and the premises feature high-quality fit-outs,” Lee added. “Based on the current transaction price, achieving a 4 per cent yield would require a monthly rent of around HK$70,000 (US$8,920.1) to HK$80,000 – a rate that is certainly achievable for this location – and I believe the risk of such an upscale tenant vacating is minimal.” “I believe the transaction price is 20% lower than the market price,” Lee said.

title: US to live-stream firing squad execution of Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan
description: Pentagon promises public viewing for Nidal Hasan in first US military execution since 1961.
content: The US will live-stream the US Army’s coming firing squad execution of a gunman who killed 13 people at the Fort Hood military base in 2009, the Pentagon said, in what would be an unprecedented broadcast of a US execution. Nidal Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist, is set to become the first person to be executed by firing squad by the US military since 1945. The execution is scheduled for December 3 at the same sprawling Texas base where Hasan opened fire with a laser-sighted handgun in ‌a medical facility. It comes amid heightened debate in the US over the death penalty following the botched lethal injection of a Tennessee woman last week. “It will be live-streamed. Details will follow,” a Pentagon official said. Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, who championed the push to execute Hasan by firing squad, confirmed plans to live-stream the execution in an X post. Media have sought to televise US executions in the past but have been blocked by the courts. No other country is known to televise or live-stream a legal execution, experts said. Public executions have become exceedingly rare worldwide. Among countries known to conduct them in recent years are Iran and Taliban-run Afghanistan. Extrajudicial lynchings in the United States, often by white mobs targeting black Americans, were public spectacles well into the 20th century. The last legally sanctioned public execution in the ⁠United States was conducted in 1936, death penalty experts said. Thousands watched that 1936 hanging of a young black man who had been convicted of raping a white woman. Hegseth told the Human Events Daily programme that deciding to execute ‌Hasan by firing squad at Fort Hood on a Thursday at 1pm – the approximate time, day of the week and location of the 2009 shooting – was a “no-brainer”. “We’ll make sure that people are able to watch it, that it’s public. Because people need to understand that … there’s serious consequences for these types of things,” Hegseth said. Asked if Hasan had ‌made any final requests, Hegseth said: “Don’t care. We’ll see him on December 3”. A military jury sentenced Hasan to death in August 2013, after finding him guilty ⁠of 45 counts of premeditated murder and attempted premeditated ⁠murder. The shooting came weeks before Hasan, now 56, was scheduled to be deployed to Afghanistan. He was left partially paralysed and confined to a wheelchair from being shot by police during his arrest. Under US military law, a US president must approve an execution by firing squad. President Donald ‌Trump did so on Hegseth’s recommendation, the Pentagon said on Monday. The group Death Penalty Action, which opposes capital punishment, said Hasan’s execution would be the first military execution since 1961. According to the Death Penalty Information Centre, ‌the 1961 execution ‌was carried out by hanging. The last known executions by US military firing squads were in 1945, the centre reported. At least five states have firing squads on the books, according to the Death Penalty Information Centre. In 2025, South Carolina carried out the first such ‌execution in the United States in 15 years. Death by firing squad ‌is one of several forms of capital punishment the Trump administration recently added to permissible forms of execution for the gravest of federal crimes, along with electrocution and gas asphyxiation. The number of federal execution options was expanded in part because of increasing difficulties in obtaining drugs for lethal injections, which have also sometimes proved challenging to carry out. Plans by the state of Tennessee to execute a woman for the first time in more than 200 years went awry last week when prison personnel botched attempts to administer a lethal injection, leaving the death-row inmate, Christa Pike, alive but hospitalised.

title: China breakthrough projected to put sustainable aviation fuel gross profit margin past 50%
description: Biomass-to-jet fuel conversion method could boost production and help meet global aviation industry’s net-zero carbon goals, researchers say.
content: Chinese researchers have developed a catalyst that converts synthesis gas into sustainable jet fuel – an advance that could boost production, help meet net-zero carbon goals and yield a gross profit margin above 50 per cent. The team verified the efficacy of the chemical catalyst in a thousand-tonne pilot test and found that combining woody biomass-derived synthesis gas, or syngas, with the cobalt-manganese catalyst enabled the “highly efficient synthesis of jet fuel”. Based on a techno-economic analysis that modelled a planned 100,000-tonnes-per-year jet fuel plant, the researchers estimated they could achieve a gross profit margin of over 50 per cent. “The excellent pilot test results and the positive techno-economic and life-cycle assessments underscore its strong potential for industrial deployment,” the team said in a paper published in the peer-reviewed journal Nature Communications in September. The team led by researchers from the Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) Shanghai Advanced Research Institute said their research also established design principles to break selectivity limitations during syngas conversion. Unlike conventional petroleum-based jet fuel, sustainable aviation fuel is made from non-fossil fuel feedstocks such as municipal solid waste, cooking oil and biomass, according to the US Department of Energy. Intended to be used as a drop-in fuel that is blended with conventional fuel, it could reduce life-cycle carbon emissions by about 80 per cent compared with standard jet fuel. These emissions savings come from the production process, as emissions are still produced in the combustion of sustainable fuels. The aviation industry accounts for about 2 to 3 per cent of global human-made carbon dioxide emissions. The International Civil Aviation Organization has set a goal for the industry to reach net-zero emissions by 2050. To achieve the goal, sustainable aviation fuels must be adopted on a large scale. Even so, sustainable fuel production is projected to reach only 2.4 million tonnes this year, or the equivalent of just 0.8 per cent of total global jet fuel consumption, according to the International Air Transport Association (IATA). In a report published in June, the IATA said jet fuel shortages and rising costs following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz could have played out differently if investments in sustainable fuels had been prioritised sooner. The main challenge facing the industry is scaling sustainable aviation fuel production so that costs can be reduced. The IATA report said sustainable aviation fuel was several times more expensive than conventional fuel, owing to still-developing production technologies, expensive feedstocks and large upfront investment requirements. There are several different established chemical pathways to obtain sustainable aviation fuel, including Fischer-Tropsch synthesis or the conversion of syngas – a mixture of carbon monoxide and hydrogen – into jet fuel-range hydrocarbons. The syngas used in this process can be derived from the gasification or conversion of different forms of biomass. The Fischer-Tropsch route “offers high feedstock flexibility, well-established industrial infrastructure with strong scalability and the ability to produce fully drop-in hydrocarbon fuels”, the Chinese researchers said, adding it was “therefore expected to play a critical role” in achieving the 2050 sustainable aviation fuel targets. The team, which also included researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University and the Shanxi Research Institute, said more efficient catalysts were needed to enable practical large-scale applications using this method. In their paper, the team detailed a new cobalt-manganese catalyst with a carbon monoxide conversion rate of nearly 83 per cent. It also had a jet-fuel range hydrocarbon selectivity of more than 67 per cent, compared with below 50 per cent for most reported catalysts. This “overcomes the long-standing activity-selectivity trade-off for previous catalysts”. Beyond woody biomass, the catalyst could be used to process various “real-world” syngas feedstocks, the researchers added. After testing their catalyst in a kilogram-scale trial, the team completed a 1,000 tonnes-per-year pilot test last year. “At present, we plan to build a factory with a 100,000-tonne annual capacity using biomass gasification-derived syngas as the feedstock” in the city of Luzhou in China’s southwestern Sichuan province before 2028, the team said. Techno-economic analysis of a plant of this scale showed that, under a baseline of 8,000 operating hours per year, it could generate an estimated US$302 million in annual sales revenue. With annual operating costs of about US$114 million and an estimated “gross profit” of US$165 million, the facility could achieve a gross profit margin of nearly 55 per cent, based on the team’s projections. Biomass feedstock accounted for more than half of the operational costs, they said, highlighting the importance of a cost-effective biomass supply chain for the project to be economically viable. The CAS-led team is not the only one aiming to scale up new sustainable aviation fuel production methods. In August, a 1,000-tonne sustainable aviation jet-fuel pilot plant developed by Sichuan Jinxiang Sairui Chemical and a research team from Tsinghua University passed a major continuous operation test. As the world’s first to produce sustainable jet fuel via direct carbon dioxide hydrogenation at this scale, the facility had technical approval from the China Petroleum and Chemical Industry Federation, which deemed it “internationally leading”, according to Tsinghua. By using tail-gas recycling and hydrocarbon recovery, the total carbon dioxide utilisation rate reached 98 per cent. The successful trial paves the way for a 10,000-tonne industrial demonstration unit. The team also estimated that a full-scale 100,000-tonne plant could recover its initial investment in 2½ years based on present fuel costs.

title: Hong Kong rejects US downgrade to lowest tier in human trafficking report
description: US cites declining prosecutions and failure to identify victims exploited in Hong Kong; city rejects downgrade as ‘entirely unfounded’.
content: The United States has downgraded Hong Kong to the lowest tier in its annual human trafficking report, citing shortcomings in prosecutions and victim identification, an assessment the city’s government rejected as “entirely unfounded”. The US State Department’s 2026 Trafficking in Persons (TIP) Report, released on Thursday, moved Hong Kong from the Tier 2 Watch List, where it had been listed for two consecutive years, to Tier 3. That places the city alongside mainland China and Macau among 20 jurisdictions in the bottom tier, which also includes North Korea, Russia, Iran and Afghanistan. The Hong Kong government rejected the downgrade in a statement issued early on Friday, calling the rating “entirely unfounded” and “a blatant attempt to tarnish Hong Kong’s sterling reputation”. “TIP has never been a prevalent problem in Hong Kong, and there has never been any sign that Hong Kong is being actively used by syndicates as a destination or transit point for TIP,” a government spokesman said, referring to trafficking in persons. The US report said the Hong Kong government did not fully meet minimum standards for eliminating trafficking and “is not making significant efforts to do so”. The rankings assess governments’ efforts to combat trafficking, not the crime’s prevalence. According to the report, Hong Kong authorities investigated 11 trafficking cases in 2025, all involving forced labour, up from seven a year earlier. However, they prosecuted one suspect, down from two, and convicted two sex traffickers, one of whom was jailed for less than a year. All 15 victims identified last year were Hong Kong residents who had been forced to work in scam centres in Myanmar and Cambodia. Authorities did not identify any victims exploited within Hong Kong, despite conducting about 12,100 initial screenings. Hong Kong government hits out at report, accuses US of double standards The Hong Kong government confirmed the screening and victim figures, saying screenings had increased by seven per cent from 2024. It said bringing residents home safely, identifying them as victims and pursuing those implicated showed its commitment to fighting trafficking. The spokesman accused Washington of double standards, pointing to studies and reports highlighting under-reporting of trafficking cases by US law enforcement. The State Department acknowledged some progress in Hong Kong, including improvements to victim screening, training for about 2,400 officials and funding to bring home residents trapped in Southeast Asian scam operations. It also noted an anti-trafficking action plan budget of HK$80 million (US$10.28 million) for 2025-26. The report renewed long-standing US criticism that Hong Kong lacks a single law criminalising all forms of trafficking, relying instead on offences covering prostitution, immigration, employment and physical abuse. The government countered that more than 50 legal provisions provided safeguards comparable to dedicated trafficking laws elsewhere. It cited Court of Final Appeal rulings that it had no positive obligation to enact a specific criminal offence covering the relevant activities prohibited under Article 4 of the Hong Kong Bill of Rights. “There is simply no one-size-fits-all solution,” the spokesman said. The report also criticised the live-in requirement and the “two-week rule” governing domestic workers’ stays after employment ends, saying they increased vulnerability to abusive employers and employment agencies. It said agencies routinely charged fees above the legal cap and penalties were insufficient to deter them. Hong Kong has about 380,000 foreign domestic workers, according to the government. Defending the rules, the spokesman said abused or exploited workers could apply to change employers without first returning to their home countries. The live-in requirement supported the policy of giving local workers employment priority, he said. The government said employment agencies could charge no more than 10 per cent of a worker’s first month’s salary upon successful placement. It cited more than 1,700 inspections of agencies serving domestic workers in 2025 and the arrests of 37 employers in connection with physical or sexual abuse. The US report also said the national security law imposed by Beijing in 2020 and the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance enacted in March 2024 had left non-governmental organisations unable to engage freely with authorities, including on trafficking. The government rejected that assessment, saying both laws expressly protected human rights and targeted only organisations and individuals that endangered national security. Scam operations feature prominently in 2026 US human trafficking study Beyond Hong Kong, scam operations feature prominently in this year’s report, which describes them as a direct threat to US national security and says Chinese nationals mostly run the criminal organisations behind them in Southeast Asia. Macau remained on Tier 3. The report said the casino hub had not reported a trafficking conviction since 2019 and again declined to provide information to US officials. A Tier 3 designation can lead to restrictions on certain US help and US opposition to some multilateral financing. Such measures are subject to presidential determinations and can be waived on national interest grounds.

title: Pentagon unveils US$350 million quantum computing push as China rivalry grows
description: New initiative aims to strengthen US military capabilities as Washington and Beijing compete for leadership in advanced technology.
content: The Pentagon announced on Thursday a new multimillion-dollar initiative for “maintaining American leadership” in quantum computing capabilities amid accelerating competition between the US and China over the military application of advanced technology. In a press release, the Office of the Under Secretary of Defence for Research and Engineering, which serves as the US Department of Defence’s chief technology adviser, announced that the new initiative, worth around US$350 million, is aimed at strengthening US leadership in quantum computing capabilities to “support national security”. Quantum computing dominance is a “critical priority” for the Trump administration, said Emil Michael, undersecretary of defence for research and engineering, citing a June executive order to accelerate the technology’s deployment, commercialisation and domestic manufacturing across the US. “Maintaining American leadership in this field is essential to preserving our technological edge,” he said. The new initiative underscores the race between the US and China to develop advanced technologies and explore their potential military applications, with both countries investing heavily in quantum computing. Quantum computing is a rapidly evolving field of technology that uses the principles of quantum mechanics to solve complex problems much faster than traditional computers. It not only provides the military with enhanced capabilities for strategic advantage by accelerating data processing, cracking classical encryption, and optimising complex multi-domain operations and logistics supply chains, but also enables it to tackle currently intractable problems in disciplines such as chemistry, materials, physics and applied mathematics that are crucial to the development of advanced weapons systems. The Pentagon is expected to apply the newly developed quantum computers under the new initiative to enable the development of next-generation weapons, platforms and other critical capabilities that could be “more lethal, cost-effective, and manufacturable”, the press release said. After China established a US$10 billion National Laboratory for Quantum Information Sciences in 2017, the People’s Liberation Army is reportedly “under development” of more than 10 experimental quantum cyber warfare tools, according to the Chinese Ministry of Science and Technology’s official newspaper, Science and Technology Daily, in January. Under China’s 15th five-year plan between 2026 and 2030, unveiled in March, strengthening research and application of quantum technology and quantum computing has been designated as core strategic priorities. In response, the US has also been pushing for increased investment in quantum computing, with US House lawmakers from both parties reportedly seeking to debate defence funding legislation that would increase annual military spending on quantum development and application by 68 per cent to US$567 million, according to a Bloomberg report in August. Last month, the US Department of Energy launched the Quantum Genesis Q Competition, offering up to US$215 million in funding for private sector companies to build and demonstrate the world’s first fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of solving complex scientific problems while continuously detecting and correcting internal errors as calculations take place. In a separate press release on Thursday, the Pentagon said that its Office of Strategic Capital has signed a US$150 million conditional loan commitment to PsiQuantum Corp to enhance the company’s advanced manufacturing and prototyping capabilities in the US, following the company’s US$125 million expanded agreement with DARPA in July under the Quantum Benchmarking Initiative. First announced in 2024, DARPA’s Quantum Benchmarking Initiative is a multistage programme aiming to rigorously verify and validate whether a utility-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer can be successfully constructed and operated by 2033. On Wednesday, DARPA selected a new cohort of companies to advance to Stage C of the programme, worth up to US$300 million, including Atom Computing, Diraq, IBM, IonQ, Microsoft and PsiQuantum, for direct physical testing and empirical validation.

title: Christa Pike walks and eats after surviving failed Tennessee execution
description: The death row inmate survived an attempted execution by lethal injection on September 30.
content: Christa Pike has begun walking and eating again at a hospital a week after surviving Tennessee’s attempt to execute her with lethal drugs, her lawyers said Thursday. Pike, 50, survived two doses of pentobarbital as the state sought to giver her a lethal injection eight days ago for the 1995 beating and stabbing death of classmate Colleen Slemmer. The drug didn’t kill her, and her arms were left burned and blistered, according to her lawyers. For the first few days of her hospitalisation, Pike was unconscious and on a ventilator. Her first steps on Wednesday were “limited” and she required some assistance as she walked on Thursday, her lawyers said in a statement. She is also regaining mobility in her arms, and she was able to eat for the first time. But the lawyers warned uncertainty remains about her physical recovery and her legal standing after the attempt to carry out her death sentence. The failed execution on September 30 has renewed scrutiny of how states carry out the death penalty. “While her physical recovery has been remarkable, significant questions remain about the long-term effects of what she endured,” her lawyers said in Thursday’s statement. “Christa is dealing with the profound psychological trauma of having survived a failed execution, including the terror, pain and uncertainty of believing she was about to die.” Pike regained consciousness Tuesday and was able to speak after awakening, they said. They initially described her as “confused” soon after regaining consciousness, and said Thursday that she continued to struggle with concentration and memory. Doctors say it is too early to assess the long-term impacts, the attorneys added. It also remains unclear whether Tennessee will try to execute her again. Her lawyers have said that they will urge Republican Governor Bill Lee to commute her death sentence to life in prison without parole. “She should never be subjected to another execution attempt,” they said in the statement. Lee has since postponed the state’s only other scheduled execution this year and ordered a review of why the execution failed. The state’s prison chief resigned after the execution attempt. Medical and lethal injection experts have focused on whether a problem with the IV line caused the drug to pool in her tissue instead of entering her bloodstream. Pike’s lawyers wrote in a court filing that “apparently at no point did any member of the execution team realise that the IV lines were not correctly placed”. State officials have offered no explanation of what occurred. As the process got under way Pike was asked if she had a final statement and she spoke of being at peace. About five minutes later, she raised her head and said her arm hurt. Later, she appeared to lose consciousness but could be heard breathing heavily until media witnesses were escorted from the witness room nearly 90 minutes into the execution. An ambulance took her to a hospital. Excluding Pike’s case, there have been 30 executions in the United States this year, all by lethal injection. The most recent was that of Jamaal Howard, who was put to death in Texas on Wednesday for killing a shop assistant during a 2000 robbery. The death penalty has been abolished in 23 of the 50 US states, while three others – California, Oregon and Pennsylvania – have moratoriums in place. The Pentagon said this week that US President Donald Trump has approved the execution of Nidal Hasan, a former US Army psychiatrist who shot dead 13 people and wounded more than two dozen at Fort Hood in Texas in 2009. Hasan’s execution by firing squad, set for December 3, would be the first carried out by the US military since 1961. Additional reporting by Agence France-Presse

title: Opinion | National security must not kill Philippines-China academic ties
description: Targeting educational exchanges in the name of security threatens an effective channel for Manila to understand and engage Beijing.
content: Educational and cultural exchanges have become a new casualty of rising tensions between the Philippines and China. About 150 Chinese teachers have left the Philippines months after Defence Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jnr renewed warnings that such people-to-people ties could pose security concerns. Families of volunteer instructors have expressed safety concerns. Beyond disrupting classes and potentially harming tourism in the Philippines, this could further narrow interaction between the two sides, creating more conditions for misunderstanding. At a time when official relations are fraying, putting academic exchanges under increased scrutiny could close one of the few channels to bridge the growing rift between the two neighbours. The departure of Chinese teachers is the latest in a string of setbacks in bilateral ties. In May, authorities raided a steel plant in Misamis Oriental, Mindanao and arrested 70 Chinese citizens who were accused of being undocumented workers. All 70 were later released after the Department of Justice ruled there was insufficient evidence to prove allegations of having violated local regulations. Beijing sanctioned Teodoro and his family the next month. In July, Chinese and Philippine vessels clashed at the Second Thomas Shoal as Manila hosted the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) foreign ministers’ meeting. In August, more than 100 Filipinos were arrested in China and accused of violating immigration laws. Manila said a Chinese coastguard vessel rammed a Philippine government ship off the coast of Palawan province last month. Earlier this month, the Philippine coastguard sent one of its largest vessels and an aircraft to drive the Chinese research ship Jia Hai Ke 7 from waters around the Batanes Islands. Despite Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jnr’s calling for a reset of ties with China in March and reiterating that call in July, steadying relations between Manila and Beijing remains elusive. Chinese visitors to the Philippines have yet to return to their pre-pandemic high of 1.74 million in 2019, managing just over 262,000 arrivals last year. Vietnam, Malaysia and Indonesia also have territorial disputes with China in the South China Sea, yet they all welcomed far more Chinese tourists last year. Rougher political weather makes a huge difference. Even Cambodia and Laos received more Chinese visitors. A similar picture emerges in investment. Chinese foreign direct investment in the Philippines reached US$164.7 million last year. In comparison, Indonesia received US$4.59 billion in Chinese investment while Vietnam saw US$3.92 billion. Political risk and souring ties are complicating fulfilment of investment pledges. The diplomatic chill has also manifested in attendance at regional trade fairs. In 2022, Marcos gave a pre-recorded video message at the 19th China-Asean Expo, held annually in Nanning, the capital of southern Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region. In last month’s edition, the Philippines was represented only by Trade and Industry Secretary Cristina Roque despite being Asean chair and this year’s “country of honour”. Securitisation is eroding the economic ballast of bilateral relations and is now threatening even people-to-people linkages. Educational ties becoming subject to national security considerations could deprive Manila of the language proficiency that can provide a foundation for an adept and nuanced policy towards Beijing. It runs counter to the promotion of Chinese language in educational settings elsewhere in Southeast Asia. Thailand has five times as many Confucius Institute locations as the Philippines. Indonesia has twice as many. The number of volunteer Chinese teachers in Thailand rose from 23 in 2003 to more than 17,000 in 2019. Instead of sending a chilling effect to scholars engaging in China studies, Manila should encourage academic dialogue to gain a range of views about its largest trade partner and the rising global power next door. Multilingual graduates of Chinese-Filipino schools with links to Chinese peers have contributed to Philippine governance, business, professions and public life. They are anchors and sources of inspiration. Deep knowledge of Chinese language and culture has helped Filipino companies succeed in the world’s most competitive market. Examples of these successes include Liwayway Marketing Corporation – the maker of popular snack brand Oishi – property developer SM Group and the Jollibee restaurant group. Deep knowledge of China helped make Chito Santa Romana and Jaime FlorCruz top-notch journalists who reported on China for US news agencies. They would later serve as Manila’s top envoys to Beijing, providing unmatched insights. Developing China expertise is essential for the Philippines. From industry and technology to defence and foreign affairs, China looms large. A policy based on fear, misconception or reliance on third-party sources should give way to one grounded in intimate knowledge and constant, multifaceted engagement.

title: US hits Venezuela’s Maduro and wife with torture charges
description: Superseding indictment accuses ousted president and wife of conspiring to abuse political rivals and Americans in custody.
content: US prosecutors on Thursday charged ousted Venezuelan president Nicolas Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores with conspiring to torture political opponents and American citizens, adding to the drug trafficking case the couple already faced. Separately, US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein, who is overseeing the case, denied a request by Flores to be released from jail due to health concerns ahead of a trial scheduled for next year. Maduro, 63, and Flores, 69, were captured on January 3 in their Caracas home during a US military operation ordered by President Donald Trump, and were ‌flown to New York to face drug charges against them that were announced that same day. A superseding indictment filed in Manhattan federal court on Thursday added the torture count to the existing criminal case. Maduro and Flores each would face a mandatory minimum 50 years in prison if convicted of all the charges. They have pleaded not guilty to the original charges, but have not yet entered pleas to the new indictment, which detailed alleged torture against nine people, including three US citizens. In a statement, Maduro’s lawyer Barry Pollack said: “President Maduro denies the charges in the new indictment and looks forward to his day in court”. Flores’ lawyers Mark Donnelly and Andres Sanchez in a statement said their client denies the allegations. They questioned why prosecutors only revealed the indictment, which court records showed ⁠was returned under seal by a grand jury on Tuesday, shortly before Thursday’s hearing. “We look forward to fully responding to the allegations in court at the appropriate time,” Donnelly and Sanchez said. Since Maduro’s capture, Venezuela has ‌boosted cooperation with the US under the leadership of his former vice-president Delcy Rodriguez. Relations between the United States and oil-rich Venezuela were tense during the socialist Maduro’s 13 years in power. US officials and human rights groups have long accused Venezuelan officials of torturing detainees, but Thursday’s indictment marked the first time Maduro faced criminal charges over ‌the allegations. The indictment alleged that thousands of Venezuelans were threatened, arrested, tortured or killed at the hands of the state between 1999 and 2025. Before Maduro became president in 2013, both ⁠he and Flores held positions in the late ⁠Venezuelan President Hugo Chavez’s government. “Maduro, Flores and other high-ranking members of their inner circle used a violent system of torture and repression to maintain their power,” Jamie McDonald, the top federal prosecutor in Manhattan, told reporters outside the courthouse after Flores’ bail was denied. Flores ‌was Venezuela’s attorney general and led its National Assembly before becoming first lady. Many of the incidents of alleged torture described in the indictment occurred during times of political unrest in Venezuela or in response to perceived threats against Maduro. In one instance, prosecutors said, Maduro in 2013 ‌ordered the arrest ‌of a Venezuelan military officer he suspected of planning a coup. Members of Venezuela’s military counter-intelligence directorate then interrogated the officer while shocking the individual with a live electric wire around 20 times and hung the individual ‌by the hands and feet for several minutes at a time, prosecutors said. In 2022, an American citizen detained while entering Venezuela was accused of conspiring to assassinate Maduro and was tortured by military counter-intelligence officers through beatings ⁠and shocks to the person’s arms, legs and genitals, according to the indictment. Flores’ lawyers had argued their client should be released on bail because she needs a cardiac procedure and wants to recover in ⁠a more comfortable environment. The lawyers proposed moving her to a residence in the New York City area with round-the-clock private security, and said she is not a danger to the community. In denying the motion for bail, Hellerstein decided the evidence against Flores appeared strong. The judge also said Flores, who wore a dark prison T-shirt and a headset to listen to a simultaneous ‌Spanish translation of the proceedings, appeared to be relatively healthy. “For ‌whatever it’s worth, her appearance today is no worse and perhaps a little better than when I first met with her on her arraignment,” Hellerstein said, referring to her first appearance in court on January 5. “She was still bandaged up from the military invasion,” Donnelly said. Prosecutors in the Manhattan US Attorney’s Office opposed Flores’ release. They said Flores has received adequate medical care at the detention centre, and if released poses an “extreme” risk of flight and danger to the public, including possible witness intimidation. Hellerstein’s bail denial will not affect Flores’ trial or potential punishment. Maduro and Flores have been held at Brooklyn’s Metropolitan Detention Centre since their capture. Their trial is scheduled for June 1, 2027.

title: USS Abraham Lincoln returns to US after 265 days at sea in Iran war mission
description: Return to San Diego follows a historic deployment marked by reported suicide attempts and food shortages.
content: Thousands of emotional reunions unfolded Thursday as the USS Abraham Lincoln, whose lengthy deployment in the Gulf supporting President Donald Trump’s war on Iran sparked fears for its crew’s welfare, arrived back in its home port. Families of servicemen and women had lined the quayside in San Diego, California, for hours, waiting to welcome loved ones they have not seen for almost a year. There were tears of joy as more than 100 new dads met their babies for the first time, or fathers were reunited with children who are so much taller than last time they were together. The nuclear-powered aircraft carrier left California in November 2025 for duty in the South China Sea and was rerouted to the Middle East before US-Israeli attacks on Iran that began in late February. The vessel completed a deployment that included a record uninterrupted 265 days at sea in support of the Iran war before making a port call in Thailand in early September. The lengthy deployment took a toll on US military personnel on the Lincoln and accompanying warships. In August, military families and lawmakers sounded the alarm about issues including reported suicide attempts and food shortages aboard the carrier. Last month, the Trump administration acknowledged in a letter to a lawmaker that there had been eight suicide attempts by US service members who were part of the Lincoln carrier strike group but said none of those people died. The letter from Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao provided details on some of the suicide attempts. It said a sailor assigned to an air wing “went overboard from the ship in early August” and was quickly recovered, while another sailor “attempted to go overboard in March and was stopped by his shipmates”. The letter also said that while food supplies on the carrier were “adequate”, limited resupply options during combat led the “number of main entrée options” to be reduced from “two to one for a short time”. The arrival in port came the day after Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth boarded the Lincoln to congratulate the crew on their mission. “What the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group did, no other carrier strike group has ever done,” Hegseth told sailors. The Lincoln, which set a record for days between ports of call, is the second carrier to endure an unusually long deployment during the Iran war and to receive the Presidential Unit Citation afterwards, typically reserved for significant achievement in combat. According to the citation that Hegseth read to the crew, the Lincoln and its strike group executed nearly 3,700 combat missions, launched 450 Tomahawk cruise missiles, shot down 77 one-way attack drones, sank 64 Iranian warships, and destroyed 21 anti-ship cruise missiles. The crew of the USS Gerald R. Ford returned in May from a 326-day deployment – the longest for an aircraft carrier in the past 50 years and a record in the post-Vietnam war era. The deployment didn’t include as many uninterrupted days at sea as the Lincoln. Another carrier, the usually Asia-based USS George Washington, relieved the Lincoln in the Middle East in August. Additional reporting by Associated Press

title: US probes Harvard, Yale, MIT, other universities over alleged visa fraud, with China focus
description: Stanford and Brown are among schools facing scrutiny over alleged visa abuse and Chinese influence on federally funded research.
content: The Trump administration is launching an investigation into nine US universities over alleged J-1 visa fraud, with officials raising concerns about Chinese scholars and the Chinese government. The J-1 programme covers exchange visitors including international researchers, scholars and students, who may receive temporary authorisation to work or conduct research in the US. At a Thursday press conference, Anthony D’Esposito, inspector general of the US Department of Labor, announced what he called a “historic investigation” into J-1 visa fraud at Harvard, Yale, Stanford, Brown, the University of Pittsburgh, UC Davis, Caltech, Arizona State University and MIT. Subpoenas have been issued to the universities, officials said. Standing alongside Vice-President J.D. Vance and other White House officials, D’Esposito singled out China, warning that the Chinese government need not break into US research labs if institutions leave their doors open. “China is not simply an economic competitor,” D’Esposito said. “The Chinese Communist Party is a sophisticated adversary actively targeting American technology, intellectual property and national security interests.” The Chinese embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It remains unclear how many Chinese scholars could be affected by the investigation. D’Esposito said about 61 per cent of postdoctoral researchers and federally funded workers at the nine universities are foreign nationals, compared with a national average of 38 per cent. Officials said the investigation will examine whether foreign influence, improper financial ties or visa abuse are compromising federally funded research at the universities. “So something weird is going on at these universities,” Vance said, arguing that the schools were using foreign workers to “undercut the wages of American grad students and American researchers”. The South China Morning Post contacted all nine universities for comment and figures on their Chinese J-1 scholars. By Friday noon, six had responded. Arizona State, Brown, MIT, Yale, the University of Pittsburgh and UC Davis all stressed compliance with US law or said they would review the investigation. ASU defended its hiring practices, and MIT said its J-1 visa holders had been vetted and authorised by the government. Pittsburgh confirmed receiving a subpoena, as did Brown. “Brown’s international scholars, students and employees make essential contributions to our campus,” Brian Clark, the university’s vice-president for news and strategic campus communications, said in a statement. “We have received a subpoena from the government for various records pertaining to foreign labour programmes administered by the US government, and we will respond promptly and directly to the government.” None provided figures for Chinese J-1 scholars. The investigation comes as the administration has broadened its scrutiny of programmes that allow foreign nationals to study and work in the United States. It has also proposed charging universities US$70,000 for each international student taking part in the Optional Practical Training programme, which allows foreign students to work in jobs related to their studies. At the same press conference, officials also announced the suspension of several major technology companies, including Microsoft and Adobe, from participating in the PERM labour certification process, a key step in securing employment-based permanent residency for foreign workers. The administration alleged abuse and fraud in the system. “Our message to Microsoft is: You’re a great American company, but you’ve got to hire great American workers,” Vance said at the event.

title: Suspect arrested in Germany after 2 officials killed in routine firearms check
description: Bavarian police breach home with explosives after 60-year-old gunman barricades himself for hours.
content: Police have arrested a 60-year-old man suspected of shooting dead two local government employees during a routine firearms inspection in the southern German state of Bavaria, police said early on Friday. The suspect was slightly wounded by gunfire during his arrest, a police spokeswoman said. Police have not yet established a motive for the killings. According to initial findings, the man allegedly shot dead a 54-year-old woman and a 45-year-old man, both employees of the Neumarkt district administration, during the inspection in the town of Berngau on Thursday afternoon. He then barricaded himself inside a residential building for hours. The officials were checking, among other things, whether the man was storing his firearms in accordance with regulations. The inspection was not intended to seize the man’s weapons. Police surrounded the building and called in specialist units. The operation continued for hours, while residents were urged to remain indoors or stay away from the cordon. During the stand-off, officers maintained telephone contact with the suspected shooter and spent a long time trying to persuade him to surrender. However, the man insisted he would not give himself up without resistance. “Ultimately, officers moved in, also using explosives,” a police spokesman said. “The 60-year-old suspect was slightly wounded by gunfire to the leg.” The man was to receive medical treatment first. On Thursday evening, police initially reported that one employee of the Neumarkt district administration had been fatally wounded. A police spokesman later confirmed that a female colleague, who had initially been reported as seriously injured, had also died. “We assume she died immediately when the shots were fired,” the spokesman said, citing the circumstances in which her body was found. Several emergency calls reporting gunfire were received by police and rescue services at around 2pm. The other deceased government employee was recovered from outside the building, police said.

title: UK navy sailor charged with spying for Russia
description: Teddy Young, 24, is accused of obtaining secret information with a view to giving it to a foreign power.
content: A UK Royal Navy sailor appeared in a London court on Thursday to face charges of spying for Russia. Teddy Young, 24, has been charged with two offences under the National Security Act, including preparing to disclose protected information between November 2024 and May 2025, London’s Metropolitan Police Service said. During the same period, Young allegedly obtained, copied, recorded or retained protected information for the benefit of a foreign power. Young has been in police custody since he was arrested on Tuesday at his home in the village of Clapham, about 80km (50 miles) north of London. He appeared at Westminster Magistrates’ Court in central London on Thursday. “The allegation is that while serving as a Royal Navy warfare intelligence rating with high level security clearance and intelligence-system access, Teddy Stanley Greenidge Young accessed and retained sensitive UK defence and intelligence material and engaged in activity consistent with preparing to pass protected information to a foreign power,” the Crown Prosecution Service said in a written summary of the allegations. Young allegedly used the dark web to try to contact Russian authorities, drafting a message that “sought to make contact with a potential threat actor”. Young, who joined the Navy in April 2024, is accused of committing the offences during his first deployment, which began on November 4, 2024. He was not asked to enter a plea during the four-minute hearing on Thursday because the charges are too serious to be considered at a magistrates’ court. Judge Annabel Pilling ordered Young to remain in custody until his next court appearance on October 16 at the Central Criminal Court in London. Police said the charges were not related to the recent security alert at RAF Fairford, a British airbase from which US bombers have launched strikes against Iran. Three suspicious vans were discovered near the base in the early morning hours of September 27, triggering an investigation that has led to the arrest of seven men. Young was previously arrested on May 21, 2025, and released on bail pending further investigation. His security clearance was suspended at that time and he was removed from his duties. The Royal Navy issued a statement acknowledging the arrest of a service member but said: “As legal proceedings are ongoing, it would be inappropriate to comment further at this stage.”

title: China’s BYD considering lithium battery plant in Argentina, foreign minister says
description: Pablo Quirno spoke after meeting BYD’s executive vice-president Stella Li, as EV car maker seeks investment opportunities in Argentina.
content: BYD is studying whether to manufacture lithium batteries in Argentina, Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno said on Thursday after meeting Stella Li, the Chinese electric vehicle maker’s executive vice-president. According to Quirno, the company was looking at “investment opportunities in Argentina linked to the lithium value chain, particularly in the production of batteries and energy storage systems”. He did not say how much BYD might spend or where the factory could go. The minister tied the talks to Argentinian President Javier Milei’s economic agenda, saying Argentina was positioning itself “as a platform for projects aimed at both the domestic market and exports”. Quirno credited the government’s policies with promoting investment and mining in the country. BYD has sold only imported cars in Argentina since it opened for business in October last year, and it has not announced production plans in the country. It sold 10,000 vehicles in August, including a Dolphin Mini in Rosario, and now has 21 dealerships, most of them in Buenos Aires. The company’s local subsidiary, BYD Auto Argentina SAU, registered with the Justice Ministry in August last year with a corporate purpose that already included making vehicles, batteries and auto parts, the South China Morning Post reported at the time. Christian Kimelman, who runs the Argentine operation, said a car factory was not on the table for now. “It is not in the plans, but anyone who knows the Argentine industry knows that, to lead the sector in the current context, you need to have some kind of vision in that direction,” he told Bloomberg Linea earlier this year. Kimelman said most of BYD’s supply for Argentina and Mexico would come from its factory in Camacari, in the Brazilian state of Bahia. The plant opened in October last year with capacity for 150,000 vehicles a year, and in March Li said it had orders for 50,000 cars from each country. Cars made in Brazil can enter Argentina largely duty-free under the automotive agreement between the two Mercosur members. Vehicles from outside the bloc pay a 35 per cent tariff, except for a quota of 50,000 units that Chinese brands have dominated. BYD has also kept shipping cars from China on its own vessels, and in January the BYD Changzhou unloaded more than 5,000 vehicles at the port of Zarate. The company registered 9,266 cars in Argentina in the first half of the year, according to the importers’ chamber. A lithium venture in Argentina would follow BYD’s failed attempt in Chile, where it had planned a US$290 million cathode plant in Antofagasta. The factory was meant to make 50,000 tonnes a year of lithium iron phosphate cathode material, using lithium from SQM at a preferential price. But BYD and Tsingshan, the other Chinese company Chile’s development agency, Corfo, picked for the scheme, both pulled out in May last year. At that time, Corfo blamed the collapse in lithium prices.

title: Trump says US will not attack Iran before November midterms
description: US president cites ‘productive discussions’ with Tehran despite rising Hormuz tensions and military build-up.
content: US President Donald Trump said in a social media post that the US would “not be attacking Iran” before November’s midterm elections, citing what he said were “productive discussions” with the Islamic Republic. The president’s comments on Thursday amounted to an unusual blending of national security issues and domestic politics. His decision to lay off on new strikes comes despite Iran escalating attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Tehran-backed militants in Yemen attacking energy facilities in Saudi Arabia and the president’s decision to move US bombers from a base in the UK because of possible Iran-linked threats. The remarks follow recent reporting in the Atlantic that Trump was mulling plans to strike Iran before the midterm contests and that the White House had asked the Pentagon to prepare options. The New York Times separately reported Thursday that senior White House national security officials recently discussed plans that included an intense three-day campaign. Trump said in an interview with Time Magazine published earlier this month that ramped-up military strikes against Iran were “possible” following the elections. Late last month, the Pentagon deployed an additional aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf, a US official previously told Bloomberg. That move bolsters the two aircraft carriers already in the region and gives American commanders more options if Trump chooses to launch new attacks on Iran, the official said. Trump has suggested Iran was waiting to see how his Republican Party would do during the midterms. In September, he explicitly dismissed the relevance of the vote when it came to the Iran war. “I gave absolutely no credence and will not give credence to the election when it comes to Iran,” Trump said. “It doesn’t even enter my mind.” In his Thursday post, the president did not offer any details about the discussions he said were happening with Iran. Talks have remained deadlocked over a host of issues including control of the vital Strait of Hormuz. The president rejected an Iranian offer after holding discussions via mediators during United Nations meetings in September. Iran’s state media reported on Thursday that Tehran would not abandon uranium enrichment or hand over its uranium stockpile, citing the head of the country’s Atomic Energy Organization, days after US Vice-President J.D.
