Registration for the public ballot to enter the marathon, half marathon, 10km, 5km harbourfront run or youth run will open on www.hkmarathon.com from 2pm on September 11, before closing at 7pm on September 20.

title: ‘Breakthrough’: Chinese shipyard set to take lucrative orders from Nordic cruise operator
description: Chinese shipyard Waigaoqiao signs MOU with Nordic cruise operator, marking another advance for the rising shipbuilding powerhouse, analysts say.
content: Shanghai Waigaoqiao, a subsidiary of China State Shipbuilding Corporation (CSSC), has secured potential orders from a Nordic cruise operator, marking the entry of Chinese shipyards into the lucrative cruise ship construction sector amid the dominance of European firms. The memorandum of understanding (MOU) was signed by Shanghai Waigaoqiao and Nor Cruises from Norway on Wednesday at SMM Hamburg, a trade fair on shipbuilding, machinery and marine technology in Germany. The deal involved two 84,000-tonne midsized cruise vessels with an option for three more, according to Waigaoqiao. The MOU would pave the way for the first batch of such foreign contracts for Waigaoqiao, and, broadly, for China’s shipbuilding industry, as it attempts to scale the value chain and enter the technology and capital-intensive cruise ship market. While Chinese shipyards have dominated global cargo and container ship segments, with strong order books for LNG vessels, they have not yet broken into cruise ship building, a market cornered by European firms. Against this backdrop, the MOU carried significance, said one expert. “Though an MOU is not automatically an order or construction contract, it still represents a breakthrough: foreign cruise ship operators are starting to look at China … to seriously engage with builders there,” said Zeng Ji, a professor of ocean science and engineering at Shanghai Maritime University. “The MOU’s execution into a formal order will help Chinese shipbuilders prove and showcase their capabilities to undertake high-end foreign cruise ship projects and compete for more business. In that case, they may break the long-held monopoly by German and Italian shipyards,” he argued. Zeng also revealed that other foreign clients, including Singapore’s Resorts World Cruises, are also in contact with CSSC. The MOU between Waigaoqiao and Nor Cruises, though, stipulated that both ships to be built in China would adopt designs from Italian industrial giant Fincantieri, a global leader in the construction of large cruise vessels. CSSC’s partnership with Fincantieri dates back to 2016, when a joint venture was set up in Hong Kong for the introduction and transfer of advanced, luxury cruise ship design and construction technologies. This occurred as the state-owned shipbuilder embarked on a years-long programme to design, construct and launch China’s first domestically built cruise ship, which culminated in the January 2024 maiden voyage of the 135,500-tonne Adora Magic City. The second vessel created under the programme, the 142,000-tonne Adora Flora City, is scheduled for delivery on November 6. About a third of the equipment on the new ship was sourced domestically, Waigaoqiao said, adding that it nears the scale of the 170,000-tonne Spectrum of the Seas, the largest cruise vessel in Asia built by Meyer Werft in Germany, which regularly docks at Shanghai. CSSC is also pressing ahead with its push to design its own cruise ships, with a separate MOU with China Tourism Group signed in March for two ships. Its efforts to break into the cruise ship segment come as the global market experiences a new expansion cycle. According to data from Clarksons, new orders for cruise ships reached a record high of 35 vessels last year, totalling 4.31 million gross tonnes. European players have extended their delivery schedules to the mid-2030s amid strained capacity.

title: As I see it | The US’ dangerous reversion to imperialism in Latin America
description: Washington aims not only to counter growing Chinese influence but to reestablish hegemonic control in the region.
content: When China’s trade with Latin America reached a record US$518.4 billion in 2024, it marked a fundamental shift in hemispheric economics. Beijing is now the largest bilateral creditor and second largest trading partner of Latin America and the Caribbean, with President Xi Jinping pledging a new credit line of 66 billion yuan (US$9.2 billion) at the 2025 China-Celac (Community of Latin American and Caribbean States) forum. Chinese investment has evolved from extractive industries towards clean energy and manufacturing, with electric vehicle production expanding across Brazil and Chinese-made vehicles capturing 57 per cent of Ecuador’s market by the first half of this year. Washington’s response under President Donald Trump has not been subtle. Rather than competing economically, the administration has reverted to traditional gunboat diplomacy under the so-called Donroe Doctrine. Washington has been employing outright imperialist methods that undermine international law and the sovereign interests of America’s neighbours in the region. The January military raid on Caracas that captured Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro exemplifies this approach. Operation Absolute Resolve killed about 80 people, including 32 Cuban security personnel, with no American casualties. Maduro is being put on a show trial in New York while the US has secured effective control over 65 billion barrels of Venezuelan oil reserves through a deal granting Washington 55 per cent of output from 17 oilfields over 100 years. Acting President Delcy Rodríguez, who once denounced foreign colonialism, signed legislation privatising the energy sector – reversing two decades of socialist policy – under evident American pressure. Washington doesn’t even bother to hide the true intention behind the violent regime change. The Pentagon is expected to take a direct stake in the parent of North American Blue Energy Partners, the private oil producer hand-picked by Washington for the deal. When devastating earthquakes struck Venezuela in June, killing at least 6,500 people, the Trump administration’s humanitarian response was summed up thus by a New York Times headline: “With $8 Billion in Venezuelan Oil Money, US Gives $300 Million in Quake Aid”. Cuba’s suffering is even starker, thanks to America’s coercive statecraft over 66 years and counting. Trump has escalated a fuel blockade and threatened to punish any nation trying to sell oil to the island state. That has produced catastrophic humanitarian consequences. The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights reported in June that Cuba’s infant mortality has doubled to 9.9 per 1,000 births, while childhood cancer survival rates have fallen from 85 to 65 per cent. Fuel supplies are down 60 per cent, prompting basic food costs to rise sharply. Essential medicines are down to 30 per cent of normal supply levels, and power cuts regularly exceeding 20 hours daily have crippled hospitals, water systems and food refrigeration. Volker Türk, the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, stated bluntly: “Children are dying because doctors lack access to essential medical supplies and medicines.” Trump’s Shield of the Americas, unveiled at a March summit in Florida, purports to counter drug cartels and Chinese influence through military cooperation among 17 nations. The initiative appears less a hemispheric alliance than an ideological coalition of right-wing governments, evoking uncomfortable parallels to Operation Condor, the 1970s network of military dictatorships that engaged in systematic repression with American support. Beijing’s loans, infrastructure projects and technology transfer do raise legitimate questions … But the appropriate response is not military intervention, resource extraction disguised as partnership, or sanction regimes that kill children The Pentagon’s maritime strike campaign reinforces these concerns. Since September 2025, US forces have struck at least 67 vessels in alleged counter-narcotics operations, killing at least 223 people, in the Caribbean and east Pacific. The Pentagon has refused to release identities or provide evidence of drug trafficking. Extrajudicial killings or just plain murders? China’s deepening economic engagement in Latin America inevitably invites scrutiny and competitive response. Beijing’s loans, infrastructure projects and technology transfer do raise legitimate questions about debt sustainability, environmental standards and political influence. But the appropriate response is not military intervention, resource extraction disguised as partnership, or sanction regimes that kill children. Regional governments are caught in the middle. Recent US presidents have warned Latin American leaders about ties to Beijing. While they offered few concrete alternatives to Chinese trade and investment, Trump has escalated from political pressure to outright military operations, thus doing away with sustained economic engagement, good-neighbour diplomacy and respect for sovereignty. Trump’s approach violates international law, alienates partners and strengthens rather than weakens China’s position by default. Washington is resorting to tariffs, deportations and militarisation; Beijing is offering trade and investment. For a region seeking development pathways beyond commodity extraction, the choice grows clearer with each military strike and each Cuban blackout. The Donroe Doctrine is becoming catastrophic for the region and the world at large.

title: Hong Kong’s Silver Bonds draw record 480,000 bids with higher interest rate
description: Hong Kong is expected to raise the final issuance to the upper limit of HK$55 billion, as applications from elderly investors have surged.
content: The latest round of the Hong Kong government’s Silver Bonds programme has attracted a record number of subscriptions in terms of both quantity and value, as the city’s elderly investors seize the opportunity to secure better returns than those offered by bank deposits. Investors submitted 478,000 bids for HK$119.8 billion (US$15.28 billion) worth of bonds during the offering period, which ended at 2pm on Friday, according to a government spokesman. That represented a 22 per cent rise in terms of value and a 28 per cent jump by number of applicants compared with last year’s offering, which drew 371,821 applications for HK$98.23 billion of Silver Bonds – itself a record high at the time. In light of the strong demand, the government is expected to raise the final issuance to the upper limit of HK$55 billion, from the original HK$50 billion, according to the spokesman. The Hong Kong Monetary Authority will announce the final allotment results on September 11, with the bonds set to be issued on September 15. The government increased the guaranteed coupon rate for its 11th batch of Silver Bonds to 4.25 per cent, up from 3.85 per cent last year and from 4 per cent in 2024. The increase came ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s next rate decision at the coming Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) on September 17. About 60 per cent of traders expected the Fed to implement a 0.25 percentage point rate increase as of Thursday, while 40 per cent expected no rate change, according to data from CME FedWatch, which is based on Fed funds futures contracts. Any rate increase in the United States will trigger a matching rise in Hong Kong, as the city institutes a policy of following US interest rates due to the local currency being pegged to the US dollar. The Hong Kong government will pay Silver Bond holders either the guaranteed minimum fixed interest rate of 4.25 per cent per annum or a floating return linked to inflation, whichever is higher. HSBC and Bank of China (Hong Kong) (BOCHK) – the two managers for the offering – alongside other banks, such as ICBC (Asia) and China Citic Bank International, have all reported robust applications from investors since the offering period began on August 21. “Amid ongoing market volatility, investors remain interested in Silver Bonds for their predictable income stream and safe-haven qualities, particularly as interest rates stay in focus,” said Winnie Ng, head of wealth and premier solutions at HSBC Hong Kong, in a statement on Friday. “Silver Bonds’ defensive return profile can help investors diversify in uncertain conditions.” HSBC saw a 23 per cent increase in subscription value and 31 per cent rise in applicant numbers from last year’s Silver Bond offering, with both totals hitting record highs. Around a quarter of applicants this year were new to Silver Bonds with HSBC, and more than half of the applications were submitted online, the bank said. At BOCHK, total upfront payments tied to the bonds were up about 20 per cent from a year ago, while the number of subscribers was up 30 per cent, according to Arnold Chow, general manager of the bank’s personal banking product department. Both numbers set all-time highs, he added. Bright Smart Securities, a major local retail broker, has also seen a rise in Silver Bond subscriptions for this year’s offering, according to co-CEO Edmond Hui Yik-bun. “The Hong Kong stock market performance has been volatile this year, while many initial public offerings in the third quarter have not performed well,” Hui said. “As such, the silver-haired investors would prefer to shift their bank deposits to Silver Bonds to get a secured return.” “Even if the US would increase the interest rate, the pace of rate increase would not be too quick, which has made the Silver Bonds offer become attractive,” he added. Additional reporting by Daniel Ren

title: AI economics: rise of machines’ token use could work to advantage of Chinese models
description: Agentic AIs now use five times as many tokens as humans, giving lower-priced models from Chinese firms a competitive edge, analysts say.
content: The global artificial intelligence boom recently crossed a landmark threshold: autonomous agents now consume more than five times as much data as human users, triggering a surge in processing costs that is giving lower-priced Chinese models a competitive edge, according to analysts. Unlike traditional chatbots that simply respond to human prompts, these agents operate independently to execute multi-step workflows, such as writing software, conducting research or managing business operations. A single assignment can trigger a cascade of automated model calls as an agent plans its task, searches databases, invokes software tools and audits its own results. This shift has dramatically altered the economics of AI deployment. Agentic requests consumed about 15 times more tokens – the basic units of data processed by an AI model – than standard human queries, according to data from model aggregator OpenRouter compiled by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz. The data showed that daily token consumption from agentic workloads on OpenRouter hit 7.3 trillion in early August – 14 times the level six months earlier. Agentic activity first surpassed human usage in February. By August, it accounted for over five times the 1.4 trillion tokens generated by human users on the platform. Token usage will continue to grow exponentially as models become more capable and penetrate more scenarios Sun Wenhao, TH Capital Much of the increase came from cached prompt tokens – repeated portions of prompts, including system instructions, conversation histories and tool definitions, that can be reused without being fully processed again. Providers generally charge less for cached input because it requires less computation, although the rapid growth in overall volume could still increase corporate AI bills. “Token usage will continue to grow exponentially as models become more capable and penetrate more scenarios,” said Sun Wenhao, a senior investment manager at Chinese deep tech venture investor TH Capital. In China, daily token calls jumped 5,000-fold to 500 trillion in June this year from around 100 billion at the start of 2024, according to official data cited by state broadcaster CCTV. To keep costs manageable, companies are increasingly turning to “model routing”, an approach where routine, repetitive tasks are directed to lower-cost models, reserving expensive, high-powered frontier models for complex reasoning, according to US enterprise software firm Salesforce. “If everything runs on premium models, it is clearly too expensive,” Sun said, adding that coding and text-based research currently dominated agent usage, mostly assisting human workers rather than fully automating jobs. Token demand could rise further once agents were trusted to carry out more tasks from beginning to end, he added. The cost sensitivity could work to the advantage of Chinese open-weight models – AI systems that are released freely over the internet, allowing users with the necessary hardware to download and customise them for their own use. For example, DeepSeek’s V4-Flash charges US$0.14 per million standard input tokens and US$0.28 per million output tokens. By comparison, OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol charges US$4 and US$20, respectively, while Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.1 costs US$10 and US$50. DeepSeek accounted for 22.7 per cent of text requests on OpenRouter as of Thursday, the largest share of any model developer, ahead of Google’s 20.4 per cent and OpenAI’s 19.6 per cent, according to the platform’s live rankings. However, cost is not the only hurdle facing widespread agent adoption. Agents could generate code, analysis and documents faster than employees could vet them, potentially shifting the operational bottleneck from AI processing speed to human oversight, according to research from the MIT Sloan School of Management published in June.

title: In Burkina Faso, Sky Dragon 30 missiles point to China’s military export inroads
description: Chinese weapons are gaining favour as the West African country cuts ties with Western suppliers, analyst says.
content: The West African country of Burkina Faso has tested what observers say is a Chinese Sky Dragon 30 surface-to-air missile, in the latest sign that Chinese military equipment manufacturers are making inroads into the central Sahel state. In footage released by the Burkinabe president’s office on Tuesday, multiple missiles were fired from a mobile launch vehicle. A matching search radar vehicle also appeared in the video. The footage is part of a documentary series marking the fourth anniversary in power by Burkina Faso’s military leader, Ibrahim Traoré. It did not say when the tests were carried out but this is the first time the landlocked country has shown the short-to-medium range missile system. Song Zhongping, a Chinese military commentator and former People’s Liberation Army instructor, said that in the past countries such as Burkina Faso had relied heavily on France and the United States. “However, they now want to break free from this dependence on Western powers, adopting an independent foreign policy while choosing self-armament,” Song said. “By buying arms from Russia and China, they aim to build their own autonomous defence systems.” Song, who identified the missiles in the footage as the Sky Dragon 30 (SD-30) developed by China North Industries Group Corporation (Norinco), said Burkina Faso was buying the weapons for counterterrorism and decolonisation. First shown at the Zhuhai air show in 2018, the SD-30 has a range of 30km (18.6 miles) and is based on the PLA’s PL-10 missile. Its multi-stage guidance architecture – combining mid-course command updates with terminal infrared imaging – extends the engagement range, enables simultaneous multi-target engagement, and provides strong resistance to electronic countermeasures, according to Chinese military magazine Ordnance Industry Science Technology. It is designed for international buyers seeking low-maintenance, short-range point defence. Its launch vehicle could also launch a Sky Dragon 50 missile, which has a 50km range, state broadcaster CCTV reported in 2018. Burkina Faso, a former French colony, has undergone a dramatic political and security realignment in recent years as the military government has severed long-standing security ties with France and Western allies. Since gaining control, Traoré has strengthened relations with countries including China and Russia. China is equipping Burkina Faso’s military and positioning itself for greater influence in the Sahel. Burkina Faso bought various Chinese equipment, including armoured vehicles and artillery and rocket systems, that has been delivered in the past two years. Among the deliveries last year were VN22B fire support vehicles, PLL-05 120mm self-propelled gun-mortar systems and SR5 rocket launch systems, according to the Stockholm International Peace Research Institute. Traoré has also strengthened military ties with Russia, making two visits since becoming president in 2022. He has yet to visit China, but the then Burkinabe prime minister, Apollinaire Joachimson Kyelem de Tambela, attended the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation in Beijing in 2024. China has also stepped up ties with Burkina Faso’s neighbours, Mali and Niger, amid waning Western influence. Mali signed a defence deal with Norinco in 2024 for military equipment and training and to transfer technology. Norinco has established sales offices in at least four African countries as demand for its military equipment has increased in Africa.

title: South Korean football referee faces hearing over using ‘period’ insult on player
description: Official will face disciplinary inquiry over incident that saw the international booked after demanding a penalty during a local league game.
content: A woman referee in South Korea will face a disciplinary hearing over accusations she insulted former Chelsea midfielder Ji So-yun by saying she was menstruating, the football association said on Friday. The inquiry will focus on an incident that saw the international booked after confronting the official during a domestic women’s league game between Ji’s Suwon FC Women and Seoul City Hall. It was sparked when Ji, a midfielder who is the top scorer for the South Korea national side, demanded a penalty for her side during the WK League match last month. After approaching the referee, Ji alleged the official said: “She’s been touchy since the start, she must be on her period.” A Korea Football Association (KFA) official said it had referred the case to the association’s disciplinary committee. The KFA did not say when the hearing will take place. The KFA’s refereeing department previously said the word “period” was not used and that the remarks did not specifically refer to Ji, according to broadcaster SBS. The Korea Women’s Football Federation (KWFF) has said the term used was “girl’s day”, a euphemism referring to menstruation. Ji, 35, told local media that she heard the referee make the remark over the communication system used by officials. The KFA said their referee council “recognised the seriousness of the allegations” and decided to refer the case to its disciplinary committee.

title: How US military presence spurred Pattaya’s rise into Thailand’s city of pleasure
description: Military links have brought waves of Americans to Thailand since the 1940s, with the crew of the USS Abraham Lincoln the latest to visit.
content: The Amazon deliveries stopped reaching the USS Abraham Lincoln in February as it entered the conflict zone with Iran. A few weeks later – much to the chagrin of the sailors on board – even that most American of meals, the hamburger, was compromised by supply shortages when burger buns ran out. But as they unwind on their first shore leave in 286 days, the 5,000 crew of the Nimitz-class aircraft carrier are finding out what tens of thousands of their forebears already knew: Pattaya will provide. “I lost a lot of weight on board,” said one young sailor, who was not authorised to speak to the media. “But I’m putting it back on here. We’re just eating and drinking as much as we can.” The Lincoln, whose fighter jet squadrons have launched strikes on Iran, has spent a record time at sea, with complaints over food shortages and even the crew’s mental health reaching American media. The length of its deployment without shore leave has stirred fierce debate over the White House’s treatment of its service personnel during the war on Iran. It is a conflict, fought alongside Israel, that was meant to take a few days or weeks but is now in its seventh month as Tehran fights to a stalemate. For some of the Lincoln’s crew – certainly the younger ones – thoughts appear to have moved on from the pains of deployment to how to maximise the four days in Pattaya, Thailand’s unbridled eastern beach resort, where roads teem with raucous bars, restaurants and massage parlours. “It’s my first time in Thailand but people at base always talk about Pattaya,” another sailor said. Shopping and eating out are the order of the day for a crew with money to burn, and groups have emerged from Pattaya’s malls laden with bags. Many restaurants and resorts appear to have done a brisk trade so far from visitors expected to spend between US$100 and US$150 per person daily. A handful, however, have found the freedom a little overwhelming after nine months at sea. Two sailors were sent back to the ship late on Thursday after a drunken scuffle near Pattaya’s neon-lit Walking Street. “The sailors were drunk and they were fighting,” said city police chief Anek Srathongyoo, describing the incident as “trivial”. Thailand is America’s oldest treaty ally in Asia with a trading relationship stretching back to the early 19th century. Military links have brought waves of Americans to Thailand since the 1940s as its footprint across Asia increased. The US military dynamised Pattaya’s development from a fishing village into the anything-goes city of pleasure it is today. Thailand hosted American bases throughout the Vietnam war, building on a presence of spies and intelligence officers that was established in 1942 as World War II raged. By 1962, US troop numbers formally based in Thailand surged from 1,000 to 35,000 as bases mushroomed across the country to attack Communist forces in Vietnam and Laos. Thailand became a crucial supply route and base for rest and recuperation for young American soldiers thrown into combat against ferocious enemies in Southeast Asian jungles. But in the shadow of defeat in Vietnam, those American bases gradually coalesced resources at U-Tapao, an airfield less than an hour east of Pattaya where the heavy B2 bombers were based. U-Tapao became a mini-city to meet the needs of the surge in foreign guests. It also became a hub for Americans up to no good. Harlem drug kingpin Frank Lucas – played by Denzel Washington in American Gangster – used U-Tapao to smuggle heroin from the Golden Triangle to the streets of New York. By 1976, a humiliated US had formally withdrawn from Southeast Asia. But men and materiel remained in and around U-Tapao. And Americans meant money, said Termsak Thepsak, 79, a retired Pattaya trader. “Once all the military bases closed across Thailand, regardless of which base they had been stationed at, traders didn’t know where to go and many of them ended up at U-Tapao, which was the last camp,” said Termsak, who used to sell gold jewellery to soldiers at the airbase. “When U-Tapao eventually closed, the jewellery shops didn’t know where to go, so they moved to Pattaya.” The Indian tailors followed, as did the sex workers who had worked near the airbase. Bawdy bars opened alongside massage parlours as a large sex industry began to take root and Pattaya was retooled from a fishing town to a raucous beach resort. “That’s how it developed into the Pattaya we know today,” Termsak told This Week in Asia. Termsak was among a group of entrepreneurial friends from the south of Thailand who found a quick buck to be made from the Americans with cash to spend. Some sold tailor-made suits, others painted portraits of the soldiers for US$5 a piece. Many of his contemporaries went on to own restaurants, hotels and tourist-facing businesses that survive to this day – a testament to the business-savvy of the young Thais of that era. US servicemen dated Thai women, and romance crossed the oceans – links maintained for as long as possible by letters and cassette tape recordings in the era before modern communications. Other locals supported the shadow economy that also flourished due to the American presence. “The American servicemen had significant purchasing power,” Termsak said. “Pattaya became a hub for all kinds of illicit activity – smuggled and untaxed goods, cigarettes … and all sorts of things. Everything seemed to end up in Pattaya.” The party is due to end for the current cohort on Sunday when the Lincoln departs for home. Both countries have continued to maintain defence ties, with the annual Cobra Gold exercises – the biggest Southeast Asian war games jointly held by Thai and US militaries – marking their 45th edition in March earlier this year near Pattaya.

title: Dairy Queen to make Hong Kong comeback with 4 stores. Is it scooping up cheap rents?
description: American ice cream chain says flagship store to open in Causeway Bay in November, followed by three other outlets across city.
content: American ice cream chain Dairy Queen will open four Hong Kong outlets in the fourth quarter of this year, as part of an ambitious expansion plan amid a wave of food and retail shop closures across the city. Dairy Queen, an 85-year-old brand, said on Friday that it would launch its flagship store at One Causeway Bay shopping centre on Hong Kong Island in November, followed by three other outlets in Kowloon, the New Territories and the outlying islands before the end of the year. “Following Causeway Bay, the Kwun Tong store in Kowloon is already under hoarding,” the company said. “A total of four stores are set to open this quarter, strategically covering Hong Kong Island, Kowloon, the New Territories and the outlying islands.” The Kwun Tong store is located in The Angle shopping centre. The coming stores mark the brand’s return to Hong Kong after a short-lived opening in Causeway Bay in 1979. The company said it had a fresh store concept tailored for Hong Kong, featuring five product lines, including milkshakes, parfaits and uniquely designed ice cream cakes. It said the city’s products would include its signature soft-serve dessert, which it described as “thick enough to hold when the cup is turned upside down” and made with an exclusive full-fat dairy mix and an air overrun of about 40 per cent to maintain texture. Edwin Lee Kan-hing, founder and chief executive of Bridgeway Prime Shop Fund Management, said Dairy Queen’s entry into the market comes after a sharp fall in retail rents and shop values, creating lower entry costs for foreign brands even as legacy merchants using older business models continue to shut down. Traditional dim sum and Chinese restaurants have been closing across the city, with the Star Seafood Restaurant Group closing numerous branches in 2025 and this year, and the 35-year-old Metropol Restaurant in Admiralty shutting in September last year. “Out with the old and in with the new,” Lee said, pointing out that commercial rents in core districts had dropped by 60 to 70 per cent from peak levels in 2013 and 2014. With lower rents and strong tourist spending power, more foreign brands would enter Hong Kong, he said. “It would not be surprising if two or three out of every 10 new outlets eventually close,” Lee said. He also characterised Dairy Queen’s decision to open four branches across four different parts of the city as a marketing tactic intended to gain rapid visibility. “The weather is getting hotter and hotter, so more people will eat ice cream, and tourists also like to eat ice cream,” Lee said. “They won’t wait for northbound consumption just to eat ice cream. A cup is only a few dozen dollars.” Lee said foreign brands had been closely monitoring tourist arrival numbers, with the recent uptick encouraging them to expand their operations to Hong Kong. The city welcomed 31.22 million visitors in the first seven months of 2026, an 11 per cent increase year on year. The total value of Hong Kong’s retail sales rose for the 15th consecutive month in July, with the government reporting an uptick of 4.5 per cent from last year. Sales in the first seven months of the year grew by 8.9 per cent year on year. Lee also noted that certain niche industries, such as traditional cafes, cigar stores and gold shops, were expanding alongside international brands to capitalise on cheaper leasing terms.

title: China, US military commanders snap 2-year break with talks in Canada
description: Yang Zhibin and Samuel Paparo meet to keep communication lines open between the two armed forces.
content: China and the US have ended a two-year break in command-level contact with a meeting in Canada between the top PLA officer overseeing the Taiwan Strait and his US Pacific counterpart. Chinese General Yang Zhibin, commander of the Eastern Theatre Command, and US Admiral Samuel Paparo met for the first time at the Indo-Pacific Chiefs of Defence Conference in Victoria, British Columbia, on Monday. The US command said on Friday that Yang and Paparo discussed the importance of maintaining open lines of communication between senior US and Chinese military leaders to reduce the risk of miscalculation and to promote safe and professional conduct between forces. The conference was co-hosted by the Canadian Armed Forces and the US Pacific Command and took place from Monday to Wednesday. A total of 32 senior military representatives from 29 countries attended. This is the second theatre-level contact since China scaled back military ties with the US in August 2022. Engagement resumed after the Chinese and US presidents agreed in San Francisco in 2023 to restart communications between the People’s Liberation Army and the Pentagon. The last such contact was in Hawaii at the Indo-Pacific Chiefs of Defence Conference in September 2024, when Paparo held talks with General Wu Yanan, the then-commander of the PLA Southern Theatre Command. At that meeting, the US Pacific Command said Paparo sent a similar message, underscoring “the importance of sustained lines of communication between the US military and the PLA to reduce the risk of misperception or miscalculation”. China opted out of the conference held in Thailand last year. At this year’s gathering, Yang used a speech to outline the position and achievements of the Chinese military in maintaining regional peace and stability and to propose that regional countries strengthen defence cooperation and exchange, Chinese defence ministry spokesman Jiang Bin said on Friday. The Chinese delegation also held bilateral meetings with delegates from various countries, including the United States, France and Singapore, Jiang said, without giving further details. Paparo also held bilateral meetings with counterparts from Asia and Europe to discuss shared security interests, and took part in meetings of the Defence Cooperation Council, and the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue, or Quad. In addition, he met counterparts from Britain and Australia to discuss Aukus, a trilateral security pact centred on equipping Australia with conventionally armed, nuclear-powered submarines to deepen military integration across the Indo-Pacific. The defence conference brings together military leaders, practitioners and regional experts to discuss regional security issues, including non-defence and non-military perspectives. The 2026 gathering focused on shared security challenges, interoperability, emerging technologies and respect for international law, the Canadian government said. It said these exchanges strengthened relationships among defence leaders and reinforced the importance of sustained cooperation in addressing common challenges across the Indo-Pacific.

title: Hong Kong golfers make history after winning Asia-Pacific Amateur Team Championship
description: Markus Lam’s four-round total of nine-under won him the Taimur Hassan Amin Trophy for leading individual at the tournament.
content: Hong Kong’s golfers made history in Beijing on Friday, holding off the might of Japan, South Korea and the hosts to claim the Asia-Pacific Men’s Amateur Golf Team Championship title. Markus Lam, Ethan Tian-jun and Jeffrey Shen Wang-ngai combined for a total of 19-under-par to finish four clear of the field, despite a back-and-forth battle in the final round. Japan, who have won the Nomura Cup 10 times and narrowly missed out last year to Vietnam, were second, with Korea in third, a further seven shots back on eight under. Victory added the city’s name to a list of teams that have defied the region’s powerhouses to win the Nomura Cup. One-time champions include the likes of India, New Zealand and Vietnam. In another first, Lam’s four-round total of nine-under won him the Taimur Hassan Amin Trophy for leading individual at the tournament at the Bayhood No 9 International Golf Club. “I’m very proud of the boys,” Tim Tang, the Hong Kong head coach, said. “They are talented individuals who work really hard so this week we just played our game. Markus just kept pushing. Ethan finished with an eagle and a birdie, Jeffrey finished two under and then Markus birdied the last hole – it was a great team effort.” Tang’s team began the final day with a two-stroke advantage over Japan, with the Philippines, China and Korea harbouring hopes of a dramatic final-day charge. But it soon developed into a two-horse race between Hong Kong and Japan. With tension mounting, the pivotal hole proved to be the par-three 15th. With the team and individual titles in the balance, Lam showed nerves of steel, draining a 35-foot birdie putt. Kaito Sato, his playing partner, then failed to convert his birdie attempt from five feet. The momentum was now firmly with Hong Kong after Shen carded a 70 and Tian a 69. With Lam’s 67, Hong Kong posted a day four team score of 136 with only the best two scores in each three-man team being counted. That gave Hong Kong an overall aggregate of 19-under 557. That was four in front of the Japanese, despite Kato’s closing 68 and a two-under 70 from last year’s Asia-Pacific Amateur Championship runner-up Taisei Nagasaki. Mao Matsuyama, the third member of the Japan team, signed off with a fourth successive one-under 71. Lam and Sato were tied for the individual lead after three rounds and there was not much to separate them on the final day as they went toe-to-toe in a nail-biting contest within the main team contest. Ultimately, it was Lam who prevailed, rolling home his eighth birdie of the day at the 18th for a 67 and a nine-under 279 total – one in front of Sato. “Congratulations to Hong Kong on pulling off a famous victory that will be talked about and remembered for many decades,” Philip Hassall, chairman of the Asia-Pacific Golf Confederation, said. “It’s testament to the growing strength of APGC member nations that we’ve now had two first-time winners of the Nomura Cup in a row.”

title: What is ‘nailmaxxing’? Natural, ‘clean’ trend is hot right now, but it’s not easy to nail
description: The latest beauty trend focuses on healthy, natural-looking nails over elaborate art. Experts weigh in on the shift towards simple elegance.
content: Chrome French tips and polka dots may have been huge last year, but nail artists say this year’s trending manicures are more low-maintenance. “The reasoning is pretty much always some combo of ‘I want my nails to look natural’, and being over chipped polish and constant infills, work environments where loud nails feel like a lot, or just wanting that effortless low-maintenance style,” says celebrity manicurist Iram Shelton. At Marc Jacobs’ spring/summer 2026 show, models walked the runway with short, bare-looking, deliberately unpolished nails. The runway chimed with a wider trend known as “naked nails”, where natural-looking nail beds, neat shapes and healthy shine replaced elaborate art and obvious colour – perhaps an extension of the “clean girl make-up” look. Social media is taking the trend one step further with “nailmaxxing” – a term for maximising the appearance and health of your natural nails. “It’s probably the biggest shift I’ve seen in my chair this past year,” Shelton says. “People who used to come in begging for chrome or crazy nail art are now like ‘make it look like I’m not wearing anything’, which is kind of funny because that look actually takes way more skill than people think.” If you want to master nailmaxxing, here is how to perfect a manicure so it looks like you barely have one at all. What actually is nailmaxxing? Much like “looksmaxxing” or “sleepmaxxing”, nailmaxxing essentially means maximising every element of how your nails look. “Nailmaxxing is essentially about maximising the appearance and health of your natural nails, looking at everything from the shape and length of the nail to the condition of the cuticles and surrounding skin,” explains nail technician Rhiannon Thayre at Paint Nails London. “Rather than focusing solely on nail art, there is much more attention on making the natural nail itself look as healthy, elongated and well-groomed as possible.” Thayre believes its popularity reflects a rejection of obviously “done” beauty in favour of more natural, effortless-looking results. “There’s also a move towards treating nail care in a similar way to skincare,” she says. “People are increasingly interested in the health of the nail and the skin around it, rather than only thinking about which colour they’re going to choose.” So what is a ‘naked manicure’? There are slightly different interpretations of just how naked your nails need to be. For nail artist Hannah Johnson at Shoreditch Nails, also in London, it is about “a well-maintained natural nail [with] no product worn on the nail”. “The look is defined by a perfectly neat shape and healthy shine, achieved with cuticle oil and buffed to a shine,” Johnson says. Thayre’s interpretation, however, requires a little more help. “The naked manicure is all about enhancing what you naturally have rather than covering it up,” she says, suggesting, “a sheer wash of nude, pink or milky colour that allows the natural nail to remain visible”. And despite the appetite for “bare” nails, Shelton says most of her clients are not abandoning nail varnish altogether – rather looking for their shade, but better. “As for the split, most people aren’t going fully bare. I’d say it’s like 80/20 towards that ‘glazed doughnut, your nails but better’ look.” How do you get healthier-looking nails? If nailmaxxing has encouraged you to scrutinise your nail beds, buying a cupboard full of strengthening products is not necessarily the answer. Johnson says three of the most important steps are “not to pick or peel your gel [or] BIAB [builder in a bottle] off”, as well as going to a salon where time and care are taken with removals and nail prep, with no over-filing or buffing of the nail plate. For at home, “oil and protecting your nails with gloves when cleaning” is a must, Johnson says. Cuticle oil is also top of Thayre’s list. “If I could get clients to adopt one nail habit, it would be applying a good-quality cuticle oil every day,” she says. “Keeping the nail and surrounding skin conditioned helps maintain flexibility, and a flexible nail is generally less likely to become brittle and snap.” She recommends looking for nourishing oils such as jojoba, alongside protecting hands from excessive exposure to water and cleaning chemicals, as Johnson also says. Do you need to give up gel and BIAB? While we all know gel manicures are not the healthiest thing for our nails, you do not necessarily need to give them up when you are pursuing nailmaxxing. “You can absolutely maintain healthy natural nails while wearing gel or builder products such as BIAB,” Thayre says. “In my experience, the biggest factor isn’t simply whether somebody wears an enhancement; it’s how well that product is applied, maintained and removed.” Johnson similarly says a break is not always required “if your gel or BIAB is intact and not lifting”. “Taking a break is good when your nails are brittle from dehydration or if there has been any damage from removing or over-prepping the nail,” she says. Both, however, say peeling products off at home is the worst thing you can do for your nails. Johnson also says not to glue lifted gel back onto the nail and instead head to the salon for a proper application. “Clients sometimes assume their nails need to ‘breathe’, but the nail plate itself is made from keratinised cells and doesn’t breathe in the way skin does,” Thayre explains. “If there are signs of thinning, soreness, significant peeling or another problem, that’s when I would reassess what’s being used and whether a period without enhancements is best.” How to recreate a naked manicure at home The good news is that this viral nail trend does not require a particularly steady hand. “The easiest way to recreate the naked manicure at home is taking your time to file the perfect shape, and using a nourishing cuticle oil to keep them hydrated and shiny,” Johnson says. If you want some colour, Thayre recommends a sheer nude, soft pink or milky neutral rather than an opaque nail varnish. “You want something that subtly blurs imperfections while still allowing the natural nail to show through. One or two very thin coats usually give that effortless ‘your nails but better’ effect.” Rather than automatically reaching for beige or baby pink, consider your undertones too. “Some people suit a cooler sheer pink, while others with warm or green undertones look better with a warmer beige, peach or neutral nude,” Thayre says. “Rather than trying to match your skin exactly, look for a shade that makes both the nail and surrounding skin look fresh and healthy.” Finish with a glossy top coat and cuticle oil – or, for a genuinely naked manicure, skip the polish entirely and carefully buff the natural nail to a shine.

title: China and South Korea accuse each other of undermining key national principles
description: Seoul protests about an official reference to ‘two states’ in Korea, while Beijing complains about an art exhibition’s ‘Taiwan Pavilion’.
content: China and South Korea have exchanged formal protests over the highly sensitive Taiwan question and Korean unity. The two countries have been trying to improve relations in recent months, but South Korean national security adviser Wi Sung-lac said he had issued “a serious objection” after an official Chinese statement welcomed moves “towards the peaceful coexistence of the two states of South and North Korea”. Meanwhile, Beijing “lodged serious representations” with Seoul over an art event that featured a “Taiwan pavilion”, prompting mainland China’s artists to withdraw from the event in protest. Wi’s protest was prompted by a statement issued after his recent meeting with Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi. “Because the Chinese side’s post-meeting statement included the expression ‘two states’ and this differs from what we think, we raised a serious objection,” Wi said. South Korea does not recognise North Korea as a separate sovereign state, instead viewing the Korean peninsula as a single territory awaiting reunification. Wi added that when Beijing and Seoul established formal diplomatic relations in 1992, China had expressed support for reunification, and treating the Korean peninsula as “two states” was a move away from reaching that goal. Wi added that South Korea was “urging the Chinese side not to use expressions that could cause such misunderstandings” but also said Wang had not used the phrase “two states” during their meeting. When the two Koreas joined the United Nations simultaneously in 1991, both stressed that the inter-Korean relationship was not one between states but a special interim relationship. But two years ago, North Korean leader Kim Jong-un said inter-Korean ties should be redefined as a relationship between “two hostile states” and references to “national reunification” were removed from the constitution. More recently, the Workers’ Party of Korea formally removed the goal of reunification from its charter, according to the Institute for National Security Strategy, a think tank affiliated with the South’s National Intelligence Service. China’s use of the “two states” formulation has raised questions over whether Beijing has effectively accepted Kim’s line. Meanwhile, Beijing said it had lodged a complaint over the use of the phrase “Taiwan Pavilion” in the Gwangju Biennale, one of the most prestigious international contemporary art exhibitions in Asia. The Gwangju Biennale Foundation, the main organiser of the event, had earlier used the title “NTMoFA [National Taiwan Museum of Fine Arts] Pavilion” but changed the name following protests from Taiwanese artists. However, this prompted mainland China to quit the event in protest. According to South Korean media reports, an official delegation from the Chinese city of Guangzhou has also cancelled a visit to Gwangju next week. Beijing sees Taiwan as part of China and has never renounced the use of force to reunite it with the mainland. Most countries, including South Korea, do not recognise Taiwan as an independent state. Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun accused the biennale organisers of having “stubbornly clung to the wrongful practice, allowing China’s Taiwan region to participate under a designation that is completely incompatible with its status”. “China is firmly opposed to this and has lodged serious representations with the [Republic of Korea] side, demanding that the relevant party immediately correct its wrongdoing,” Guo said on Thursday, using the South’s official name. “We hope that the ROK government will honour its political commitments, earnestly shoulder its responsibilities and uphold the one-China principle with concrete actions.” Hours earlier, the Chinese embassy in South Korea also posted a statement on social media that “strongly urged the organisers of the biennale and the Gwangju municipal government to correct the mistake immediately and avoid causing serious negative impacts on the biennale’s reputation and on China-South Korea relations”. Beijing’s ambassador to Seoul, Dai Bing, visited Gwangju last week to meet city mayor Min Hyung-bae. South Korean media reported that Dai expressed his concerns about the Taiwan Pavilion, while the city government and biennale foundation apologised for procedural shortcomings and said they “respected” the one-China principle. The Chinese embassy’s statement about the visit did not mention the dispute. South Korean foreign ministry spokesman Park Doo-soon said the decision about the pavilion had nothing to do with the government and he hoped it would not “affect Korea-China relations or exchange and cooperation between the two countries”. Dai has also tried to strike a positive note about relations between Seoul and Beijing recently. At a meeting with National Assembly Speaker Cho Jeong-sik last month he said the two countries had become “inseparable strategic partners”. He also attended a tourism event in Seoul on Thursday, where he said ties were “entering a virtuous cycle of improvement and development” and he would encourage more South Korean tourists to visit China.

title: 2 Reform UK advisers to Farage step down amid donation scandal
description: The Labour Party has asked police to investigate after a report said Reform might have arranged for a foreign donor to pay for opinion polls.
content: Britain’s populist Reform UK said two senior advisers to leader Nigel Farage stepped down on Friday after an undercover investigation alleged the party had broken electoral law by arranging for a foreign donor to pay for political polling. Reform denied any wrongdoing and said it had been the victim of a hoax perpetrated by climate activists. The governing Labour Party wrote to the police asking them to investigate possible criminal offences, including an alleged proposal to channel a larger overseas donation through a ‌UK intermediary. The investigation, broadcast by Channel 4 just as Reform’s annual conference opened to the public, said two senior figures in Reform had arranged for a US company to pay more than £30,000 (US$40,586) for three opinion polls commissioned by the party. Such an arrangement could breach British laws on political funding, which ban foreign donations. Posing as wealthy donors from the United States with British connections, the undercover team from an investigative group called Verbatim said it spent a year speaking to top officials in Reform about possible donations, culminating in a lunch with Farage. Channel 4 said Verbatim was an independent organisation founded by journalists from the Centre for Climate Reporting, but that it had verified their findings, which included covertly filmed footage of meetings. Farage, a veteran Brexit campaigner who is under parliamentary investigation over earlier donations, told LBC radio: “The party has broken no laws. The party ‌has not taken any dodgy money or anything like that whatsoever.” Reform, which has seen its commanding lead in opinion polls falter over undeclared donor allegations, announced an internal investigation and said the two officials featured in the undercover filming – head of policy James Orr and ‌Farage’s right-hand man Dan Jukes – had stepped down pending its results. Orr, a philosophy professor at the University of Cambridge and friend of US Vice-President JD ⁠Vance, said in a video on social media that ⁠Reform had not been involved in commissioning the poll. “There’s absolutely no way this could amount to a benefit or donation in kind at all,” he said. “It wasn’t internal party polling. It wasn’t Reform UK’s poll. It was a public ‌poll arranged by an independent person paying an independent pollster, and those polls were published immediately for the general public.” The latest accusations over donations come on the first public day of the party’s annual conference, which Farage had hoped would offer him ‌a chance ‌of a reset after a difficult summer. Farage, 62, is being investigated by a parliamentary watchdog over a £5 million donation from crypto-billionaire Christopher Harborne in 2024. He denies any wrongdoing but has seen ‌support for his party soften in recent weeks. On Friday, Farage said both Jukes and Orr had “said things that shouldn’t have been said” in relation to donations purportedly originating ⁠in the United States, but no such donation had been accepted by the party and that the two had been “entrapped”. In a letter to the Metropolitan Police, Labour said the documentary contained two ⁠further possible breaches: discussion of channelling a donation from a US-based donor through a UK-based son and the suggestion that similar methods have been used in the past. A spokesperson for Reform said: “Reform UK has been the target of a hoax perpetrated by foreign-funded, climate change activists posing as would-be party donors. The party denies any wrongdoing. “Reform ‌UK has a robust vetting process for prospective donors ‌approved by the Electoral Commission.” The Metropolitan Police said it was aware of the allegations in the broadcast and would assess any information provided to them. This did not amount to the formal launch of an investigation. The Electoral Commission, which oversees and regulates political finance in Britain, said: “We are considering all relevant information, in line with our regulatory remit, and we are in touch with the Met Police. “The Electoral Commission has not approved the donor vetting process for Reform, or any other party. Parties are responsible for ensuring their internal processes and controls are fit for purpose.”

title: Hong Kong Disneyland Hotel to close from October 12 for major renovation
description: Victorian-style property, open since 2005, will feature Disney movie-themed rooms in makeover, with no reopening date set.
content: Hong Kong Disneyland Hotel will temporarily close from October 12 for a comprehensive renovation and upgrade, with no completion date announced, as the resort shifts focus to seasonal culinary offerings and immersive storytelling. Hong Kong Disneyland announced on Friday that the Victorian-style property, open since 2005, will be revamped with Disney movie-themed rooms, while retaining the hotel’s classic charm. “As the world’s only Disney resort backed by mountains and facing the sea, this place perfectly blends Disney magic with natural scenery, bringing guests a unique holiday experience,” said Anita Lai Pui-shan, vice-president of communications and public affairs. “The renovated hotel will retain its classic charm while integrating immersive story experiences, innovative design and better service, further consolidating Hong Kong Disneyland’s leading position in regional tourism.” The closure leaves the resort’s two other properties to absorb demand. Disney Explorers Lodge offers 750 rooms while Disney’s Hollywood Hotel has 600 rooms. Lai noted that average occupancy across all three hotels exceeded 80 per cent during the recent summer holiday, in line with the broader Hong Kong market. Over the coming months, the resort will continue to roll out Halloween and Christmas-themed dining, including some halal-certified offerings. The seasonal line-up includes the return of “Jack Skellington’s The Nightmare Before Dinner”, featuring theatrical lighting and smoke effects, alongside Christmas Frozen-themed treats in the World of Frozen area. Meanwhile, the hotel’s Crystal Lotus restaurant – known for its 2,238 crystal lotus entrance and Disney character dim sum – will be unavailable until the renovation is completed.

title: German firms back tougher EU trade measures on China despite business risks
description: The DIHK finds German firms facing Chinese competition back stronger EU action, but its trade chief warns against ‘blanket measures’.
content: More than half of German companies said the European Union should take stronger trade measures against China even if their own businesses would suffer higher prices, tariffs or retaliation, according to a survey of about 1,300 German firms published by the German Chamber of Commerce and Industry (DIHK) on Thursday. That tougher stance comes despite many German companies acknowledging their reliance on Chinese supply chains and production sites for their own competitiveness. Among companies with their own operations in China, support for tougher measures stood at 49 per cent, still ahead of the 46 per cent that opposed them. Competition from Chinese rivals was widespread across sectors, with two-thirds of respondents reporting an increase. The industrial sector – including machinery and automotive – was hit hardest: 83 per cent of those surveyed reported greater competition, and half described the pressure as strong or very strong. The survey came as Brussels and Beijing face the risk of a trade war ahead of an October deadline for tangible progress on economic disputes, as Berlin moves towards a more defensive posture. Chancellor Friedrich Merz said last week that German industry had “apparently changed its opinion” on global imbalances, and asked his cabinet to draw up proposals to address the trade imbalance with China. “Europe must decisively address and counter distortions of competition,” said Dr Volker Treier, DIHK’s head of foreign trade. “But it must not harm itself with blanket measures.” Treier described competition from China as entering a “new dimension”. Chinese suppliers had closed much of the gap with German firms on technology and quality, the report said, and had even gained technological leadership in some sectors such as electric mobility. As competition from China intensifies, two-thirds of companies called for a coordinated EU approach towards China, while 60 per cent wanted to reduce strategic dependencies. Nearly half backed excluding Chinese companies from critical infrastructure projects. The pressure was closely linked to companies’ exposure to China. Among firms with their own operations or investments there, 88 per cent reported growing competition, compared with 38 per cent of those with no direct business ties to the country. Europe must decisively address and counter distortions of competition. But it must not harm itself with blanket measures Volker Treier, German Chamber of Commerce and Industry Yet Treier cautioned that more competition did not necessarily mean less business in China. Only 12 per cent of companies facing stronger competition said they would consider exiting contested business lines. Half were cutting costs, while nearly a third planned to deepen cooperation with Chinese partners. The report found China’s supply chains and production sites could be essential for some German companies to stay competitive. Some companies said, for example, that buying new machinery from China was cheaper than repairing existing equipment in Germany. Treier also warned that trade defence could not compensate for home-made disadvantages. “If high energy and labour costs or excessive bureaucracy are holding our companies back, we have to solve those problems here,” he said. “This is not a call for a trade war,” Treier said. “Companies want fair competition, not isolation.” The impacts of rising Chinese competition are spilling over into the European labour market. Volkswagen Group announced on Thursday plans to slash another 50,000 jobs by 2030, citing intensifying competition and shifting demand, following similar reports of job cuts by carmakers including BMW. Trade talks between the EU and China are ongoing. Vice-minister of commerce Ling Ji held talks in Beijing with the European Commission’s deputy director general for trade and economic security Denis Redonnet between August 31 and September 2. A spokeswoman for China’s commerce ministry, Huang Ling, said on Thursday that trade talks between the two should address mutual concerns on an equal footing. “There should be no unilateral demands or conditions, let alone threats of closing markets at the slightest pretext,” Huang said. Additional reporting by Xinyi Wu

title: Meet Thea Frodin: from young Serena Williams body double in King Richard to US Open debut
description: The 17-year-old, who lost to No 2 seed Elena Rybakina in the first round, wants to graduate from high school before deciding on whether to turn pro.
content: Thea Frodin was only 12 when she was the body double of actress Demi Singleton, who played young Serena Williams in the 2021 film King Richard, which chronicles Serena and Venus Williams’ rise to tennis stardom with the help of their father Richard Williams. Earlier this week, the rising tennis star made her US Open debut. The 17-year-old was up against reigning Australian Open champion Elena Rybakina on September 1. She was eliminated, but this is just the start of Frodin’s tennis career. Here’s everything you need to know about the up-and-coming tennis star, Thea Frodin. She grew up playing tennis Thea Frodin was born in December 2008 in Southern California. She started playing tennis when she was six and by 12, she was already proving her talent on the court, so much so that she was cast as the body double of actress Demi Singleton who played young Serena Williams in the Oscar-winning film King Richard starring Will Smith. Frodin spent months mastering the movements and strokes required to mimic a young Serena for the film. “Being able to play the role of somebody that I looked up to for my whole life was super special. I was honoured. She was one of the players that I looked up to most, just when I was starting to play, and she’s such an inspiration to me,” she said at the time, according to The Sun. She is unsure about a professional tennis career Since starring in the film, Frodin has continued to hone her talents. In 2023, she was first runner-up in the girls’ 16s event at the Orange Bowl, a prestigious annual youth tennis tournament held in Florida. Frodin, who is six feet tall, went on to qualify for the US Open as a wild card after winning the USTA Billie Jean King Girls’ 18s national championship and beating out five seeded players. “I tried going out there to see what it would be like just to, I guess, feel no pressure … just go out there and have a fun time,” Frodin told The New Zealand Herald after her loss against Rybakina on September 1. “I feel like that’s what I accomplished, and obviously I have a lot to learn, but I’m excited with most of the things I did out there.” She has also expressed that she’s still unsure about whether she will pursue a professional career in tennis after graduating from high school. “I think I’m trying to just finish high school, see where the rest of this year takes me,” Frodin said. “I’m not rushing into kind of making a decision with all that,” she told the newspaper.

title: 5 ParknShop and contractor staff who forged pay claims plead guilty to fraud
description: Hong Kong corruption watchdog says defendants colluded to make pay claims for staff who were not on shift, defrauding retail giant of HK$3.2 million.
content: Five former employees of Hong Kong supermarket chain ParknShop and its contractors have pleaded guilty to conspiracy to defraud by falsifying workers’ attendance records to cheat the retail giant of HK$3.2 million (US$408,000). The Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) said on Friday that an investigation revealed that the former supermarket employees colluded with contractor staff over two years to deceive ParknShop by falsifying attendance records for 13 warehouse workers who were not on shift at the chain’s distribution centre. The defendants – Lau Kin-pong, 44, then a senior supervisor at ParknShop’s eCommercial Distribution Centre, Tai Kin-man, 43, then assistant manager of Earnward Warehouse, and three former warehouse workers employed by Logistics Network Management, Wong Wai-fung, 27, Wong Pak-kan, 28, and Lau Tsz-pan, 28 – all pleaded guilty to conspiracy to defraud at the District Court on Friday. The corruption watchdog said the scheme was carried out at ParknShop’s eCommercial Distribution Centre, where logistics personnel sorted online orders and packed goods for delivery to customers. The workers were supplied by a contractor, Logistics Network Management, but supervised by another company, Earnward Warehouse. According to the watchdog, Logistics Network Management facilitated wage payments and billed ParknShop based on workers’ shift hours, while daily attendance sheets were verified by Earnward Warehouse’s assistant manager. Between June 2019 and April 2021, the five defendants used an identical clocking machine to fabricate the attendance records for the 13 logistics warehouse workers. The ICAC said the workers never worked at the distribution facility during the specified period and did not receive any wages. Instead, the defendants forged the workers’ signatures on time cards and also used the personal data of job applicants and former staff. The five defendants admitted that, from 2019, they were invited by a warehouse operations manager at the distribution centre to falsify the records and deceive the supermarket into releasing wages. The five defendants and the operations manager subsequently shared the HK$3.2 million they fraudulently obtained among themselves, the ICAC said. Judge Ernest Lin Kam-hung adjourned sentencing to March 5 next year and remanded the defendants in custody. Co-defendant Cheng Cheuk-kei, 43, then warehouse operations manager at the ParknShop distribution centre, earlier pleaded not guilty to one count of conspiracy to defraud, the ICAC said. His trial is scheduled for February 10 next year, the agency added.

title: Why less visibility into how OpenAI’s new GPT-6 Astra ‘thinks’ is sparking safety concerns
description: The Hugging Face breach in July highlights the importance of being able to inspect what models are ‘thinking’, say analysts.
content: OpenAI’s new model, GPT-6 Astra, has less direct visibility into how a model thinks, a development that has sparked concerns coming just weeks after the Hugging Face hacking incident that required a Chinese open model to investigate, according to analysts. When announcing Astra on Thursday, OpenAI said it was “the world’s most intelligent and aligned model,” with a “significant jump in cyber capabilities”. OpenAI president Greg Brockman said at the end of a press call announcing Astra’s arrival that it likely represents AGI, or artificial general intelligence – AI that matches or outperforms human intelligence. However, OpenAI also said the model’s written reasoning was “harder to monitor” compared with GPT-5.6 Sol, the previous generation released in July. “We have found that GPT-6 Astra is more capable of controlling its own CoT (chain of thought) than GPT-5.6 Sol, and less likely to include incriminating information in its CoT,” OpenAI said, referring to the intermediate reasoning steps an AI generates while solving a task. The shift in visibility stems from a technique known as recurrent depth, or looped transformers, which reuses parts of a neural network. As a result, it processes complex logic inside hidden mathematical loops rather than in step-by-step readable text, The Information reported on Tuesday ahead of the launch. OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki on X called the report “confusing”, without naming the media. OpenAI did not disclose architectural details of the new system. A company representative said in a statement to the South China Morning Post on Friday that the decline in monitorability was “a real challenge that [it] takes seriously”. The representative added that the new model does not use “neuralese”, a controversial technique where AI reasons internally using mathematical representations rather than words. As frontier AI labs race to squeeze greater intelligence out of increasingly expensive computing infrastructure, the decrease in visibility has drawn global attention, especially after OpenAI’s agents breached the Hugging Face platform in July, highlighting the importance of being able to inspect what models are thinking. Is recurrent depth a bad thing? Unlike existing AI architectures that pass text through a fixed series of computational layers to determine the next word, recurrent depth loops the data through these layers repeatedly. This approach can have a positive impact on performance and costs. Hamish Low, research associate at the Institute for AI Policy and Strategy, said it may “reduce the amount of memory required by having a smaller model repeat some of its internal processing” amid growing memory chip costs. The technique effectively buys “greater reasoning depth with fewer weights and potentially lower memory requirements,” said Wei Sun, principal analyst for artificial intelligence at Counterpoint Research. However, this approach reduces “the amount of reasoning humans can directly inspect,” which “creates an emerging intelligence-versus-observability trade-off”, Sun said. What are the security concerns? Reading the chain-of-thought reasoning can be critical for understanding the high-profile Hugging Face incident, analysts said. “Having much of the reasoning occur in a closed box rather than by ‘thinking out loud’ through normal human language will make it much harder to understand how these AI systems are operating,” said Kyle Chan, a fellow at the Brookings Institution. Researchers investigating the Hugging Face incident were able to reconstruct the agents’ behaviour partly by examining their written chains of thought. When Hugging Face detected the intrusion, its security team initially tried using commercial frontier AI models to help analyse the incoming attack, but those requests were blocked by the providers’ automated safety guardrails. Consequently, it opted to run Z.ai’s open-weight model, GLM-5.2, locally to contain the attack. “The fact that the Hugging Face incident happened, and then right afterwards, they are releasing a model that’s harder to monitor – that’s why so many people are freaked out,” said Ben Hayum, research assistant for the Technology and National Security Program at the Centre for a New American Security (CNAS). “If we keep getting substantial gains in the internal processing we can do without external visibility into it, AI model alignment becomes a lot harder from the get-go in terms of creating a safe model,” he added. Are Chinese AI firms adopting it? Z.ai, also known as Zhipu, has started looking into the looped transformer architectures. In an earnings call earlier this week, company founder Tang Jie discussed using a “Loop Transformer” to increase the effective depth of its models and described the direction of its next-generation GLM-6 model as “self-evolution”. Analysts said this technique was attractive to Chinese developers, given their limited access to advanced compute resources. Low at the AI policy institute said Chinese AI firms might have stronger incentives to adopt it amid ongoing price wars, but it depended on how large the benefits were. “The hardware they have, their research priorities and training data, and how they balance lower costs against speed and model performance also affect their decisions,” he added. Counterpoint’s Sun said the technique could be attractive, but it “should be viewed as compute reallocation, not free compute.” “The same economics apply in the US too,” she added. It remained to be seen whether other companies follow suit, said Jinge Wang, an AI safety research engineer at Concordia AI. If AI companies’ primary goal was to enhance capabilities, model interpretability and monitorability would “inevitably deteriorate”, Wang said. Additional reporting by Vincent Chow

title: Inspired by childhood surgery, Chinese man now works alongside saviour surgeon 19 years later
description: Huang says the doctor saved his life and gave him a second chance, and his gratitude has transformed into a profound passion for medicine.
content: A young Chinese man recently became colleagues with the doctor who saved him from a congenital heart defect 19 years ago, prompting many to marvel at the wonder of fate. Huang Hongxin, 23, has recently enrolled as a postgraduate student in the neurosurgery department at Xiangya Hospital, affiliated with Central South University. Nearly two decades ago, Huang underwent a life-saving surgery to address his congenital heart disease at the same hospital. His condition included pulmonary artery stenosis and patent foramen ovale, which other hospitals had difficulty treating. Originally from Jiangxi province in eastern China, his family travelled to Xiangya Hospital in central Hunan province, where Professor Long Long and Professor Hu Qinghua’s team successfully performed the surgery on Huang. Thanks to their dedicated efforts, Huang was able to grow up like any other ordinary child. As he matured, he gradually came to understand the profound significance of that life-saving surgery. “The doctor saved me and granted me a new life,” he remarked. His gratitude towards the doctors blossomed into a deep passion for medicine. In 2024, Huang’s grandmother was also hospitalised in the neurosurgery department of Xiangya Hospital due to a cerebral aneurysm. She was treated by Professor Huang Jun’s team, who meticulously analysed imaging data and discussed surgical plans repeatedly to ensure a successful surgery and prevent potentially fatal brain haemorrhage. This experience further solidified Huang’s desire to join Xiangya Hospital. He diligently prepared for the postgraduate entrance exam and was recently admitted. Now, he studies under Professor Huang, who saved his grandmother’s life. Moreover, the wonder of fate did not end there. To young Huang’s surprise, as he undergoes clinical residency training – which requires students to rotate through different departments – his first assignment is in cardiac and vascular surgery, and his first mentor is Professor Long Long, the very same doctor who saved his life 19 years ago. Young Huang expressed his commitment to refining his professional skills through hard work, with the goal of protecting the health of more patients. He has taken a memorable photo with his lifesaver, both wearing surgical gowns. The image and his inspiring story have resonated deeply with many online. “The best way to express gratitude is to become you,” commented one online observer. “It is a relay of life and an inheritance of passion,” remarked another.

title: Swimmer Yu Zidi among bumper China team for Asian Games, but Zheng Qinwen misses out
description: The squad has an average age of 24 and also features reigning Olympic champions Wang Zongyuan, Chen Yuxi, Sun Yingsha and Wang Manyu.
content: Yu Zidi, the 13-year-old swimming sensation, will be among a bumper 815 Chinese athletes heading to the Asian Games in Japan this month, state media said Friday. Comprising 36 Olympic champions, the squad has an average age of 24, and over a quarter of the athletes are 20 or under, with most making their Games debuts. Yu, who became the youngest medallist in swimming world championships history last year aged just 12, is part of a team comprising 404 women and 411 men who will compete in 38 sports. Reigning Olympic champions include divers Wang Zongyuan and Chen Yuxi, as well as table tennis gold medallists Sun Yingsha and Wang Manyu. However, Zheng Qinwen, the 2024 Paris Games women’s singles tennis champion, will not be involved. Diver Wang said the Games “represents the highest-level comprehensive sporting event in Asia and serves as a genuine test of our preparation”. “We will showcase China’s standard and strength on the regional and global stage,” Wang added. The total delegation comprises 1,274 members, including staff from 69 countries and regions, such as Australia, Spain, France, the Netherlands and Great Britain. China have topped both the gold medal and overall medal tables at every Asian Games since 1982 and ⁠delivered a record-breaking performance on home soil in Hangzhou ‌in 2023, winning 201 gold medals and 383 medals overall. The 2026 Asian Games will run from September 19 to October 4, featuring 43 sports and athletes from 45 countries and regions.

title: Malaysia declares emergency in Sarawak town as haze pollution level hits 521
description: Indonesian police have arrested 112 people suspected of starting the recent forest and peatland fires in 10 provinces on Sumatra and Borneo.
content: Malaysia declared an emergency on Friday in a town in Sarawak state on Borneo Island after air pollution breached the country’s emergency-level threshold linked to fires in neighbouring Indonesia. The Air Pollutant Index in Serian, a small agricultural town of just under 90,000 near the border of Indonesia’s Kalimantan province, surged to 521 on Friday, according to Malaysia’s environment department. Sarawak’s much larger capital, Kuching, also showed a hazardous reading of 311. Malaysia’s King Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar has consented to the declaration of an emergency in Serian, which would allow more effective measures to be taken, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim’s office said in a statement. It did not provide details but officials have said a reading above 500 could provide for non-essential work and outdoor activities to be halted. Schools are already shut if the index is above 200.
