Born in Austria and raised in Hong Kong, Bernie was fluent in Cantonese, adored and mastered martial arts and was described as wise beyond his years. Known for his kindness – he once sheltered a homeless boy – Bernie was a stunt performer in Los Angeles when he was diagnosed with Aids, contracted from a woman he loved and later married, before he died, in 1996, aged 33. Even in the shadow of loss, Bernie refused to let their story end in tragedy. Together with Kwan and her new husband, Vienna-born actor and producer Norbert Meisel, now aged 96, the family completed a final project: Rebellious (also known as The Biker Poet), a 1995 film about a biker discovering himself, a testament to Bernie’s creativity and enduring spirit. In the years since, Kwan has devoted herself to Aids awareness advocacy, channelling her grief into purpose. She also wrote Celebration of a Life: Memories of My Son (1997), a memoir that honours Bernie and preserves his memory. Arthur Dong, the Oscar-nominated filmmaker and American Book Award-winning author of Forbidden City, USA (2014), has interviewed Kwan on many occasions over the past 20 years. He recalls the magnetic presence she brought to every set. “Nancy candidly confronts the xenophobic and sexist attitudes that once branded her a ‘real-life China doll’, despite the pivotal influence of producer and mentor Ray Stark, who promoted her as a ‘girl of many nations’.” Kwan became a symbol of possibility for actors navigating Hollywood’s rigid and often Eurocentric standards. “I am from the East and West. My father is Chinese, my mother is English, and bringing that together … I feel very proud. The world is getting smaller, we recognise each other more and I wish I had even more cultural roots to embrace. It’s a wonderful thing,” she reflects. “Nancy was among the most beautifully photographed women of the 60s,” notes Dong. “That she was biracial made her worldwide popularity even more historic, particularly in the image- and race-conscious world of entertainment.” Her pragmatism has always stood out to him. “In 2004, when I asked her to sum up the roller-coaster trajectory of her career, she replied, ‘What’s fair in life? There’s no fairness. As an actor, you have to keep that in mind; otherwise, you might as well not be in this business. Nothing lasts forever. Times change.’” Even in her mid-80s, Kwan retains vitality and joy. Asked what she does to relax, she replies, “Probably tai chi, meditation […] that is the way I am.” Her energy and elegance are palpable. “I’ve been in the business a long time now. I made my mark in the 60s, and now it’s [the mid-2020s]. It’s been a long journey, and I’ve met so many people along the way. Many Asian actors I know are still working, thank goodness, and television has opened up opportunities for them.” Any advice for budding artists? “Just work hard,” she says. “Do what you can, steadily. Go out there. The film business is changing, too.”

title: Trump to speak on both nights of Republican midterm convention amid turnout concerns
description: The US president was originally set to close out the event but will now also take the stage the first night to ‘set the tone’.
content: US President Donald Trump will now speak on both nights of the Republican Party’s unusual midterm convention next week, a party official said on Wednesday, an expanded role that will compete for ‌viewers with the start of the NFL season. Trump had originally been scheduled to deliver an address on Thursday to close out the September 9-10 convention in Dallas, but now will deliver the keynote speech on Wednesday and speak after US Vice-President J.D. Vance on Thursday evening as well, the party official said on condition of anonymity. “President Trump wants to set the tone for the entire convention,” the party official said, explaining why Trump ⁠was now going to speak on the first night. The change comes as some party insiders have said they are concerned ‌the Republican National Committee may struggle to attract members and activists to the event. Trump is grappling with weak approval ratings amid voter dissatisfaction over the Iran war and persistent inflation, raising ‌the stakes for Republican candidates fighting to preserve their party’s narrow congressional majorities in November. The convention begins just ⁠after Labour Day on ⁠Monday, when campaigns typically start their final sprint towards Election Day. Another senior Republican Party official, who asked to remain unidentified, said he has heard the ‌party is struggling to attract attendees to the convention and that the White House and Trump’s political team have stepped up efforts to encourage Republicans to attend. Organisers ‌have expressed ‌confidence that the American Airlines Centre arena, where the convention is being held, will be filled. One Republican operative familiar ‌with the event, however, said he had heard the convention will allow more everyday supporters than initially planned because organisers have ⁠not been able to find enough Republican officials and donors to attend. After months of negative headlines tied to the Iran ⁠war and rising living costs, party officials see the gathering as their best opportunity to rally voters behind Trump’s agenda ahead of the November 3 election. Some Republicans, however, remain sceptical it can meaningfully shift voter sentiment. The ‌convention’s opening night will coincide ‌with a Super Bowl rematch between the New England Patriots and Seattle Seahawks, airing on NBC and its streaming service, Peacock. On Thursday night, Trump and Vance will compete for viewers with a highly anticipated NFL rivalry match-up between the San Francisco 49ers and Los Angeles Rams in Melbourne, Australia, which will stream exclusively on Netflix.

title: Editorial | Deal reached on Wang Fuk Court flats clears the way for recovery
description: Resolving resettlement for most Tai Po fire victims now paves the way for the next essential step towards closure: full accountability.
content: With the first anniversary of the Tai Po fire less than three months away, Hong Kong’s recovery from the disaster is making steady progress. Nearly all affected households have accepted the government’s buyout offer, providing residents with a clear path towards rebuilding their lives. Meanwhile, the independent inquiry into the blaze is expected to table its report next month – an important step towards establishing accountability and ensuring that lessons are learned and acted upon. The near-unanimous acceptance by Wang Fuk Court households of the HK$7.8 billion (US$994.8 million) buyout offer marks another milestone in handling the aftermath of the inferno that claimed 168 lives and displaced thousands of residents last November. Of the estate’s 1,984 owners, 1,967 accepted the offer by the August 31 deadline, leaving only 17 outstanding cases. The overwhelming 99.1 per cent response is an endorsement of the government’s approach to help survivors rebuild their homes elsewhere. It also reflects a consensus among households that they should strive to move on, even as they await a fuller understanding of how their homes were wiped out in the city’s worst high-rise building blaze and what must be done to prevent a recurrence. Of course, no monetary offer can restore lives lost, erase the trauma of survivors or recreate the homes and neighbourly ties destroyed by the disaster. The residents have not forgotten what happened, nor should they be expected to. But most have decided that the practical path towards recovery lies in accepting the offer that enables them to start anew elsewhere. The buy-back enables most owners to make new plans – whether it is to buy another home, opt for the special subsidised-housing arrangements, or simply put behind the months of agonising loss and uncertainty. Their decision is also broadly in line with the wishes of society at large. Hong Kong people expect the authorities to handle a disaster of this magnitude with compassion, urgency and pragmatism. The outcome gives the government a clear basis to proceed with the next stage of recovery. The 17 owners who did not accept the offer should not be dismissed as stubborn holdouts standing in the way of recovery. Given the different views and circumstances among the affected households, the offer was never expected to be taken up by all. Some owners may have accepted simply because the alternative – remaining in uncertainty while waiting for the legal processes to run their course – was just more unbearable. Others who did not accept the deal may simply be too overwhelmed by their emotions to act. It is unfortunate that they missed the opportunity for an early conclusion to the resettlement issue, making it more challenging for them to move on. The government could potentially trigger compulsory acquisition of the remaining flats by legislation. Whatever its next steps, it must proceed with sensitivity and transparency, offering the concerned homeowners a solution that is lawful, fair and reasonable. Equally important are the pursuits of accountability and building and fire safety reforms. The questions of what went wrong and who should be held accountable are still weighing heavily on the minds of the survivors and the wider community. Answers are urgently needed, not just for the sake of justice, but also to hasten the necessary reforms to address and fix the systemic lapses that led to the fire. The independent committee appointed by Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu must therefore proceed as quickly as possible. The family of those killed, injured residents and the wider public deserve a clear account of the circumstances that contributed to the disaster. Lee has rightly pledged to hold those responsible to account. Any individual, company or public body found to have breached legal obligations or failed in their responsibilities must answer for their failings through the appropriate channels. The overwhelming acceptance of the flat buy-back is a positive step towards bringing closure to this horrific episode. But it is only the first step. The tragedy can only be laid to rest when resettlement is resolved, justice is served, lessons are learned and institutional safeguards are strengthened.

title: How Africa’s first Shaolin Temple shares Chinese martial arts and culture
description: The temple in Zambia has become one of the most visible symbols of China’s cultural footprint in a country where its influence already runs deep.
content: From a distance, the Shaolin Temple outside Lusaka appears almost like a mirage, a slice of central China dropped into the Zambian landscape. Then the dragons emerge from beneath the pagoda, their brightly coloured fabric bodies hoisted on poles by teenagers moving with surprising precision. Nearby, smaller children tumble across a weather-beaten foam mattress, twisting into barrels and forward rolls as 30-year-old instructor Yan Chen barks commands. The sprawling complex houses Africa’s first Shaolin Temple – part of a Buddhist monastic martial arts tradition – set on a 20,000-square-metre (215,300 sq ft) plot in Ngwerere, 18km (11 miles) north of the Zambian capital. The site was donated by Chinese businessman Jiang Qingde, with the cost of building the cultural centre estimated at nearly US$6 million. It has become one of the most visible symbols of China’s cultural footprint in a country where Beijing’s influence already runs deep through investment in mines, roads, factories and infrastructure. John Bwalya arrived at the temple three years ago. “I grew up watching The Karate Kid on TV and told myself I needed to learn this thing,” he says, recalling the 2010 reboot of the film series featuring martial-arts star Jackie Chan. Now 23, Bwalya lives at the temple alongside 36 other students, most from underprivileged backgrounds. Shaolin is one of the most well-known schools of wushu (Chinese martial arts). There are many videos online and films showing the rigorous training of Shaolin monks. This school originated at the Shaolin Temple in the Songshan mountains of central China’s Henan province. The temple was built around 495 and is the ancestral temple of the Zen school of Chinese Buddhism. At the Shaolin Temple in Ngwerere, under the watch of four Chinese instructors, a Zambian and an Ivorian, students’ days begin as early as 3am. The compound is their school, training ground and home: they sleep, study and train there, leaving only for a few days each December to visit their families. Students also earn a stipend from performances. Saulo Woonga, 18, did not want to come. His mother sent him after he got into a fight with another boy in their neighbourhood. “I was beating another guy,” he says. “So, my mum decided that ‘you need to go in the Shaolin Temple.’” Mathews Mafulu, also 18, arrived with a different problem. He was being bullied and, by his own admission, was lazy. Kung fu has changed him, he says, making him “jacked up, creative and a little strong”. Mafulu, who has lived at the temple for five years, does not see the Chinese presence around him as an intrusion. “It’s not like the Chinese are taking over Zambia,” Mafulu says. “It’s like exchanging cultures. We are learning new things from the Chinese and we are also teaching them new things about Africa.” Their early-morning routines, acrobatics, dragon dances and training sessions have drawn millions of views on TikTok and Douyin, China’s version of TikTok. Ronald Mwale is one of its biggest faces. The 26-year-old, who now speaks Chinese and goes by the Chinese name Hang Shao, has travelled to China four times and is preparing for a year-long stay there soon. His videos, chronicling life inside the temple, have made him a social media sensation, attracting some 615,000 followers on TikTok. Yet when he first arrived, he had little interest in China itself. “All I was interested in was training martial arts,” he says, watching younger students rehearse. Today, his ambitions stretch far beyond the training yard. He hopes to become an actor and dreams of following in the footsteps of performers from Henan province, the cradle of Shaolin kung fu and Zen Buddhism, where many of the temple’s traditions originated centuries ago. A few hours later, the training yard falls quiet and the students file silently into the temple. Dressed in orange and yellow robes, they bow shoulder to shoulder before Buddhist altars and begin chanting prayers beneath ornate ceilings painted in red, blue and gold. At the doorway, a handful of curious visitors stand quietly, phones raised as the students’ voices rise and fall in unison. For instructor Chen, who arrived in Zambia in 2022 after growing up in a poor community in China, the temple is about more than martial arts. “It gives them hope for their lives,” he says.

title: Trump calls Xi’s Washington visit ‘exciting’, but claims US leads China in AI race
description: US president praises Xi and predicts they have ‘a lot of good things to discuss’ at summit, while bragging of beating Beijing in tech war.
content: US President Donald Trump claimed on Wednesday that the US held a significant lead over China in artificial intelligence, touted what he termed unprecedented levels of inbound US investment and said he was thrilled about Chinese President Xi Jinping’s visit to Washington later this month. The president’s bravado comes as inflation and oil prices rise, his war of choice with Iran drags on and his polling numbers hit new lows ahead of the US midterm elections in November. “AI is going up, and we’re leading China in AI very substantially,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office. “By the way, we have the president of China coming on the 24th. That’ll be very exciting. Great, love to love to have him. A lot of good things to discuss, very, very productive things to discuss with President Xi.” Analysts say expectations are relatively low for meaningful deliverables or significant structural reform coming out of the September summit, similar to the May sit-down between Trump and Xi in Beijing. “I’m not hearing much,” said Zack Cooper, senior fellow with the conservative American Enterprise Institute, “because there’s not going to be much”. On Tuesday, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sharply criticised China for failing to sign on to a joint communique at the G20 Finance Ministers meeting this week in North Carolina. “Non-market-based economies pushing out a never-ending stream of cheap exports is not sustainable,” Bessent added. The transactional president also praised his administration’s record on attracting huge amounts of foreign investment, although analysts say some of the numbers are difficult to verify or involve pledges that are notional or easily reversed. “There’s never been a time when US$20 trillion dollars of investment is coming in, and the other number was by China many years ago, the previous record,” he said. “But this is a record that’s five times greater.” The Trump administration has recently entered into a trade war with Canada after talks collapsed late last month when Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney broke off negotiations, accusing the US of acting in bad faith with “unfair and uneconomic” late-stage changes. The US countered that Ottawa was abandoning prior commitments, with Trump calling Canadian negotiators “clowns” and “nasty people”. On Wednesday afternoon from the Oval Office, Trump said China was easier to negotiate with than America’s northern neighbour. “A lot of people say, ‘Who’s the toughest one to deal with? Is it China, sir? Is it China? Is it Vietnam?’ I said, ‘No, actually, it’s Canada’. Canada has felt emboldened. They had presidents that didn’t know what was happening. Not only the last one, all of them.” Later in the day, at a dinner in the Rose Garden, Trump suggested the Chinese president holds the US in high esteem in ways he did not under previous US presidents. “When President Xi comes in two weeks, he respects America now,” Trump said. The US commander-in-chief also said the renewed strikes against Iran were effective. “We knocked out a lot,” he said. “We now control the Hormuz Strait, and we have many boats going through that every day, every night. Many, many boats loaded up with oil.” Trump suggested that momentum in the six-month war, which he initially said would wrap up in four to five weeks, was with the US. “They’re not doing well at all,” he said. “And so it’s just a question of time. Just a question of time.” Wednesday’s event saw Trump surrounded by US travel executives as he celebrated a strong summer of travel in the USA, with 290 billion miles travelled on highways and 78 million visitors to national parks. The 2026 Fifa World Cup added US$18 billion to the economy and supported 160,000 jobs, he added. The president also said his administration would announce within the next 30 days details on an airspace software modernisation initiative, designed to replace legacy air traffic control infrastructure with real-time digital and AI-driven platforms. Trump has criticised the American people for their recent pushback over AI and the rapid spread of huge data centres. “The only reason that communities throughout the U.S.A. should not want Data Centres is if they want to end up being backwards and poor,” he said in a social media post Monday. “If they want to be successful and rich, with far lower taxes and jobs all over the place, let Data Reign.”

title: China’s new home finance rules reduce buyer risks but may not revive the market: analysts
description: Analysts say lower mortgage payments alone may not persuade buyers to jump in while prices remain under pressure.
content: China’s new housing finance rules reduce the risk of buying a new home but analysts are not convinced they will be enough to tempt hesitant buyers still weighed down by falling prices and weak confidence. The changes are designed to reduce the risk in buying pre-sold homes. Mortgage funds for pre-sold homes will be released only after submission of the project completion filing, when the homes are certified as safe and ready to move in, rather than when the main structure is finished. The maximum mortgage term has also been extended to 40 years from 30. The measures address a problem that emerged during China’s property downturn, when some buyers were left paying mortgages on homes that developers struggled to complete. But analysts said concerns about handover were only one factor behind the decline in home purchases. “I don’t think the primary goal of this reform is really to … stimulate property demand,” said Karl Choi, head of China property research at Bank of America. “It is [just] the right thing to do.” Choi said the reforms pointed to a move towards a system in which buyers had greater certainty about what they were purchasing. If homes were increasingly sold after completion, “what you see is what you get”, he said, adding that it also reduced the risk of unfinished projects. Whether this will translate into stronger sales is another question. Choi said weakness in the housing market was also linked to China’s economic outlook, job and income prospects, as well as expectations that prices could continue to fall. “If you’re worried that property prices will drop another 10 per cent, then chances are you [will] actually wait to buy,” Choi said. Fitch Ratings also expected that the changes would have limited effect on near-term demand, though they could improve project delivery and funding discipline. “Housing demand is likely to remain weak as the mortgage easing is unlikely to offset high inventory levels and low buyer confidence,” Fitch said in a report on Tuesday. Longer mortgage terms may lower monthly repayments, but Barclays noted in a report last week that they would also increase the total interest paid over the life of a loan. It added that demographic pressures, income expectations and high housing inventories would remain largely unchanged. Jeff Zhang, an equity analyst at Morningstar, shared the view that the new policies would have limited impact on boosting demand, but added they would “likely reshape the home supply and funding structures of developers”. He expected state-owned developers with strong liquidity and a larger presence in higher-tier cities to gain market share. A tighter land pipeline and a growing share of projects in central areas could also help stabilise home prices over time. Morningstar expected higher-tier cities to show earlier signs of recovery by the end of 2026, although restoring homebuyer confidence could take longer. The land market could provide one of the first indications of how the reforms were affecting the industry, according to Choi at Bank of America. “Between higher interest expenses and also lower asset turnover, there will already be a lot of pressure on developers’ earnings,” he said. “But the offset is that land prices should come down.”

title: US lawmakers target China, birth tourism as citizenship fight intensifies
description: Congressional hearings put Chinese birth tourism in the spotlight as the Trump administration presses its challenge to automatic citizenship.
content: US lawmakers targeted China and birth tourism on Wednesday for the second time this week during hearings on birthright citizenship, a constitutional right upheld by the Supreme Court in June but still under challenge from the Trump administration. “The demand for US citizenship for the children of Chinese nationals has led to unscrupulous companies assisting these individuals for profit,” said Chip Roy, a Republican from Texas. Wednesday’s Judiciary hearing was called to review June’s Supreme Court birthright decision in Trump vs Barbara and explore potential legislative responses. This followed Tuesday’s House Oversight session on birth tourism. Brandon Gill, a Republican from Texas, said on Tuesday that the concept of birthright citizenship is being exploited by foreign nationals, including those from adversarial nations such as China and Russia. “China is definitely an adversary to this nation [that] has worked in many ways to undermine us,” added Michael Cloud, another Texas Republican, responding to expert testimony. “We could spend a whole half an hour or hours actually on that.” Mary Gay Scanlon, a Democrat from Pennsylvania, said allegations surrounding birth tourism and “anchor babies” amounted to hallucinations. “Setting aside the fact that the Republicans’ own witnesses cannot show actual proof that birth tourism happens on any meaningful or widespread basis, any congressional response certainly does not involve upending constitutional fundamentals,” she added. The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform said in a press release on its website that nearly 26,000 babies are born annually to women on tourist visas, while an estimated 70,000 births in 2023 were to women in the US as temporary visitors. There is no federal dataset that measures birth tourism, with available estimates that vary widely, indicating the practice is rare. Penn State researchers estimated that birth tourism accounted for fewer than 0.3 per cent of all US births in any year from 2014 to 2024. Close to 3.6 million US births were registered in 2023, according to the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention. Even going with the Oversight Committee’s figures, births attributed to temporary visitors would represent less than 2 per cent of all US births that year. Public discussion often casts birth tourism as particularly widespread among wealthy Asians, the Penn State report said. But, it added, “the majority of birth tourists are Hispanic mothers”. Trump’s second term has seen him target both legal and illegal immigration, affecting nearly every part of the system, from restrictions on visas for skilled workers and students to an increased ICE presence. On Trump’s first day back in office in 2025, he signed an executive order that directed federal agencies not to recognise the citizenship of children born in the US when their parents were undocumented or present under temporary visas. The Supreme Court in Trump vs Barbara ruled 6–3 to block the executive order to restrict birthright citizenship. The ruling held that children born in the US to parents who are unlawfully or temporarily present are citizens at birth under the 14th Amendment. After the ruling, Trump took to social media to pen a sardonic post about China. “I would like to congratulate President Xi, and the Great Country of China, on their massive Birthright Citizenship WIN! President DONALD J. TRUMP,” Trump wrote. This week’s hearings come at a critical juncture in the Trump administration’s fight against birthright citizenship. Since the ruling, the federal government has made several attempts to continue challenging automatic citizenship as it stands today. In his latest push, Trump signed two executive orders in August. One of them directed officials to investigate suspected birth tourism operations, consider legal action against businesses facilitating such practices and strengthen visa screening. The other order sought to expand the categories of children who the government says are not entitled to birthright citizenship, directing federal agencies to examine remaining legal restrictions. On Wednesday, a federal judge blocked the Trump administration from carrying out the second order for now, saying the move was likely to be unlawful. US District Judge Deborah Boardman in Greenbelt, Maryland, issued a preliminary injunction at the request of immigrant rights advocates, noting that the president’s order was “almost certainly unconstitutional”. “The Supreme Court has spoken: children in the certified class are ‘citizens at birth’,” the judge said.

title: Meet Sophia Thomalla, TV star and girlfriend of US Open hopeful Alexander Zverev
description: Despite domestic abuse allegations against the reigning French Open champion by exes Olya Sharypova and Brenda Patea, Thomalla has remained steadfastly supportive.
content: German tennis star Alexander Zverev just pulled off an epic first-round win at the 2026 US Open. The top seed beat Italy’s Lorenzo Sonego 6-4, 3-6, 6-7 (7), 7-5, 6-4 in a match that lasted four hours and 53 minutes, finishing at 1:55 am on Wednesday in New York. “I’m just happy I won,” the French Open title holder said in a post-match interview with the ATP Tour. “Incredible battle. A lot of ups and downs. Nearly five hours for a first round. I think this is the longest first-round match I’ve ever played in my life.” Zverev, who reached the Wimbledon final in July, came close to winning his first US Open men’s singles title in 2020, but ultimately lost to Dominic Thiem. “I still feel like I should have won in 2020, that doesn’t change,” he said at a press conference last week. “I feel like I’m one of the 128 players that are favourites in the draw,” he added. Through his ups and downs, the 29-year-old star athlete has had one familiar face in his player’s box: his girlfriend of over five years, Sophia Thomalla. Here’s everything you need to know about her. What is Sophia Thomalla’s background? Sophia Thomalla was born in East Berlin on October 6, 1989, to actor parents Simone Thomalla and André Vetters, who separated in 1995. She spent her early childhood in Berlin before relocating to Cologne and Kleinmachnow with her mother. Known for her striking body art, Thomalla began getting tattooed at a young age – with one statement piece featuring the name and birth date of actor Sven Martinek, who dated her mother in the late 1990s, per German tabloid Klatsch-Tratsch. She’s a TV personality Thomalla followed her parents into showbiz and established herself as an entertainer. She studied at the Konstantin School of Drama in Bochum and is best known for hosting Germany’s adaptation of the popular dating show Are You the One?. She won the German version of the reality series Let’s Dance in 2010 and has appeared in German television shows like Commissario Laurenti, Der Bergdoktor, and Eine wie Keine. Thomalla also enjoys kickboxing, owns the liquor brand Hardkorn Spirits, and is an ambassador for and shareholder in the construction-tech company Schüttflix. Who else has Sophia Thomalla dated? Thomalla’s famous exes include Rammstein frontman Till Lindemann, for whom she has multiple tattoos. The 36-year-old also dated English musician Gavin Rossdale, the lead singer of Bush, and was married to Norwegian singer Andy LaPlegua, founder of the band Icon of Coil. Before dating Zverev, she was linked to German footballer Loris Karius – the former Liverpool goalkeeper who now plays for FC Schalke 04. Thomalla and Zverev began dating in 2020. “Sophia is someone who gives me peace and security. I play extremely well with her behind me,” the Hamburg-born tennis star told Tennis Magazin. Despite domestic abuse allegations made against Zverev by his former partners Olya Sharypova and Brenda Patea – which he has denied – Thomalla has remained steadfast in her support.

title: In Focus | Chinese students, wary of geopolitics, seek international diplomas without leaving home
description: China’s growing number of educational joint ventures receive more applicants as students seek a simpler path to an international edge.
content: One Shanghai family made an unconventional choice as they pored over college options this summer: rather than opting for overseas study or one of the many institutions within the borders of the financial centre, they picked a lesser-known university in a third-tier city – a Sino-foreign joint venture they felt would confer career benefits in the long run. Rose Hu said her son gained admission to the Guangdong Technion–Israel Institute of Technology in the coastal city of Shantou to study mechanical engineering and robotics, a field he was passionate about, and one deemed to have strong job prospects. “The biggest attraction of this institution to us is where graduates end up,” Hu said. “Most go on to top master’s programmes in the United States, the United Kingdom or Hong Kong, which aligns perfectly with our plan – we’re committed to science, technology, engineering and mathematics and intend for our son to pursue a graduate degree at a renowned university. “Tuition is also reasonable for a regular family. If he studied abroad, it could cost 10 times more.” Hu said studying at the institute cost 100,000 yuan (US$14,826) a year, but those costs would be significantly defrayed with a 40,000-yuan scholarship. The family made their decision amid a period of explosive growth in higher education joint ventures in China. In May, the Ministry of Education approved more than 80 new joint institutions and over 130 joint programmes at the bachelor’s degree level and above. That followed a boom last year that saw more than 100 institutions gain approval. By early this year, the national total exceeded 320. Like Hu’s son, an increasing number of Chinese students are being lured by these programmes, which allow them to earn a relatively cheap international degree without straying far from home, or becoming embroiled in rising geopolitical tensions. Choosing this institution gives us a clear path in tech-related fields Rose Hu, Shanghai The programmes are also seeing growing interest from international students – mainly from countries involved in the Belt and Road Initiative trade development plan, where Chinese companies are investing and hiring more, according to industry insiders. They said the trend could dovetail well with China’s efforts to stimulate its economy and compensate for a drop in domestic student enrolments. “I think the overall number of Chinese students studying overseas is likely to shrink in the next few years,” said Zhang Wuhua, chairman of Shanghai-headquartered Ambright Education, which operates schools that prepare students for overseas education. “This is not due to diminished interest or need, but largely a measured response to concerns including persistent geopolitical volatility. “At the same time, the number of students pursuing a ‘study-abroad’ experience through Sino-foreign cooperative programmes and institutions without leaving China will keep growing.” There were 570,600 Chinese students studying overseas last year, down about 20 per cent from the 2019 peak, according to figures released by the Ministry of Education in April – the first issuance of these numbers since the Covid-19 pandemic. The emerging alternatives offered by Sino-foreign joint institutions align well with the in-demand academic disciplines of science and engineering, a major consideration for Chinese families focused on job prospects and concerned about the higher risks and less rosy career outlooks faced by those studying overseas. By the end of last year, engineering programmes accounted for 48 per cent of these cooperative education initiatives, according to a report released by the Hurun Research Institute in June. Nearly 60 per cent of the Sino-foreign cooperative institutions and programmes that gained approval last year were concentrated in emerging interdisciplinary fields such as artificial intelligence, big data, new energy, bioengineering and advanced manufacturing, Hurun said. Hu said her son was now studying at the institute in Shantou and was enjoying the “international” experience there. All his lecturers except for one were foreigners. “Choosing this institution gives us a clear path in tech-related fields: if his academic performance is not outstanding, he will find a job at a technology firm in the Greater Bay Area after graduation, and if he excels, he can pursue a master’s degree at a more prestigious university overseas,” she said. Sun Yat-sen University’s Lingnan College in Guangzhou launched a full international undergraduate programme taught in English this year. Under its inbound “two plus two” model, students will complete their first two years abroad and then attend Lingnan College for the final two years. One of the first of its kind, the model is expected to help bring international students to China for the later years of their undergraduate degrees, in contrast to the more common outbound “two plus two” model for Chinese students going abroad. “The emergence of this model means that China’s international education is gradually shifting, from a one-way flow of ‘students going abroad’ to a ‘two-way flow of educational resources’,” Zhang said. Lingnan College said in June that the programme was targeting students in countries taking part in the Belt and Road Initiative as a response to “the accelerating overseas expansion of Chinese firms and their urgent need for cross-cultural talent versed in local markets and the Chinese model”. “The motivation is very practical,” Zhang said. “As Chinese companies expand overseas and increase investment in their countries, local annual salaries are often higher than those offered by Japanese and Korean firms. “They hope to increase their chances of entering these companies by studying in China, solidifying their language skills, gaining practical social experience and understanding the knowledge structure that Chinese enterprises require.” These students previously had to choose between Western and Chinese universities, but Zhang said the emergence of Sino-foreign cooperative education means they no longer have to struggle with that choice. For example, if they attended the University of Nottingham Ningbo China, they would receive a University of Nottingham diploma without leaving the country. Domestic universities were also motivated to launch cooperative programmes, largely as a way to improve their difficult financial situations, said Chu Zhaohui, a senior researcher at the National Institute of Education Sciences. Chinese students going abroad spend tens of billions of yuan every year – why not keep that spending within the country? Zhang Wuhua, Ambright Education At Zhejiang University, for example, tuition fees for regular undergraduate programmes ranged from 5,000 to 6,000 yuan per academic year, but one of its cooperative programmes, the Zhejiang University-University of Edinburgh Institute, charged students from China 160,000 yuan a year. In addition, local governments also provided financial support for cooperative education, which was something universities could not afford to miss out on. “Many universities are currently facing financial problems, with some even unable to pay salaries,” Chu said, adding that he believed the rapid expansion of cooperative education in the past couple of years had primarily been driven by government policy. “This is written into the 15th five-year plan, and there are assessment requirements for universities,” he said. According to China’s education plan for the period from 2026 to 2030, authorities will encourage high-quality foreign universities specialising in science and engineering to set up cooperative programmes in China, and launch international talent development initiatives for outstanding students. Zhang said one of the motivations for that drive was the need to boost domestic economic circulation. “From an economic perspective, Chinese students going abroad spend tens of billions of yuan every year – why not keep that spending within the country?” he said. “And from an educational perspective, it relates to China’s ongoing commitment to opening up.” And overseas students could help fill lecture theatres. In an article published in China Higher Education magazine last year, a Ministry of Education official said university enrolment was expected to peak in 2032. Zhang said: “If we lay the groundwork now, then when the number of Chinese students declines, we will have a large number of overseas students to fill the gap – so this is an arrangement with strategic foresight.” But he warned that the quality of international students being recruited was a concern. He said students in Europe or Southeast Asia tended to regard China’s top universities – which Chinese students fought tooth and nail to get into – as safety options, because the admission threshold for international students at Chinese universities was very low. “They would say, ‘If I can’t get into a local school, then I’ll go to Tsinghua in China’, which is something really sad for our universities,” Zhang said. The Chinese government launched the China Scholastic Competence Assessment exam for international students at the end of last year. Zhang said the National Higher Education Entrance Examination taken by domestic high school students was more than twice as difficult, but even so, placement tests at top universities like Nanjing University and Fudan University found that “a large number” of international students scored just 30 to 40 points out of 100 in mathematics.

title: Opinion | 3 key belt and road connectivities that Hong Kong drives
description: Hong Kong’s Belt and Road Office is focusing on strengthening links related to infrastructure, rules and standards, and people-to-people connections.
content: Recently, I joined Secretary for Commerce and Economic Development Algernon Yau Ying-wah in Malaysia for the official opening of the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Office in Kuala Lumpur. The occasion marked an elevation in Hong Kong’s economic and trade ties with Malaysia and the broader Southeast Asian region. During the visit, Hong Kong’s Belt and Road Office hosted a forum that brought government officials, business leaders and professionals together for substantive discussions – underscoring Hong Kong’s practical role as a functional platform for Belt and Road Initiative cooperation. The Belt and Road Office continues to coordinate efforts that strengthen “hard connectivity” in infrastructure, “soft connectivity” in rules and standards, and “people-to-people connectivity” with belt and road partner countries. Through all-round connectivity, Hong Kong is deepening our participation in high-quality belt and road cooperation across multiple fields. On hard connectivity, the Belt and Road Office actively engages the project authorities in partner countries and regions to build a structured cooperation platform. This platform identifies opportunities for Hong Kong companies and professional services to participate in both major and “small but beautiful” projects. We also organise outbound missions that bring diverse sectors together to explore belt and road opportunities. In June this year, Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu led a business delegation to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, advancing Hong Kong’s comprehensive engagement with Central Asian economies. The visit yielded strong results, with 96 cooperation agreements and memorandums of understanding signed, covering projects valued at more than US$1.65 billion. The Belt and Road Office concluded memorandums with key institutions in both countries, laying solid groundwork for collaboration. We will encourage the relevant project authorities to conduct roadshows or release information in Hong Kong, enabling local enterprises to connect more precisely with these opportunities. At the same time, we have brought major events from belt and road countries to Hong Kong. For instance, LEAP East, a premier global tech event, left the Middle East for the first time and chose Hong Kong as its host – positioning the city as a new international stage for technology exchange. Soft connectivity in rules and standards serves as a vital pillar of high-quality belt and road cooperation. The Belt and Road Office has brought together more than 20 public organisations and institutions as Hong Kong belt and road capacity-building platforms. The platforms deliver training for personnel from partner countries across transport and logistics, financial services, legal services, development and construction, environment and ecology, innovation and technology, health and integrity. In doing so, the office facilitates the alignment of rules and standards and fosters understanding. This April, we convened the Seminar on Belt and Road Capacity Building Platforms to strengthen collaboration among participating institutions, and share Hong Kong’s governance experience and professional expertise. People-to-people bonds form the foundation of genuine connectivity. We are building a shared belt and road talent pool. More than 6,000 students from belt and road countries are studying at Hong Kong’s universities, and around 400 undertook internships in the city last summer – helping to develop the human capital needed for multilateral cooperation. On the cultural front, the Asia+ Festival runs from September to November each year, celebrating the cultural diversity of Asia, and belt and road countries. This year’s edition will bring together more than 30 countries and regions, and feature over 100 performances and activities, creating vibrant cross-regional artistic dialogue. In parallel, major cultural exhibitions from Qatar and Egypt have been presented at the Hong Kong Palace Museum, while collaborations with Uzbekistan are advancing, allowing Silk Road civilisations to converge in Hong Kong and promoting learning among cultures. The Belt and Road Summit remains Hong Kong’s flagship economic and trade platform for belt and road cooperation. The 10th edition last year drew 6,200 participants from more than 70 countries and regions, and facilitated cooperation agreements which, together with new projects and deals finalised before the summit, approached US$1 billion in value. The 11th Belt and Road Summit takes place on September 9-10 under the theme “Advancing High-Quality Development: Embarking on a New Journey”. For the first time, the programme will include a dedicated “Go Global Chapter”. The summit will also highlight opportunities in Central Asia and the Middle East, as well as emerging areas such as the low-altitude economy. Belt and road signature project sessions will continue, enabling precise matching between enterprises and projects. We warmly invite stakeholders from all sectors to join us and share in the opportunities. Hong Kong will continue to serve as both a “superconnector” and “super value-adder” between the mainland and the rest of the world. From delivering projects under hard connectivity, to aligning rules through soft connectivity, to bringing people closer through people-to-people bonds, Hong Kong is contributing our distinctive strengths – through practical action – to the building of a community with a shared future for mankind.

title: Trump ‘happy’ Prince Harry and Meghan left US: ‘I was not a fan’
description: The US president says the couple treated the UK royal family with ‘great disrespect’.
content: US President ⁠Donald Trump said on Wednesday that he was “happy” Prince Harry and his family left the US and relocated back to Britain. “I am happy about it. I was not a fan,” Trump said in the Oval Office when asked about the recent decision ‌by Harry and Meghan, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, to leave California after six years. The family arrived back in Britain at the end of August. The couple stepped down from official royal duties in 2020 when they moved to the US. “I thought they treated the royal family with great disrespect. I didn’t like ⁠it,” Trump said, mentioning his “good relationship” with the late Queen Elizabeth and her successor King Charles, ‌who is undergoing treatment for cancer. The president specifically criticised Meghan. “I didn’t like the way she acted. I thought she was terribly disrespectful,” ‌he said. After the couple’s move to the US, Harry in an Oprah interview accused ⁠the royal family ⁠of neglect. Meghan, whose mother is black and father is white, said that when she was pregnant with ‌her son there were “concerns and conversations about how dark his skin might be when he’s born” within the royal family. Prince ‌William, Harry’s ‌older brother, defended the family after the accusation and said “we’re not racist”. Harry also cited ‌press scrutiny and the government’s failure to provide security for his family as reasons ⁠for moving to California. Now back in Britain, Harry and Meghan are expected to remain non-working royals. A ⁠person close to the couple said last month that the family planned to move somewhere outside London for an extended period with their children, Prince Archie, seven, ‌and Princess Lilibet, five, who ‌will go to school in Britain. It is unclear what changed for the couple, but Harry has said he wants his children to spend time in Britain. “If I were the royal family, I would not have taken them back,” Trump added on Wednesday.

title: Dutch shift 86 tonnes of gold from US and Canada to London, citing ‘geopolitical unrest’
description: DNB moves reserves to boost liquidity in crisis response as analysts warn widespread shifts could dent confidence in US.
content: The Dutch central bank said Wednesday it had moved 86 tonnes of its gold reserves out of the US and Canada to London, citing “increasing geopolitical unrest”. The DNB bank said gold reserves held in London could be traded more easily than those held in New York and Ottawa. “This makes it the quickest for DNB to deploy in a crisis situation,” the bank said in a statement. “With this step, we have improved the deployability of the gold reserves. We assume that we will never need to deploy the gold, but it is nevertheless necessary to strengthen our resilience and preparedness,” DNB President Olaf Sleijpen said. The total Dutch gold stock amounted to 612.4 tonnes and was valued at €72.2 billion (US$83.7 billion) at the end of 2025, the DNB said. Before the deployment, the Dutch bank held 31.3 per cent of its gold in New York and 19.7 per cent in Ottawa. After the move, each country accounted for 18.5 per cent of the Dutch gold reserve. The share of gold held in London increased from 18.1 per cent to 32.1 per cent. The bank still holds 30.8 per cent of its gold in the Netherlands. The transfer was carried out partially by buying and selling and partly by physically transferring gold, the bank said. The bank moved more than 27 tonnes of physical gold from the US and Canada to Zeist. The same quantity of gold was moved from Zeist to London, preventing the melting down of gold bars. “By combining buying and selling and physical transport, the risks associated with physically moving a large quantity of gold have been spread,” the DNB said. The operation took place between March and August of this year, the bank said. Laurent Schwartz, president of the Paris-based National Gold Counter, which facilitates gold trading in France, said central banks had been moving their reserves around for about a decade. “The current political context in the United States might also push certain central banks into favouring other storage locations,” Schwartz said. The London market is the deepest and most liquid, Schwartz said, making it easier to deploy in times of crisis. “Central banks can more easily lend their gold there to other banking institutions,” he added. John Plassard, analyst at Cite Gestion Private Bank, said the Dutch move was intended “for there to be more immediate availability in the event of a crisis”. For the moment, it was a “fairly one-off move” but he warned that if other central banks followed suit, it could damage confidence in the US. At the beginning of the year, there were concerns raised in Germany about the security of their central bank’s reserves in New York. However, the powerful Bundesbank has decided for the moment not to shift its reserves away from New York. “The New York Fed is and remains an important storage site for our gold,” the bank told public television station ARD in January.

title: Tiger Woods gets 5-year driving ban after plea deal over rollover crash in Florida
description: Legendary golfer initially pleaded not guilty to a driving under the influence charge after the crash near his home in March.
content: Tiger Woods has been banned from driving for five years ⁠after reaching a plea deal ⁠on Wednesday related to his impaired-driving case. The ⁠15-time major champion, who initially pleaded not guilty, was present for the change-of-plea hearing when Judge Darren Steele said two five-year driving licence suspensions will run at the same time: one on a reckless driving charge and one on a careless driving citation. The 50-year-old Woods, who was also handed fines, has 30 days to appeal against the ruling. Woods also pleaded no contest to refusing to submit to testing and was fined court costs, according to court documents. A no-contest plea is not an admission of guilt, but means the accused will offer no defence. The plea is treated as a conviction in the criminal justice system. “There are no exceptions. If ‌you were to drive for any reason at all, you would go immediately back to jail,” Steele told the court. Woods, dressed in a dark suit and tie, arrived at the Martin County Courthouse seated in the front passenger seat of a black SUV and did not answer questions from the gathered reporters as he and ⁠girlfriend Vanessa Trump, US President Donald Trump’s former daughter-in-law, walked in and out of the building for the 8.30am change of plea ‌hearing. Woods, regarded as the greatest golfer of his generation, initially pleaded not guilty to driving under the influence charges stemming from his rollover crash in March. At the time, Woods ‌told authorities he was looking down at his phone and did not realise the truck in ⁠front of him had ⁠slowed down before his crash. No one was injured in the crash. According to a probable cause affidavit, Woods had two hydrocodone pills in his ‌pocket and officers observed him to be lethargic, slow, “sweating profusely”, with eyes that were bloodshot and glassy, and pupils that were “extremely dilated”. Steele had granted Woods’ ‌request to ‌travel outside the United States to receive treatment in a controlled environment and, in a March statement, the ‌golfer said he was stepping away to seek treatment and focus on his health. In May, the judge granted prosecutors’ ⁠request to subpoena Woods’ prescription drug records, covering a period from the start of 2026 to March 27, the ⁠day Woods’ Land Rover rolled over on a two-lane road near his Jupiter Island home in Florida. In July, the judge granted a similar request that allowed prosecutors to obtain hospital records connected to ‌the golfer’s medical treatment following ‌his crash. Woods has won 15 major championships, second only to Jack Nicklaus with 18. He also has won 82 PGA Tour events, a record he shares with Sam Snead. He spent a record 683 weeks as world No 1 and is the only player to have held all four major titles at the same time, a feat known as the “Tiger Slam”.

title: Amid war with Iran, Trump muses renaming Hormuz as ‘Trump Strait’
description: White House shares rebranded Gulf map as US president warns renewed air campaign against Iran will not last ‘too long’.
content: US President Donald Trump on Wednesday suggested renaming the Strait of Hormuz as “Trump Strait” despite ongoing clashes with Iran – then hours later implied he wasn’t serious. Trump has made a series of geographical name changes to international bodies of water in his second term, at least partly with the aim of trolling other countries. The latest suggestion came as Trump insisted the US had full control of the crucial waterway, even as fresh clashes raged there with Iran. “Now that we have it under U.S.A. control, should we change the name Hormuz Strait to TRUMP STRAIT??? Like America itself, it would be ‘hotter’ than ever before!” Trump said on his Truth Social network. The White House later posted a map of the Gulf on social media with his suggested name, adding: “It’s got a nice ring to it”. Trump has in recent weeks repeatedly threatened to claim sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz, even posting a map showing the waterway as a “new US territory”. It's got a nice ring to it pic.twitter.com/Fmzc9iUu8u — The White House (@WhiteHouse) September 2, 2026 Trump, however, later played down the idea of rebranding the Strait of Hormuz. “It was just thrown out there,” Trump said with a chuckle after an Agence France-Presse reporter asked him in the Oval Office if he was serious about renaming it. But a number of the 80-year-old Republican’s previous suggestions have been dismissed as being humorous before they ended up happening for real. Last week Trump signed an order renaming Lake Ontario as “Lake America” amid a trade war with neighbouring Canada, just days after apparently raising the idea in jest. Trump also renamed the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America” on his first day back in the White House in January 2025. Neither Mexico nor Canada have accepted the changes. He has also gone on a spree of renaming things after himself, including the Kennedy arts centre in Washington, while the US Treasury meanwhile on Wednesday issued US$1 coins featuring Trump’s face to mark the 250th anniversary of US independence. The Iran war remains a deadly serious issue, with no sign of ending more than six months after the initial US-Israeli assault. Fighting has flared again after weeks of calm, with US forces launching fresh strikes near the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday in response to what Trump said were new minelaying efforts by Iran. Iran said one of the US strikes killed four people at a wedding, branding it a “war crime”, and launched a wave of retaliatory strikes at US bases in Jordan, the UAE, Kuwait, Bahrain and Iraq. At home, Trump has presided over a steep rise in US fuel costs as a result of the war and his Republican Party looks likely to lose at least partial control of Congress in the November midterm elections. Iran has effectively shut down the choke point, through which a fifth of the world’s oil passes, in retaliation for the war Trump started along with Israel in late February. Trump said on Wednesday that the United States was ready to attack Iran again – while adding that the renewed campaign would not last “too long.” “It was a very heavy attack last night, and we’re prepared to do another one any time we want,” Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.

title: Vietnam arrests deputy minister over probe into huge bribes
description: Tran Van Thuan’s arrest comes as police investigate a scheme involving ‘smuggling’ and reselling of medical equipment at inflated prices.
content: Vietnamese police arrested a deputy health minister on Wednesday for allegedly accepting huge bribes, part of an investigation into a company accused of smuggling medical equipment, authorities said. Vietnam has pursued a high-profile anti-corruption campaign in recent years that has netted dozens of business leaders and senior government figures. Deputy Health Minister Tran Van Thuan, a leading oncologist in Vietnam, was taken into custody “due to his acceptance of bribes involving a large sum of money”, the public security ministry said in a statement, without specifying the amount. Thuan, 56, was appointed deputy health minister in 2020 and chairman of the National Medical Council in 2024. His arrest came as part of a police investigation involving “smuggling” and “violations of accounting regulations causing serious consequences” at Viet My Medical Investment Joint Stock Company, the ministry’s statement said. Police have arrested two executives and an accountant at the firm, which was allegedly set up to trade, resell and inflate the prices of medical equipment and pharmaceuticals before importing them from Singapore and Hong Kong into Vietnam, state media said. Police also accuse company leaders of attempting to illegally import medical equipment. Vietnam’s sweeping anti-corruption drive, accelerated by President To Lam, has removed many of his opponents, according to analysts, leaving him as the country’s most dominant leader in decades. In May, former health minister Nguyen Thi Kim Tien was imprisoned for six years over her mismanagement of hospital projects, state media said. Tien was embroiled in corruption scandals in previous years and was once voted the least popular official by lawmakers in the one-party state.

title: 2 Filipino sailors killed in Iran’s attack on vessel, Saudi Arabia says
description: Iran has threatened tankers attempting ⁠to sail through the Strait of Hormuz without authorisation, impeding energy exports from the Gulf.
content: Saudi Arabia, the world’s biggest crude exporter, said on Wednesday that an Iranian ‌attack on an oil tanker owned by its national shipping company had killed two Filipino seafarers. Sidr, owned by Bahri, was one of two supertankers carrying Saudi oil reported to have been hit late on Monday while transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Tehran has threatened tankers attempting ⁠to sail through the narrow waterway without authorisation, impeding energy exports from neighbouring ‌oil-rich Gulf countries. About one-fifth of global oil and liquefied natural gas trade used to pass through the Strait of ‌Hormuz before the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran on ⁠February 28. Bahri ⁠said the seafarers were killed in a security incident involving Sidr at 11.40pm local time on Monday. “The kingdom stressed the necessity of halting escalations, and respecting international maritime safety and ‌the ‌security of global energy supplies,” the Saudi foreign ministry said. “Bahri remains in ‌continuous contact with the vessel and is coordinating closely with the relevant ⁠authorities and maritime industry stakeholders, while continuing to closely monitor developments,” the company ⁠said in a statement. In July, another Bahri vessel, the Wedyan supertanker, was hit while passing through the strait close to Oman’s ‌coast. Two other Bahri ‌vessels, Masa and Amzan, were attacked in the Red Sea in July and August after the Iran-backed Yemen’s Houthis declared a naval blockade against Saudi Arabia. Meanwhile, Iran targeted Gulf allies of the United States on Wednesday, firing drones at Kuwait and Bahrain after a night of US aerial bombardment of Iran. Iranian officials said one of the US strikes on the country overnight struck a wedding party, leaving at least four people dead and dozens wounded. Fighting between the US and Iran has increased this week after the US hit Iranian rocket launchers on an island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, saying Iran was planning to use them to shoot mines into the waterway. Iran retaliated by firing missiles at American bases in Jordan, which were all intercepted. Additional reporting by Associated Press

title: SCO takes landmark stand on nuclear security as Iran comes under renewed attack
description: The bloc underscores members’ rights to peaceful nuclear development in broader pushback at Western powers, analyst says.
content: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation has issued its first dedicated declaration on nuclear safety and security, condemning attacks on peaceful nuclear facilities and outlining practical cooperation, amid tensions over Iran’s nuclear programme and wider questions of global nuclear governance. The document was adopted on Tuesday at the bloc’s 25th anniversary summit in Bishkek by leaders of all 10 member states – China, Russia, India, Pakistan, Iran, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Uzbekistan and Belarus. It called for stronger cooperation on regulation, emergency response and the fight against illicit trafficking of nuclear materials, while reaffirming that nuclear security responsibility rested entirely with each state. It also underscored members’ rights to the peaceful use of nuclear energy under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty. Zhu Yongbiao, director of the Centre for Afghanistan Studies at Lanzhou University, pointed to several converging factors behind its adoption: China and Russia’s long-standing interest in deeper cooperation; growing demand for safety frameworks as civilian nuclear programmes expand in Central Asia, particularly Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan; and Iran’s full membership since 2023. Zhu said it heightened concern over nuclear risks amid the Iran conflict and the Israel–Palestine situation, and regional unease over Japan’s nuclear waste water discharge, but the new document was not an abrupt reaction to recent US-Israeli strikes on Iran’s nuclear facilities. “Similar initiatives had already been circulating within the organisation,” Zhu said. The proposal was first raised at the bloc’s 2025 Tianjin summit by Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, who called for a declaration to support peaceful nuclear energy, emergency response and the global non‑proliferation regime. In his summit speech on Tuesday, Chinese President Xi Jinping explicitly endorsed strengthening nuclear safety partnerships and linked them to China’s Global Security Initiative. “We believe in a sensible, coordinated, and balanced approach to nuclear security, and support a stronger multilateral partnership for nuclear safety and security,” he said, framing the declaration within a broader agenda that prioritises “common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security”. Xi told fellow leaders that the SCO must “stay committed to taking security as a key goal and foster an environment of common security”, while urging the early opening of four SCO security centres to boost members’ capacity against threats ranging from terrorism to cyberattacks. Russian President Vladimir Putin underscored the issue of sovereignty, insisting that nuclear safety must remain under national control and denouncing what he called Western “double standards”. The declaration stated that responsibility for nuclear safety rested with facility operators and the host state, echoing long-standing International Atomic Energy Agency principles. Member states voiced “deep concern” over the illicit trafficking of nuclear and radioactive materials, threats to nuclear facilities and infrastructure – including cyber risks – and the danger of nuclear terrorism. Without naming Iran, the text said members “resolutely condemn any attacks or threats of attacks against peaceful nuclear facilities, deeming such acts a violation of international law”, and called for restraint, de-escalation and a political settlement. The language echoed the broader Bishkek Declaration adopted at the close of the SCO summit the same day, which explicitly supported Iran’s sovereignty, condemned military strikes on Iranian territory and civilians, and opposed unilateral coercive measures. The nuclear document also outlined practical steps, including regulatory exchanges, stronger domestic control systems, joint research and training, physical protection upgrades, radioactive waste management, radiation monitoring, early‑warning data sharing and personnel development. The declaration came amid stalled US-Russia arms control talks and Washington’s reported review of its nuclear posture to expand tactical options in potential regional conflicts with Russia or China, after the last remaining bilateral treaty, New Start, expired in February this year without a successor. Washington has pressed Beijing to join trilateral arms control talks with Moscow, a proposal China has rejected as disproportionate given the size of its arsenal relative to the US and Russia. At the same time, US officials have accused China of expanding its stockpile without sufficient transparency over missile tests and alleged secret nuclear experiments, charges Beijing has dismissed as “groundless”. Li Lifan, an expert on Russia and Central Asia at the Shanghai Academy of Social Sciences, said the declaration’s emphasis on sovereign control, peaceful use and resistance to unilateral measures reflected a broader pushback against what he called “nuclear hegemony” by Western powers. “China’s stance on nuclear issues has remained consistent, avoiding the kind of practices and thinking often associated with Western approaches,” he said. The document’s stress on the peaceful use of nuclear energy also aligned with Beijing’s long-standing position, Li added. “China has been consistent in its opposition to the first use of nuclear weapons proposed by countries including Russia. This also represents China’s attitude towards nuclear deterrence,” he said. But Zhu cautioned against overreading the declaration as a direct challenge to Western initiatives. “Its intent lies more in asserting autonomy than direct rivalry,” he said. The SCO, he noted, was seeking to “shape perceptions and nuclear safety norms grounded in international law, global order, and members’ own interests, while projecting a unified non‑Western voice in global governance”. He said it was noteworthy that despite differing views among members about relations with the US and Israel, the SCO nonetheless reaffirmed collective support for Iran’s sovereignty and opposition to the use of force against members. “In essence, ‘supporting member sovereignty plus opposing attacks on peaceful nuclear facilities’ has become the broadest consensus within the SCO,” Zhu said.

title: Israel ready to remove Palestinians in Gaza once US approves, minister says
description: Defence Minister Israel Katz says there is ‘no real solution’ without migration and that Trump’s displacement plan is ‘frozen’.
content: Israel has plans ready to remove Palestinians from the Gaza Strip but is waiting for the United States to figure out where to take them, the defence minister has said. “There is no real solution for Gaza in the end without this migration,” Defence Minister Israel Katz told a conference hosted by Israeli news site Ynet and newspaper Yedioth Ahronoth on Wednesday. The Israeli government “is organised and prepared to get them out – by sea, by air, by every way possible”, he said. The US embassy referred requests for comment to the State Department in Washington. US President Donald Trump, at the start of his second term, stunned much of the world by calling for all two million Palestinians to leave the Gaza Strip. Trump spoke of developing the Mediterranean territory, devastated by Israeli bombardment since the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas, into a luxury resort destination. Trump walked back the idea following strong pushback, including from Egypt, the only country other than Israel to border Gaza. The proposal was also condemned by Palestinians themselves, for whom any effort to force them off their land would recall the Nakba, or catastrophe – their mass displacement during Israel’s creation in 1948. Announcing a Gaza war ceasefire in October, Trump laid out 20 points for the territory that included no forced displacement. Katz, known for his outspoken remarks, said that Trump had only “frozen” the idea as he looked for countries to take in Palestinians, as Egypt was not an option. “The plan hasn’t been cancelled; it is being discussed all the time, even now, and I think there is no other solution for everyone’s good,” he said. “But for it to happen, we need the US. When will we get their approval? Whenever it becomes clear that Hamas is not meeting its obligations” under the ceasefire, he added. Katz, without citing his source, said 80 per cent of people in Gaza wanted to leave but that Hamas was preventing them. Forced displacement of civilians in occupied territory is considered a war crime under the Geneva Conventions. The International Criminal Court has issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Katz’s predecessor Yoav Gallant over alleged war crimes, which both Israel and the US deny. Israeli attacks have already internally displaced the vast majority of Gaza’s people following the unprecedented Hamas attack, which killed 1,221 people, according to official Israeli figures. Israel’s offensive has since claimed 73,470 lives in Gaza, with more than 1,330 since the ceasefire, according to the Gaza health ministry, which operates under Hamas.

title: Hong Kong police arrest 2 from clinic over sales of bogus ‘cancer vaccine’
description: Authorities seize more than 50 unregistered injections in investigation into product marketed as vaccine against more than 20 types of cancer.
content: Hong Kong authorities have arrested a man and woman from a clinic on suspicion of selling a laboratory reagent as a bogus vaccine against more than 20 types of cancer. The arrests followed a joint operation by the Department of Health and police, during which investigators raided 13 premises linked to the company, said Frank Chan Ling-fung, an assistant director of health who oversees drug matters. Chan said there had been no reports of illness among people who had received the “WT1 cancer vaccine”. While WT1 refers to a legitimate protein target being studied in cancer research, the case involved patients allegedly being injected with a German laboratory chemical containing the protein that is only for research purposes. The chemical is not registered as a medicine anywhere in the world. Authorities seized more than 50 unregistered injections, most of them vitamin-type health products. The injections were classified as Part I poisons under local law. The clinic had previously come under official scrutiny after media reports exposed its alleged illegal practices. Reports said the clinic and its affiliates promoted the WT1 jab on mainland Chinese platforms, advertising injections in Hong Kong for HK$120,000 (US$15,305). Chan said undercover officers had been told that the injections cost five-figure sums. He added that the man, 28, who was in charge of the clinic, and the woman remained in custody and further arrests could follow. Media outlets reported five years ago that a manager at the clinic and another employee allegedly smuggled unregistered immune-cell therapy injections into the city, administering them to celebrities and regular residents. Asked why no action had been taken over the past five years, and whether the case had been referred to the Medical Council, Chan told reporters to direct their questions to the watchdog for the sector. Chan said the Department of Health had ordered local advertising publishers to remove related promotions that might have breached the Undesirable Medical Advertisements Ordinance. For advertisements on mainland platforms, Hong Kong authorities had notified regulators over the border and requested the posts’ removal.

title: Man arrested over theft of HK$5,885 in foreign currency on Bangkok to Hong Kong flight
description: Suspect allegedly walked from back of plane to open overhead storage compartment at front of cabin and rummaged through bag, source says.
content: Hong Kong police have arrested a man on suspicion of stealing nearly HK$6,000 (US$770) in foreign currency while flying to the city from Thailand, with a passenger allegedly capturing the incident on camera and reporting it to cabin crew. The force said the 57-year-old man was arrested for the alleged theft after the HK Express flight landed in the city shortly before midnight on Wednesday. While police estimated the currency was worth about HK$6,000, a source put the amount at 25,000 baht, which is equivalent to HK$5,885. The insider said the suspect had allegedly walked from the back of the plane to open an overhead storage compartment at the front of the cabin. “He was rummaging through a black bag, and took away cash from the bag, putting it into his pocket,” the source said. The South China Morning Post learned that another passenger was believed to have witnessed the theft, filming it on his smartphone and alerting cabin crew. The insider said flight attendants then located the bag’s owner and notified airport staff to make a police report. The airport police district’s criminal investigation team is investigating the case.

title: Can Singapore be the ‘natural choice’ to bridge Asean and Central Asia?
description: Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong says Singapore aims to explore ways to boost cooperation between both regions in various sectors.
content: Singapore is positioning itself as a bridge between Central Asia and Asean, as both regions increasingly look to each other amid growing disruption to global trade and intensifying superpower rivalry. The political appetite exists, but analysts say trade benefits will still hinge on overcoming obstacles such as geography and a lack of connectivity. Singapore’s Senior Minister Lee Hsien Loong pitched the city state to Central Asian businesses during his visits to Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan from August 24 to 31. “Singapore has long been a gateway to Southeast Asia, a region of more than 700 million people and one of the fastest-growing parts of the world,” he told the Uzbekistan parliament on Monday. Lee said the city state, set to assume chairmanship of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations next year, would explore ways to boost cooperation between both regions in potential sectors such as transport, connectivity and energy. “We strive for a Southeast Asia which is linked to many countries and regions, where many partners can participate in and benefit from Southeast Asia’s stability and success, and Central Asia fits well into this vision.” Lee also voiced hopes for an increase in bilateral cooperation with Central Asian states. Singapore and Tashkent have agreed to start negotiating a free-trade agreement to further boost “nascent economic ties”. “Amidst all the uncertainty and turbulence in the world, smaller countries like us must continue to strengthen our partnership and cooperation – globally, between our regions, and bilaterally,” he said. Other Asean states have also recently stepped up efforts to advance cooperation with Central Asian countries. Leaders from Vietnam and Kyrgyzstan agreed to expand cooperation in potential areas such as science, technology, transport and people-to-people exchanges on the sidelines of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation Plus Summit on Monday. They also vowed to promote both parties’ bridging role in enhancing connectivity between Southeast Asia and Central Asia, according to local media. In June, Thailand and Kazakhstan signed a 2027-2028 road map outlining plans to advance cooperation in multiple sectors such as food security, hospitality and medical tourism. Foreign Minister Sihasak Phuangketkeow had earlier said Bangkok was ready to serve as a bridge in developing cooperation with Asean states. Converging interests Disruptions to trade routes due to global conflicts have reinforced the importance of cooperation between both regions, analysts say. Central Asia, which acts as a “land bridge” connecting China, Europe and the Middle East, is increasingly important to Asean as the bloc seeks investment opportunities and a stronger supply chain, according to Sabina Insebayeva, assistant professor of political science and international relations at Kazakhstan’s Nazarbayev University. Interest in the Middle Corridor – which runs through Kazakhstan across the inland Caspian Sea by ship to Azerbaijan, onwards to Georgia and into Turkey – as an alternative trade route has grown due to disruptions to established channels, she noted. Meanwhile, the landlocked Central Asia was likely to view Southeast Asia’s maritime routes as a link to Eurasia, as it tried to secure resources and capital to strengthen economic resilience, said Hoo Chiew-Ping, senior fellow at the East Asian International Relations Caucus. “Southeast Asia offers an attractive blueprint as a high-growth, neutral hub that maintains balanced relations with major global powers, including the US, Europe, China and Russia,” she said. While there is ample goodwill and willingness to enhance bilateral and regional cooperation, analysts warn that geographical differences and a lack of connectivity may hamper the development of a partnership which is still in its early stages.
