title: Meet Britney Spears’ son, Jayden James – model, musician and the new face of MAC Cosmetics
description: After debuting on Vetements’ Paris runway, the younger son of the ‘Princess of Pop’ and Kevin Federline is forging his own path in music.
content: Britney Spears’ youngest son, 19-year-old Jayden James, has just been announced as the new face of MAC Cosmetics. Spears’ complex personal life has been extensively covered by the media, so it’s no secret that she did not have the best relationship with her ex-husband Kevin Federline and their children. View this post on Instagram This year, Jayden seems to be spending more time with his pop star mother. In a video Spears shared on Instagram in March, she took mirror selfies and did outfit checks with her son at her house. “[S]pending time with family and friends is such a blessing!!!” Spears captioned the post. Jayden was also joined by his older brother, Sean Preston, on a yacht day with their mother. Jayden is slowly making a name for himself, with plans to further his modelling and musical careers. Here’s everything you need to know about Jayden James. How was his relationship with Spears growing up? Spears and Federline met in 2004, when he was a backup dancer for her ex-boyfriend, Justin Timberlake. After dating for just three months, the couple got married in 2004 and welcomed their firstborn, Sean Preston, on September 14, 2005. Their second child, Jayden James, was born on September 12, 2006. Spears filed for divorce that same year, citing irreconcilable differences. According to Us Weekly, Spears and Federline had agreed to share equal custody in 2007 after their divorce was finalised. However, in January 2008, the dancer was given sole custody after Spears went through a “mental breakdown” and was put on a 5150 – an involuntary 72-hour psychiatric hold. The pop star was later allowed to see her kids a few times a week. The exes would go on to co-parent the boys. Jayden and Sean moved to Hawaii in 2023 with their father and his wife, Victoria Prince. How did Jayden James get into modelling? Jayden and Sean made their runway debuts this June at Paris Fashion Week Men’s, walking for Vetements’ spring/summer 2027 show. After the experience, Jayden expressed his interest in modelling again. “I feel like I could do better, since this was my first fashion show and everything,” he said in an interview with Vogue in July. “I could master my walk better – I was definitely stiff because I was nervous.” While Spears did not attend the show, she still found a way to support her sons. “Oh my god, she was so nervous for us. She was just looking out for us and making sure that this was what we wanted to do,” Jayden told Vogue. “[S]he sent us flowers to our hotel as a good luck thing, and called and texted us so many times. It was good to have that and to carry that with us before we went out there.” The “Princess of Pop” had confidence in her sons, with Jayden saying, “I feel like she knew we had it. She was like, ‘Yeah, you guys are my sons. You’ve got this.’” He also wants to make music Jayden is a self-taught musician, and one of the first songs he taught himself to play was Queen’s “Bohemian Rhapsody”. On an Instagram Live session, Jayden shared that he considers his mother’s hit “Toxic” one of her best songs. He and Sean both seem to want to follow in their mother’s footsteps. Sean told Vogue, “Music is the foundation of everything for me. Jayden and I have done music our whole lives, and we definitely gravitate towards that more than anything else.” According to Maczine, a magazine by MAC Cosmetics, Jayden is working on introducing his music to the world, but only when he is ready. Who is Jayden James dating? Jayden is dating Gabrielle Helene. It is unclear when exactly they got together, but their relationship became Instagram-official in 2023. The couple made their red carpet debut this May at a Dior show. Jayden told Maczine about his skincare routine, saying, “My girlfriend does my whole routine for me, so if you wanna ask her about that, I think she’s the better person.” Their relationship seems to be going strong, with Helene joining her boyfriend in Paris in June, where they spent quality time around the French capital. Additional reporting by Faye Bradley

title: Hong Kong gold imports fall 18% in July as mainland giants rush to build vaults
description: While monthly shipments cool from record highs, banks and logistics giants are racing to secure physical space for the city’s rising bullion trade.
content: Gold flows into Hong Kong eased to about 107 tonnes in July despite mainland corporate buyers pouring capital into new bullion vaults, as they bet on the city’s strategic ambition to establish itself as Asia’s premier hub for the precious metal. The city’s non-monetary gold imports fell about 18 per cent from June, a month that registered a decade-long high as banks built up inventory ahead of the trial launch of the city’s gold clearing and settlement system that opened on July 7. The value of shipments fell to HK$114.71 billion (US$14.63 billion) from HK$142.02 billion, according to data released by Hong Kong’s Census and Statistics Department. “Import demand related to stocking has started to stabilise since the gold inventory build-up was largely completed in June,” said Ming Lam, councillor of the Greater China Division of CPA Australia. “Investors and traders may rebalance their overall investment portfolios, including their positions in gold.” Even with the monthly correction, appetite remained strong compared with February, when imports stood at just 72.16 tonnes. The robust demand comes as banks and logistics companies bet on Hong Kong’s gold vaults, moving to secure physical storage capacity as shipments for the precious metal expand. SF Express, China’s largest courier, is setting up a gold vault in Tsing Yi this year, according to a government registry provided to the South China Morning Post. Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, the mainland’s largest state-owned lender by total assets, is also developing a precious-metals storage facility. Industry players noted that Hong Kong’s newly introduced gold clearing and settlement system had established a framework for transferring static gold holdings. While still in its early stages, the system could boost regional liquidity and streamline operations, helping institutions to manage both physical and financial gold exposure. Family offices across Hong Kong and Singapore, for instance, had shown growing interest in gold trading, said William Chow, deputy group chief executive officer at Raffles Family Office. Looking at the broader implications, Vikas Gupta, head of Trading, Asia Currencies and Emerging Markets at JPMorgan Chase, noted that a “vibrant gold trading system in Asia, including inventory, futures and repos, could influence prices in London and New York”. Meanwhile, mainland China’s net gold imports via Hong Kong rose by about 11 per cent in July from a month earlier to 56.193 tonnes, marking a 28 per cent increase compared with the same period in 2025, official data showed. The growing inflow comes amid strong retail buying of gold jewellery, bars and coins on the mainland. Total gold consumption reached 511.41 tonnes in the first half of 2026, up 1.23 per cent year on year, according to data published in August by the China Gold Association. China became the world’s largest gold consumer in 2013 and has since consumed about five times that of the United States, three times that of Europe and nearly double all other emerging markets combined, S&P Global Ratings reported in August. Meanwhile, gold prices traded higher at about US$4,630 an ounce on Thursday following the US Treasury announcing last week that it would at least double the size of its liquidity-support buy-back operations for long-dated bonds, fuelling concerns about the erosion of the US dollar’s purchasing power.

title: ‘Panicked’: pause to US visa interviews affects more than 100 Hong Kong applicants
description: Sudden global restrictions by Trump have some applicants in city fearing US may scrap immigration pathway.
content: More than 100 Hong Kong-based applicants have been affected by the indefinite postponement of US immigrant visa interviews worldwide, consultants have said, with student and travel applications also disrupted. The global pause, which marks a sharp tightening of legal immigration under the Trump administration, has left some Hong Kong applicants fearing the United States could scrap the entire pathway, rendering their efforts futile and their money wasted. In an email seen by the South China Morning Post, the US consulate in Hong Kong told one applicant that her interview, set for this week, “has been rescheduled”, adding that confirmation of the new date and time would follow. The message did not explain the reason for the cancellation or provide a new interview date. Willis Fu Yiu-wai, a senior immigration consultant at Goldmax Associates, said about 10 of his Hong Kong clients were informed over the past two days that their immigrant visa interviews had been postponed indefinitely, while others were still undergoing vetting before the interview stage, which was proceeding normally. “They are really panicked, because they have paid the application fee and some have been through the process for two to three years, and the final step is the interview at the consulate,” he said. “They are worried that they might not be able to migrate to the US, as there are rumours that the immigration programme is terminated.” Fu added that some clients applying for non-immigrant visas, including business, student and travel visas, had also had their interviews postponed. Fu said he had never seen such an arrangement in his more than 10 years in the industry, describing it as “extremely rare”, but he expected the disruption to last one to two months. He argued that the latest policy was aimed at curbing illegal migrants and asylum seekers, and that the US had not suspended immigration pathways entirely. The senior consultant noted that some new non-immigrant visa applications submitted last week had interviews scheduled for October, a significantly longer wait than usual. Such applicants are generally required to attend an in-person interview with a consular officer, with limited exceptions for certain renewals. Peggy Lau Pik-ki, head of business development at Uni Immigration Consultancy, said more than 100 clients applying for investment immigration had been affected, including some mainland Chinese based in the city. She said the applicants received only short notice, with one client scheduled for an interview on Thursday being informed of the postponement only the day before. While the move was uncommon, Lau pointed to the US tightening of student visa requirements last year, saying it was “not very surprising”. She noted that the US had not terminated the processing and scrutiny of immigrant visas and remained open to new applications. Echoing Fu, Lau said she believed the suspension would be temporary and expected it to last at most a few months. She added that its impact on applicants and people’s intention to move to the US would be minimal, as the approval process for such visas typically took years. “I believe a group of people are still longing to move to the US … they believe the US is a place that they wish to live in,” Lau said. “[This] is a hurdle, but it is part of the process, so you just have to suck it up.” Andy*, who has applied for a US employment immigration visa, said he was originally expected to have an interview at the consulate next month under the previous timetable. Despite not receiving any formal notice so far, he believed the appointment would be postponed. “It is the final push, but it is like getting stood up,” he said. “The immigration policy in the US has changed frequently over the past two to three years. It’s elusive. While Andy said he was not too anxious since he expected any delay would only last a few months, a pause in the process would inevitably disrupt his plans. Such hurdles could force him to request a delay in onboarding for his job in the US, while his children’s school enrolment would also be affected as he had originally planned to arrive by January, so they could start when the new term began, he said. “Now my arrival time may be postponed to April or May,” Andy said. “The timing is awkward as it will fall in the middle of the school term.” He said he had applied for the immigration visa in 2022 and had hoped to provide his children with a better environment for development and education, adding that some of his family already lived in the US. “We have already made the decision to move to the US, and we will stick to the plan,” he said, stressing that he was not worried about a growing hostility towards migrants. He also urged the US government to quickly announce the next stage of the policy so applicants could have more certainty. On Wednesday, the US State Department said that “appointments for visa services” had been adjusted as officers underwent training at embassies and consulates worldwide, citing the need to protect Americans “by upholding the highest standards of screening and vetting of visa applicants”. *Name changed at interviewee’s request

title: Malaysian airport staff find body in wheel well of plane from Japan
description: Police say the unidentified victim is in his or her twenties and may have been dead for more than 72 hours.
content: The body of an unidentified person was found inside the wheel well of an aircraft at Malaysia’s Kuala Lumpur International Airport Terminal 2 (KLIA2) on Thursday (Aug 27). The body, whose gender has yet to be determined, was discovered at about 6.55am in the wheel well of a flight from Tokyo, Japan, which landed at about 6.30am. It is learnt that the body, clad in jeans and a white shirt, was found by engineering personnel who were tasked with opening the aircraft’s wheel well. The personnel detected a suspicious foul smell coming from the wheel well before opening the compartment. The body was subsequently discovered and the matter was reported to the KLIA2 police station operations room. Police forensic personnel were later deployed to the scene to conduct further investigations. Initial investigations found that the victim was believed to be in his or her twenties and may have been dead for more than 72 hours. However, no identification documents were found on the body. Investigations are ongoing to determine the victim’s identity and cause of death. This article was first published by The Star

title: 3 people injured, 4 cats dead after power bank catches fire in Hong Kong flat
description: Fire breaks out at So Uk Estate in Cheung Sha Wan just before 3am, forcing nearly 80 residents to flee before firefighters extinguish flames at 3.29am.
content: Three people have been injured and four cats have died after a power bank caught fire in a public housing flat in Hong Kong, forcing nearly 80 residents to evacuate. Police said they received a report at 2.51am on Thursday from a resident that the power bank inside her flat at So Uk Estate in Cheung Sha Wan had caught fire and that she managed to escape in time. Multiple other calls reported thick smoke coming from the location. The Fire Services Department said firefighters arrived shortly afterwards, deployed a hosepipe and a breathing-apparatus team to extinguish the fire and rescue residents, and raised an aerial ladder for inspection. A total of 78 residents were evacuated, with some taking their pets downstairs. Two men and a woman, aged 62 to 64, reported feeling unwell on a staircase while fleeing after inhaling smoke. Police said they sustained limb injuries and were sent to Caritas Medical Centre for treatment. The fire department said that at 3.29am, firefighters extinguished the blaze and rescued four cats from the flat. They covered the animals with blankets and laid them on the ground. “Firefighters performed cardiopulmonary resuscitation on the cats and used animal masks to assist the cats’ breathing,” a department spokesman said. The cats were later handed over to the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals, which confirmed that they ultimately died. Police said it was believed that the power bank overheated and caught fire. “At this stage, there is no evidence to suggest criminal elements were involved,” the force said.

title: North Korea vows ‘powerful response’ to US$125 million US-South Korea arms deal
description: Pyongyang says the potential sale of ‌AIM-9X Sidewinder missiles and related equipment poses ‘a new threat’ to its security environment.
content: North Korea’s foreign ministry on Thursday denounced a US decision to approve the sale of missiles and related equipment to South Korea, vowing to respond “strongly and immediately” to hostile acts in various areas, state media Korean Central News Agency reported. The remarks come as US President Donald Trump renewed overtures to North Korean leader Kim Jong-un, expressing interest ⁠in another meeting and saying this month that Kim had responded to his outreach. Analysts say Pyongyang ‌had shown little official willingness to resume talks. “We once again and clearly recognised the expression of the US open attitude to be always hostile to the DPRK,” ‌the ministry said in remarks carried by KCNA. DPRK stands for the Democratic People’s Republic ⁠of Korea, the ⁠North’s official name. The ministry was responding to the US State Department’s approval of a potential sale to South Korea of US$125 million worth of ‌AIM-9X Sidewinder air-to-air tactical missiles and related equipment, which Pyongyang said posed “a new threat” to its security environment. North Korea also criticised a US ‌plan ‌to fund activities related to documenting its human rights situation and gathering information on the country, describing ‌the efforts as part of a campaign aimed at creating instability in its social system. The ministry said ⁠Washington had this year approved sales to South Korea of various weapons systems, including advanced air-to-air missiles, naval ⁠helicopters, attack helicopters and precision-guided bombs, while encouraging Seoul to boost its war-fighting capabilities. “Now that the military integration of the US and its allies is being accelerated in the Asia-Pacific region, ‌we cannot overlook the adverse effect ‌of the US sale of its weapons to the ROK on the regional security environment,” the ministry added, using the initials for South Korea’s official name, the Republic of Korea. North Korea was aware of such threats and would have a “serious, immediate and powerful response” to hostile acts in different spheres, the official added.

title: Hong Kong privacy watchdog arrests boxer for allegedly doxxing opponent
description: Suspect allegedly twice posted victim’s personal information on social media, revealing name, photo and workplace, among other details.
content: Hong Kong’s privacy watchdog has arrested a boxer suspected of doxxing an opponent on social media by disclosing his personal information and workplace without consent. The Office of the Privacy Commissioner for Personal Data (PCPD) said on Thursday that the 29-year-old suspect had targeted the victim twice. The pair fought each other at a boxing tournament in early 2025. The suspect allegedly posted his opponent’s personal details on his social media accounts twice after the tournament — once in March last year and again this month The posts included negative comments about the victim and disclosed his English name, Chinese “alias”, photo, social media account handle and workplace details. The watchdog said the alleged premeditated conduct, intended to cause harm, violated the Personal Data (Privacy) Ordinance. Those convicted face a maximum fine of HK$1 million (US$127,600) and up to five years in prison. The suspect has been granted bail while the watchdog continues its investigation. “The PCPD reminds members of the public that they should not dox others because of personal disputes,” it said, adding that doxxing was a serious offence.

title: Wang Yi calls on US to ‘overcome obstacles’ ahead of Xi-Trump meeting
description: In meeting with US envoy, China’s top diplomat urges Washington to focus on a positive agenda as the two sides prepare for Xi’s trip.
content: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi has urged Washington to help “remove interference and overcome obstacles” to high-level exchanges as the two sides prepare for President Xi Jinping’s expected visit to the US next month. Meeting US ambassador David Perdue in Beijing on Wednesday, Wang said both sides should put the Xi-Trump consensus into practice, focus on a positive agenda and manage differences to keep ties “stable, healthy and sustainable”, according to China’s foreign ministry. In a social media post, Perdue later described the talks as part of “preparations for President Xi’s reciprocal visit to Washington”. Wang’s message comes ahead of an expected September 24 meeting between Xi and US President Donald Trump at the White House. Citing “various risks and challenges” in the relationship, Wang said that “under the guidance of the two heads of state, both sides are working to build a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability”. “Facts have proven that improving and developing China-US relations, peaceful coexistence on the basis of mutual respect, and then win-win cooperation serve the fundamental interests of the two peoples and meet the common expectations of the international community,” he said. Perdue struck a similarly conciliatory note, calling Trump’s May visit to China “very successful” and saying Washington was ready to “strengthen communication, advance cooperation” and prepare for “important high-level interactions in the next stage”. The US ambassador said the two sides should build a constructive and stable relationship “on the basis of respect and reciprocity”, according to the Chinese foreign ministry. On Thursday, Perdue wrote on social media that he had held “productive discussions this week” with Wang, Foreign Vice-Minister Ma Zhaoxu, and assistant foreign ministers Hong Lei and Cai Wei. He added that the two sides were “working together to achieve a constructive relationship of strategic stability with fairness and reciprocity”. Since Trump and Xi’s meeting in Busan, South Korea, in October last year, the China-US relationship has held to a fragile trade truce while new disputes over Iran sanctions, visas, technology and restrictions targeting alleged forced labour have added friction. Both sides still say they want “strategic stability” and are working on trade and investment arrangements, but few concrete breakthroughs have been reached. This week, the US Treasury launched what Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called “Operation Economic Outcast”. The package hit about 60 entities allegedly tied to Iranian oil, missiles, nuclear procurement and cyber activity, including firms and a tanker linked to mainland China and Hong Kong. It stopped short of sanctioning big Chinese banks. Beijing called the measures “illegal unilateral sanctions” and said it would “take all necessary measures” to protect its interests.

title: Chinese scientists discover that trees are producing ozone smog in Beijing
description: The city’s poplars and willows have been identified as the source of an unexpected spike in ozone levels during the heat of the summer.
content: Beijing’s hundreds of thousands of weeping willows and poplars have been a welcome source of shelter from the fierce summer sun for more than four decades – but they may also be an unexpected source of pollution, according to new research. Scientists warned that this urban greenery may be “choking” the Chinese capital’s 20 million residents by increasing the levels of ozone in the city’s air. Smog caused by the ozone released by car exhaust has been recognised as a public health problem since the 1940s, with some severe incidents known to have killed hundreds of people. Beijing’s ozone levels had puzzled researchers because many cars in the city have gone electric, but they have now identified the compounds released by the trees as the most likely culprit. An international team led by scientists from Jinan University in Guangzhou initially intended to measure how human activities generated ozone pollution – but they soon discovered that the trees in Beijing generated far more smog than expected, according to research published in the journal Science Advances. This is because they produce unusually high levels of isoprene, a volatile organic compound (VOC) that produces ground-level ozone when it reacts with the nitrogen oxide typically produced by vehicles or factories. Although Beijing is not the only city to have this problem, it has an unusually high proportion of species such as white poplars and weeping willows, which make up an estimated 35 per cent of its urban greenery and produce high levels of isoprene. Other high-emissions trees, such as oaks and eucalyptus, are less common in urban areas. The city’s authorities began greening the city in 1979 and by the end of 2018, had planted an estimated 284,000 poplar and willow trees in the area encircled by the fifth ring road, which is generally regarded as the main urban area. The trees have obvious benefits such as rapid growth, an ability to survive the city’s cold winters and the plentiful blind they provide during the summer. However, even before the release of the latest study, these species were known for causing seasonal problems – they shed their catkins in the early spring, triggering respiratory and allergy problems. “We conducted a horizontal comparison of Beijing’s observation results with existing urban data from around the world and found that Beijing’s standardised isoprene emission intensity from vegetation is at the highest level among existing urban observations, approaching the levels observed in temperate forests,” the study’s lead author Yuan Bin, from Jinan University, told China Science Daily. The problem is made worse by the Chinese capital’s hot summers, which cause plants to produce more ozone. Data showed that when the temperature in Beijing rose from 20 degrees Celsius to 35 degrees (68 to 95 Fahrenheit) the rate at which they broke down in the atmosphere to form pollutants rose by around 700 per cent. In contrast, pollution caused by human activity increased by only about 40 per cent. The study concluded that vegetation accounted for about 10 per cent of total VOC emissions, but these went on to form more than half (52 per cent) of the ozone detected in the city. The study did not call for the immediate removal of poplar and willow trees, but suggested that the proportion of other species planted in the city should be gradually increased. Researchers calculated that replacing 10 per cent of the high-emissions trees with other species would cut isoprene emissions by at least 29 per cent. “In addition to urban greening in existing cities, planners of large-scale urban developments … may wish to consider urban tree selection in terms of VOC emissions to alleviate future air-quality management challenges,” Yuan wrote. They added that it was still important to continue efforts to reduce harmful emissions from human activities, especially during summer. Passionate about science? title: Malaysia’s Ismail Sabri denies failing to declare millions in cash, gold bars
description: The prosecution claims the former prime minister did not disclose about US$40 million in assets to the anti-corruption agency.
content: Malaysia’s former prime minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob pleaded not guilty in a Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court on Thursday to failing to declare millions of ringgit in local and foreign currencies and gold bars. The 66-year-old is the second ex-leader to face criminal charges since Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim took office in 2022, pledging to root out entrenched corruption. Ismail Sabri’s charge under Section 36(2) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) Act comes more than a year after he was named as a suspect in a sprawling corruption and money-laundering investigation involving government publicity-spending during his administration. According to the charge, Ismail Sabri allegedly gave a written statement in February 2025 that failed to comply with an MACC notice requiring him to declare specified assets. Those assets, valued at close to US$40 million, consisted of physical cash in multiple currencies, encompassing 14.77 million ringgit, S$6.13 million, US$1.46 million, 3 million Swiss francs, €12.16 million, 363 million yen, £50,250, NZ$44,600, 34.75 million UAE dirhams and A$352,850, as well as five Suisse fine gold bars. If convicted, the MP for the central constituency of Bera faces up to five years in prison and a maximum fine of 100,000 ringgit (US$25,000). Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin granted Ismail Sabri bail of 300,000 ringgit with one surety, rejecting the prosecution’s proposed 500,000-ringgit bail and request for his passport to be surrendered, local media reported. His lawyer, Amer Hamzah Arshad, said the defence argued that the proposed bail was “manifestly excessive” and that confiscating his passport would have been punitive. “There is no necessity for his passport to be surrendered. He has proven himself not to be a flight risk, and there is no evidence to show that he is a flight risk,” Amer told reporters after the hearing. “He is here to clear his name.” The court fixed September 29 for the next hearing. ‘Unprecedented’ prosecution Amer said the defence team was studying the charge and had raised concerns in court about its “propriety and legality”, adding that they could apply to challenge it. The defence is focusing in part on earlier forfeiture proceedings involving assets seized during the MACC investigation. Last year, a sessions court ordered more than 169 million ringgit in cash linked to Ismail Sabri and his former political secretary to be forfeited after neither man contested the prosecution’s application and no third party came forward to claim the money. The forfeiture was made under Section 41(1) of the MACC Act, a provision dealing with property where prosecution for an offence has not been instituted. As part of the proceedings, prosecutors indicated they would not be pursuing any charges, Amer said. “The fact that there is suddenly a change of heart by the prosecution is something that we have to look into,” he said. “That is why we say it is unprecedented. This situation has never arisen before.” He declined to elaborate on whether that constituted an agreement not to prosecute Ismail Sabri but said the circumstances were “very peculiar”. “We will definitely take the necessary action to challenge the validity and propriety of the charge,” he said. Thursday’s proceedings had originally been scheduled for August 7 but were postponed after Ismail Sabri was admitted to the National Heart Institute with an abnormal heart rhythm and was fitted with a pacemaker. Ismail Sabri is the latest senior politician to be caught in the MACC’s dragnet, and the second former prime minister to be brought before the courts under Anwar’s watch. His predecessor, Muhyiddin Yassin, was charged in 2023 with four counts of abusing his position to obtain bribes totalling 232.5 million ringgit for his Bersatu party, and three counts of money laundering involving 200 million ringgit into his party’s accounts. Another ex-prime minister, Najib Razak, is already serving a prison sentence for corruption. He was handed a further 15-year jail term last December after being convicted of abuse of power and money laundering involving 2.3 billion ringgit in funds linked to scandal-ridden state investment fund 1Malaysia Development Berhad. In a rare coincidence, all three were at the Kuala Lumpur court complex on Thursday for different hearings. Prosecutors also went after prominent tycoon and former finance minister Daim Zainuddin and his wife, Naimah Khalid. Both were charged in January 2024 with failing to declare their assets as part of the MACC’s investigation into revelations of their family’s offshore holdings from the 2021 Pandora Papers. Following his death in November 2024, Daim was acquitted of all charges. Naimah, who continues to face charges, and her family have maintained that the crackdown was “frivolous, malicious and politically motivated”, accusing Anwar of seeking revenge against his political enemies. Daim was widely seen as a close adviser to two-time former leader Mahathir Mohamad, who in 1998 sacked Anwar as his deputy and later saw to his jailing on charges of corruption and sodomy. Anwar and his supporters have maintained that the charges were politically motivated and aimed at ending his political career.

title: In Malaysia, injured elephant Sulong’s 100km trek home drives logging debate
description: The Asian elephant’s long journey back home has stirred outrage over logging and habitat loss in Malaysia.
content: The lonely journey of a bull elephant trying to return to its jungle home has captured the hearts of Malaysians over the past week, putting a spotlight on the plight of wildlife struggling against deforestation and rapidly expanding human activity. The elephant – dubbed “Sulong” by Malaysians keenly following social media updates on his weeks-long journey – was first spotted by motorists on August 17, walking slowly along the busy East-West Highway in an apparent attempt to reach the northeastern state of Kelantan. Wildlife authorities had previously relocated Sulong to a forest reserve in Gerik, Perak, more than 230km (140 miles) southwest from the forest surrounding Chalil, a remote village in Kelantan’s Gua Musang district, where locals had raised concerns of repeated incursions on farms and village land. Videos of Sulong’s trek soon went viral. Images of the gentle giant limping slowly with an injury to its front right leg proved too much to bear for some. “Imagine an injured elephant walking hundreds of kilometres on unknown terrain, purely following its instinct to return home,” read one emotional social media post. “He is not a problem. He is not a disturbance. He is just a wild animal, a living creature in search of its home.” Heartbreak and hope as injured elephant ‘Sulong’ treks 100km back to Gua Musang. pic.twitter.com/7RxUGeuOf1 — ZoologiMY (@ZoologiMY) August 26, 2026 After weeks of trudging along asphalt roads, Sulong finally made his way back into the forested area of Jeli in Kelantan on Wednesday, according to wildlife authorities – roughly halfway home. Department of Wildlife and National Parks director general Abdul Kadir Abu Hashim said rangers had maintained twice-daily surveillance throughout Sulong’s journey to monitor his health and guide him towards the jungle. Authorities continue to track his movements using drones and ground teams. But Sulong’s ordeal has also triggered public anger over habitat destruction, which some argue forces wild animals into human settlements to search for food. “The root cause of elephants encroaching into villages is because forests are levelled and widespread logging that destroys the natural habitat of wildlife … if you don’t want elephants or tigers to encroach into villages, DON’T CLEAR FORESTS!” read one post. Agriculture and forestry are major drivers of Kelantan’s economy, accounting for a fifth of the state’s annual revenue – primarily through oil palm, fruit plantations and timber. The state earned just over 900 million ringgit (US$223.4 million) from logging activities in 2024, and officials expect to maintain earnings from the sector while keeping to national logging quotas. But even minimal forest loss can have an adverse effect on wildlife, the WWF has warned, saying Sulong’s journey is a clear sign that wild animals need “large, connected forest landscapes to survive”. “Wildlife corridors are essential, ensuring elephants can move safely between habitats in search of food, water and shelter,” the wildlife conservation body said in a statement on Wednesday. “This also highlights the importance of maintaining healthy forests and ecological corridors while addressing underlying issues of habitat fragmentation and land loss.”

title: Live broadcast of Fan Zhendong’s German Cup clash sells out Chinese cinemas in minutes
description: Table tennis star Fan Zhendong will play for club side Borussia Dusseldorf in a German Cup clash against Ochsenhausen on Saturday.
content: Fan Zhendong may have dropped out of the table tennis world rankings and China’s national team but his popularity on the mainland appears as strong as ever. The Olympic champion’s German Cup match on Saturday will be broadcast live in 56 cinemas across the mainland, and tickets sold out within three minutes in some cities. Last week, video streaming platform Youku Sports and state-backed film distributor Huaxia Film jointly announced that they would live-stream Fan’s appearance in his Borussia Dusseldorf side’s clash with Ochsenhausen. Tickets for the tie, which starts at 5pm and pits Fan’s side against the five-time cup winners, went on sale for between 50 and 90 yuan (US$7.50-US$13). According to reports, three days after the announcement, screenings in Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Hangzhou were fully sold out by early morning, with limited tickets remaining in Beijing and Wuhan. In Beijing, the Huaxia Film Centre allocated six auditoriums for simultaneous broadcasts, all of which sold out. Ticket prices were mostly set at 63 yuan (US$8.80), with a Dolby Atmos hall priced at 99 yuan. Ticketing platforms showed that three cinemas each in Shanghai and Shenzhen will host screening events, with all sessions fully booked. Cinema staff told local media that tickets for Saturday’s event sold rapidly to individual buyers, adding that there were currently no plans for additional screenings. “We were also shocked; it sold out within three minutes,” a staff member at one cinema with 167 seats said. Another 159-seat venue sold out in about half an hour, while a third cinema said its 466-seat auditorium, typically reserved for celebrity roadshows and live event broadcasts, sold out in roughly 15 minutes. During the sales period, online users raised concerns over inflated ticket prices, with rumours circulating of tickets being resold for 200 to 300 yuan. Youku Sports responded that it was contacting relevant departments to address the issue quickly. “Because we do not hold pricing authority, we are unaware of individual cinema pricing and cannot intervene in advance,” Youku Sports posted on its official Weibo account. “Thank you very much for alerting us; we are filing formal complaints. We also ask everyone to consume rationally and firmly resist such behaviour.” Early on Thursday, Fan made his away debut for Borussia Dusseldorf in the third round of the 2026–2027 Table Tennis Bundesliga season. Playing as the team’s top singles player, Fan comfortably beat France’s Lilian Bertrand 3-0 in the second match to lead Dusseldorf to a 3-0 victory over SV Werder Bremen. According to Dusseldorf’s previously announced August schedule, Fan was originally slated to play only home fixtures and the German Cup, making this appearance an added fixture intended to help him regain match sharpness ahead of the cup tie. This marks Fan’s second consecutive season in the German league, having played for Saarbrücken in the 2025–2026 season, where he recorded 20 wins in 23 matches and was named league MVP.

title: Catastrophic mudslide near China-Nepal border leaves hundreds missing
description: Over 160 confirmed dead as rescue efforts continue amid mounting international aid.
content:
A massive mudslide and flash flood hit the Gyirong Port region near the China-Nepal border on Wednesday, resulting in at least 160 fatalities and over 1,000 individuals unaccounted for on both sides of the border.
As per the most recent announcement from the Shigatse municipal government during a press conference on Thursday morning, three deaths have been confirmed, with 558 individuals still missing in the Chinese territory.
Two survivors have been rescued. Earlier figures of 265 missing were revised upwards as search efforts expanded, according to the update.
Chinese authorities have mobilised more than 1,500 personnel, including firefighters, military troops and engineering teams. Vice-Premier Zhang Guoqing has arrived at the scene to direct operations.
A barrier lake has formed near the port, complicating rescue efforts, according to state broadcaster CCTV.
Nepal police reported late on Wednesday that 157 bodies had been recovered.
According to the Nepali Prime Minister’s Office, 484 tourists are missing, including 391 foreign nationals from at least 26 countries. Among them are 142 Indians, 47 from the United States, 34 from Australia, 33 from Britain and 24 from Canada.
Sunil Sharma, a spokesman for the Nepal Tourism Board, said that 133 of the missing tourists were Indian pilgrims.
The disaster hit Gyirong county in Tibet’s Shigatse at around 10.30am on Wednesday, originating from the Nepali side.
The area sits alongside a key pilgrimage corridor leading to Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash and Lake Manasarovar, which draws hundreds of devotees from India and beyond each year, especially during this peak season.
Initial assessments by Nepali officials pointed to a possible earthquake-triggered collapse of a glacier’s lower section, which may have unleashed the devastating floodwaters.
Countries and organisations around ⁠the world ⁠have begun sending ⁠cash, relief supplies and other assistance to Nepal as it responds to the aftermath of a devastating flash flood that killed more ‌than 160 people and left hundreds missing.
China has coordinated emergency supplies and cash assistance for Nepal, China’s Ambassador to Nepal said in a post on the social media platform X.
The EU is ready to “mobilise further European assistance”, European Commission President Ursula ‌von der Leyen said on X.
India has ⁠sent 10 ⁠metric tons of disaster-relief supplies, including temporary shelters, blankets, hygiene kits, solar ‌lamps and medicines, India’s foreign ministry said.

title: Bruno Mars to play 4 shows in Hong Kong next May, returning after nearly a decade
description: Grammy-winning US pop star will perform on May 7, 8, 11 and 12 in ‘Romantic Tour’ that also includes stops in Singapore, Japan and Thailand.
content: American pop star Bruno Mars will return to Hong Kong for the first time in nearly a decade to play four shows at Kai Tak Stadium in May 2027 as part of an expanded Asian leg of his “The Romantic Tour”. The Grammy-winning singer-songwriter would perform in Hong Kong on May 7, 8, 11 and 12, with other Asian dates planned in Singapore, Japan, Thailand and elsewhere, organiser Live Nation announced on Thursday. The concerts will be Mars’ first in Hong Kong since his 24K Magic World Tour shows at AsiaWorld-Expo in 2018 and his first performances at the city’s newest mega venue. The stadium, part of Kai Tak Sports Park, opened in March 2025 and has a maximum capacity of 50,000. It hosted four shows by British rock band Coldplay last year, attracting nearly 200,000 fans in total. Registration for a special “artist presale” will open at noon on September 23. A presale through travel website Trip.com will begin at the same time, according to Live Nation. General ticket sales will begin at noon on September 24, priced from HK$799 (US$102) to HK$1,499.

title: Meet Adéla’s boyfriend, Jackson Shanks – the music producer who’s worked with Selena Gomez and Le Sserafim
description: He has been dating the rising Slovak pop star and ‘Ain’t In LA’ singer for a year, having first been spotted together at a Sabrina Carpenter concert last November.
content: Every year, the internet searches for a song to define the summer, and one of this year’s contenders is definitely “Ain’t In LA” by rising pop star Adéla Jergová. A viral trend on social media right now is using the phrase “It can’t always be LA, someone’s gotta hold it down in … ” where fans around the world name their city, which is in line with the song’s message of empowering girls by honouring their hometown roots and taking pride in their upbringing. View this post on Instagram Best known by her mononymous stage name, Adéla created the hit song after visiting her home country, Slovakia. Per The Line Of Best Fit magazine, she was inspired upon seeing photos of her mother posing in front of a wall of smuggled pop culture posters at 18. The 22-year-old recently became the first Slovak artist to enter the Billboard Hot 100 chart, where “Ain’t In LA” ranked No 61 as of Thursday morning. All eyes are now on the singer as she carves out her niche in the music industry, and as usual, interest in her love life has surged. Last year, she was seen spending time with a mysterious man, who was later identified as music producer Jackson Shanks. Here is what to know about the breakout star’s beau. What is Jackson Shanks’ background? Jackson Shanks is a producer from Los Angeles. He attended Campbell Hall, where he played in the Campbell Hall Steel Band. Shanks signed a publishing deal with Universal Music Publishing Group in 2023. Record producer and songwriter Blake Slatkin – who has collaborated with high-profile artists such as Justin Bieber, The Kid Laroi, SZA, Gracie Abrams, Jungkook and Katseye – has mentored him. Slatkin is also a producer on Adéla’s upcoming debut album, Prima, which is set to release next month. Shanks is making his way in the music industry and has already worked with a wide array of artists. His most successful production credits include “Talk to You” by Dutch duo Anotr, “Hot” by South Korean girl group Le Sserafim and “Touch Tank” by US indie rock musician Quinnie. He has also produced for Selena Gomez and Benny Blanco. How long have Adéla and Jackson Shanks dated? Shanks was first seen with Adéla in late November last year, when they appeared in the background of a proposal video shared on TikTok. The clip, taken at Sabrina Carpenter’s Short n’ Sweet Tour concert in Los Angeles, shows Adéla and Shanks hugging, and the pop singer opens her mouth in shock when a man proposes to his partner in front of them. Adéla told the In Your Dreams With Owen Thiele podcast this January that she met Shanks through a producer friend and recently confirmed with Teen Vogue that they are marking their first anniversary this month. In the interview, the Slovak singer joked that dating Shanks for a year felt like “a lifetime when you’re 22”, adding that her boyfriend “doesn’t get scared away by my craziness, the craziness in my life, or my family, or my career”. The pair have attended parties and events together; their most recent appearance was at Lollapalooza in Chicago, where Adéla made her major festival debut.

title: Yayoi Kusama, Japanese artist famous for pumpkins and polka dots, dies aged 97
description: The avant-garde artist, who enjoyed a strong following in Hong Kong, died on August 14 at a hospital in Tokyo due to multiple organ failure.
content: Yayoi Kusama, the Japanese avant-garde artist whose obsessive polka dots, towering pumpkin sculptures and mesmerising Infinity Mirror Rooms captivated audiences worldwide, has died at the age of 97. The artist died on August 14 at a hospital in Tokyo due to multiple organ failure. Her studio and the city’s Yayoi Kusama Museum confirmed the news on August 27. “Throughout an extraordinary lifetime devoted entirely to artistic creation, Kusama pursued an internationally acclaimed career as a pioneering avant-garde artist whose creative practice encompassed visual art, performance, fiction and poetry,” her studio said in a statement. The museum added that Kusama “held fast to her belief in saving the world through love until the very end”. Kusama enjoyed a particularly strong following in Hong Kong, and the city functioned as her primary commercial art market across Asia. Notably, it hosted the largest retrospective of her work on the continent outside her native Japan. That landmark exhibition, “Yayoi Kusama: 1945 to Now”, was launched by Hong Kong’s M+ museum to celebrate its first anniversary in November 2022. Spanning eight decades, the retrospective featured more than 200 works and proved a massive public draw, attracting more than 280,000 visitors before it concluded in May 2023. The museum assembled the display with works loaned from major public museums and private collections across Asia, Europe and the United States, alongside materials from Kusama’s personal studio archives. Three major new works commissioned specifically for M+ debuted at the retrospective: Death of Nerves, Dots Obsession – Aspiring to Heaven’s Love and Pumpkin (all 2022), which featured two giant pumpkin sculptures. Beyond museum walls, auction rooms across the city – including Christie’s, Sotheby’s, Bonhams and Phillips – regularly broke record sales with her works as headliner lots. In April 2019, her oil painting Interminable Net #4 (1959) was sold for HK$62.43 million (US$7.96 million) at Sotheby’s Hong Kong, beating the previous world record for Kusama from 2014 and setting a record for a work by a female artist sold at auction in Asia at the time. In May 2023, Christie’s Hong Kong sold A Flower (2014) for HK$78.1 million, the highest price for any Kusama work in Hong Kong. More recently, Bonhams HK sold Infinity (1995) for HK$46.4 million in May 2024. The city also served as a major launch pad for her commercial activations, especially during her 2023 global campaign with Louis Vuitton, which featured public art takeovers and eye-catching pop-ups across central retail hubs. Kusama’s final years were remarkably productive. Her late career was marked by major retrospectives such as the Fondation Beyeler and Museum Ludwig’s touring exhibition (2025-26), solo shows at the Yayoi Kusama Museum (2025-26) and “Yayoi Kusama: Infinite Love” at SFMOMA in San Francisco (2023-24). A major retrospective at Cologne’s Museum Ludwig concluded on August 2, just weeks before her death. Kusama’s studio confirmed that she painted until her final days. “We will carry forward Kusama’s wishes and, through art, continue to bring hope and strength for the future to people around the world,” the studio’s statement read. From childhood hallucinations to global artistic acclaim Born in 1929 in Matsumoto, Nagano prefecture, Kusama endured a difficult childhood marked by an abusive mother and a philandering father. Her wealthy family managed plant nurseries, and as a child, Kusama began experiencing hallucinations in which flowers would swarm around and speak to her. Her coping mechanism was to draw what she saw – fields of dots and nets that would become her lifelong visual language. “I don’t want to cure my mental problems, rather I want to utilise them as a generating force for my art,” Kusama was quoted as saying in an article published by the South China Morning Post in 2017. “My art originates from hallucinations only I can see … All my works in pastels are the products of obsessional neurosis and are therefore inextricably connected to my disease.” I am fighting with my sickness from childhood. This made me original and creative Yayoi Kusama Later, she grew frustrated with the confining nature of Japanese society and rejecting an arranged marriage, Kusama left for America in 1957 at age 28 and began making her iconic “infinity net” paintings – vast fields of impastoed polka dots that stretched across the canvas. In 1962, she sold her first infinity net painting to artists Frank Stella and Donald Judd for US$75. In 2014, her White No 28 (1960) sold for US$7.1 million at Christie’s in New York, making her the most expensive living female artist at the time. Throughout the 1960s, Kusama staged provocative “body festivals” with naked performers painted in polka dots, to the point where Andy Warhol was famously accused of copying her work. Infamously radical in her art, she published a publicly distributed manifesto titled “An Open Letter to My Hero, Richard M. Nixon” at the height of the Vietnam war in 1968, as part of her anti-war performance art – offering to sleep with the just elected US president in exchange for an end to the war. Around 1977, a few years after returning to Japan, Kusama voluntarily entered a psychiatric hospital in Tokyo and lived there for decades, being driven to her nearby studio each morning. She divided her time between the hospital and her studio until her final days. Despite her struggles, Kusama achieved belated but spectacular recognition in her later years. She received Japan’s prestigious Order of Culture in 2016, and the Yayoi Kusama Museum opened in Tokyo in 2017. She became one of the world’s bestselling artists, with total career auction sales exceeding US$1 billion. “I am fighting with my sickness from childhood. This made me original and creative,” she told the SCMP in 2005. “The development of my philosophy in sculpture, installation and happenings was all my ideas, against the old-fashioned ideas.”

title: How a Hong Kong dim sum ritual and nostalgia inspired Orchard’s Fortune Chai
description: The city’s yum cha tradition, a bartender’s chai memories and a fortune cookie garnish come together in this silky, spice-tinged Armagnac cocktail.
content: “When I went to a dim sum place, I had tea in a small teacup and thought the action of drinking tea with your hands felt unique,” Dipesh Rai says. “You don’t really drink any other drink with such an action. It inspired me to make a cocktail with the action of drinking tea in mind.” Rai is poised to take the head bartender position at Orchard next month after developing cocktails like the Fortune Chai in a recent update to the bar’s menu. Founded by Alex Pun, Orchard is Hong Kong’s only bar whose primary focus is on fruit spirits or eau de vie, but drinks like the Fortune Chai showcase Rai and the team’s ability to build creatively on that base concept, evoking ideas like the process of drinking tea in a city like Hong Kong. Taking cues from the Brandy Alexander, Rai “wanted to capture a dessert cocktail, but … didn’t want the thick, creamy texture that comes with [it]”. Armagnac, a regional brandy distilled from grapes, is fat-washed in brown butter, then batched with liqueurs – a creme de cacao liqueur infused with chai masala and another made to evoke the flavours of biscotti. This forms the drink’s base batch. “The warming spices in the masala chai, I felt, always went very well with dark spirits such as Armagnac. It also has a little to do with me,” Rai explains regarding the infusions. “I grew up waking up to warm spices in the air as my mum was brewing chai every morning. To this day, it’s a very nostalgic memory. I chose masala chai as I wanted to add a little part of myself to the cocktail.” The base batch is then mixed with Cocchi Americano sweet vermouth, saline solution and chocolate bitters, served on the rocks and topped with a fortune cookie garnish. “Obviously, you can’t enjoy warm, freshly brewed chai masala without a biscuit, or maybe that’s just me,” Rai says. “I went through hundreds of types of biscuits, but it suddenly clicked when I saw a fortune cookie. It’s a fun, interactive garnish for guests as well as a small icebreaker to engage with.” Between the tea-drinking inspiration, the nostalgia of chai masala, the fortune cookie and the silky reinterpretation of the Brandy Alexander’s mouthfeel, the Fortune Chai offers a deeply personal, tactile way to experience Armagnac. Even though Armagnac may be relatively familiar given its similarity to cognac, guests can also expect to sample a bit of the base spirit, a practice that helps pave the way for other cocktails on the menu that may feature more exotic eau de vie. “This allows the guests to taste the spirit on its own first,” Rai explains, “then experience how it expresses itself in the cocktail. That comparison has been really important – it helps the guest connect the purity and character of the spirit with the finished drink. Over time, we have seen guests become more curious, more confident and more open to eau de vie and fruit spirits as a category.” When we last spoke to Pun about the Redemption, Orchard was still encountering guests so new to eau de vie that they assumed the spirit category was a type of flavoured vodka. It’s clear now that building a tactile and flavour experience gives guests multiple entry points to understand eau de vie at Orchard. About the drink’s reception so far, Rai says, “Watching the reactions and smiles after reading their fortunes is still my favourite thing to do.” Anatomy of a cocktail Name: Fortune Chai Bar: Orchard, 28 Gage Street, Central Price: HK$130 Main ingredients: Butter-washed Armagnac, chai masala-infused creme de cacao, biscotti liqueur, Cocchi Americano, chocolate bitters, saline solution Presentation: Served on the rocks, garnished with a fortune cookie Flavours: Silky, earthy, sweet, aromatic, dry spice, chocolate, biscuit, spirit-forward

title: Mouthing Off | Why is the US-Canada trade war seemingly hinging on drinking games?
description: As tensions rise between former besties Canada and the US, the former’s refusal to sell US alcohol is a highly contentious point.
content: Macroeconomics is hardly my forte, but it is fascinating how a major international trade war between Canada and the US – two friends turned rivals – seems to hinge on one minor sector: booze. The dispute between the two countries has escalated into all-out rancour after a breakdown in trade negotiations this week, resulting in US President Donald Trump imposing a broad 50 per cent tariff on a wide range of goods entering the US from Canada. A major reason for the failure in talks is one party’s decision not to sell alcohol made by the other country. Canada, for the most part, has been refusing to stock American booze in its stores since early 2025. In one of his first acts as the 47th US president, Trump decided it was priority number one to pick on his friendly neighbour, with whom he was in a free-trade pact. He unilaterally jacked up tariffs because… actually, I don’t know why. Your guess is as good as mine. In response to the provocation from the self-proclaimed “stable genius” – who also slung personal insults, like calling the Canadian prime minister a governor and suggesting Canada should become the 51st US state – most provinces were highly offended and sought revenge strategically. Besides Alberta and Saskatchewan, the other territories and provinces all decided to ban alcohol imports from south of the border. So, no Jack Daniels, no Jim Beam, no Maker’s Mark, and no California wines from Robert Mondavi, Opus One and others. In terms of the overall economy, the alcohol market is a tiny fraction – less than 1 per cent of the gross trade between Canada and the US – but, boy, is that niche ever high profile and loud. As a counterpunch by Canada, it is superficial but provocative – a bit like taking someone’s hat off their head and throwing it to the ground. The alcohol ban has received a ton of notice. Distillers and winemakers are regularly interviewed about how they are affected. Politicians on both sides of the border remark on the impacts on constituents. Just seeing empty shelves formerly filled with American spirits has become a sore point for Trumpists, and a source of patriotic pride for Canucks. North of the border, the ban is a powerful symbol of resistance against an unreliable and bossy downstairs neighbour. The thing is, even if the policy were to be reversed, I have a feeling that many Canadians would still not buy American products; fuelled by their distaste for the US, they would probably choose European spirits or, better yet, home-grown whiskey and wine. Alcohol consumption is decreasing around the world, but spirits and drinks remain an important touchstone to the North American psyche. It still lubricates social traditions and bonds, and maintains identity and pride. Each bottle of Napa Valley Cabernet and Kentucky bourbon is perceived to reflect such regional craftsmanship. If the United States or Canada really wanted to hurt each other, they would target truly vital industries like cars, energy and dairy. But nobody wants a pyrrhic victory. Instead, this reminds me of two fighters who decide “only the body, no headshots”.

title: Anwar Ibrahim weighs delaying Malaysia general election to late 2027 amid poll setbacks
description: The Malaysian prime minister reconsiders snap election plans as state poll defeats, stalled reforms and rival alliances threaten coalition.
content: Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim is looking to push back national elections until the second half of next year, people familiar with the matter said, as state poll defeats and soured partnerships reveal his political vulnerability. That time frame would mark a significant delay. Just months ago, the 79-year-old leader was said to be mulling a snap election as soon as this October, perceiving his greatest risk at the time to be rising fuel prices. But two humbling state election losses since then, along with the growing risk of a split with a key coalition partner, have delayed that schedule until after the 2028 budget release – possibly around next October, according to the people, who asked not to be identified detailing private strategy deliberations. Another consideration is the expected boost to public sentiment when Malaysia hosts the Southeast Asian Games in September 2027, said one of the people. No final decision had been made on the timing of the next general election, the people said. Anwar’s office did not respond to a request for comment. The premier told parliament last month that his government should complete a full term to safeguard political stability and economic growth. “So, let us work. We have a mandate,” he said. “When the election comes, then we can battle it out. I have no issue with that.” Anwar also faces the prospect that the two largest Malay-Muslim parties – his national governing partner, United Malays National Organisation, and the opposition Pan-Malaysian Islamic Party (PAS) – may join forces. After successfully cooperating in two recent state elections, they are exploring a tie-up again in the next state poll in Malacca, which is expected in the coming months. Sentiment was building within the political establishment that Anwar was heading towards an inevitable defeat in the next general election, the people said, adding that the potential election delay was an attempt to change that outcome. The current term of the parliament ends on December 18, 2027, and elections must be held within 60 days after that. Election timing will partly depend on whether Umno and PAS can forge an alliance nationally. Top leaders in Umno, which leads the Barisan Nasional coalition, have said they support Anwar’s government although party members were pushing for a tie-up with the Islamist party for the sake of national unity. Anwar and his advisers are seeking a compelling political narrative that highlights his stewardship of Malaysia’s economy, which is getting a boost from an inflow of artificial intelligence-related investment and resilient electronics exports. The challenge was that many voters feel the pinch of rising costs, while frustration was growing among his supporters over the slower-than-expected pace of reforms, the people said. Recent state election losses for Anwar’s Pakatan Harapan coalition have exposed the discontent, as well as the sinking popularity of his own party, the People’s Justice Party. Known as PKR, it won just four of the 49 seats it contested in the state elections in Sabah, Johor and Negeri Sembilan since November. The Democratic Action Party, the biggest component of the bloc, also lost ground, including in Negeri Sembilan, where Pakatan Harapan was ousted after two terms in power. PKR and DAP spent decades championing reforms such as an independent anti-corruption agency, repealing laws like the Sedition Act, and requiring asset declarations by politicians and government officials. Yet after nearly four years in power, the lack of progress has contributed to voter frustration. That discontent was evident at DAP’s congress this month, where delegates voiced growing impatience with Anwar’s reform agenda even as they chose to remain in his government. Anwar’s party has also been weakened by the departure of prominent figures, including former economy minister Rafizi Ramli, who has since launched Parti Bersama Malaysia. The new party aims to court voters disillusioned by Anwar’s unmet reform promises but uneasy with the conservative, race- and religion-based politics championed by his rivals.

title: South Korean police look to charge 7 for lying about concrete structure in Jeju Air crash
description: The transport ministry officials put out false media statements claiming the localisers had been installed in line with regulations.
content: South Korea’s police said on Thursday they were seeking indictments of seven transport ministry officials over the 2024 Jeju Air crash that killed all but two of the 181 people on board. The Boeing 737-800 operated by Jeju Air skidded off the runway at Muan International Airport in southern South Korea after its landing gear failed to deploy, slamming into a concrete structure and bursting into flames. Authorities have found traces of bird strike in the plane’s engines and the plane’s two black boxes stopped recording about four minutes before the crash. Many experts say the concrete structure, which housed a set of antennas called a localiser that guides aircraft during landings, must be blamed for the crash as well – as it should have been built with more easily breakable materials. Police said on Thursday the seven officials were involved in the production of media statements that said the localisers were installed in accordance with relevant domestic and international regulations, though that was not true. Police said they referred the cases to prosecutors, asking for the seven officials to be indicted on a criminal charge of falsifying official documents. The penalty upon conviction could be up to seven years in prison. The Transport Ministry said it had no comment on the police announcement. Police said they were investigating nearly 70 other people, including those involved in installation of the localisers or operations of the Muan airport. The crash was South Korea’s deadliest aviation disaster since 1997. But no exact, formal cause of the crash has been announced and no one has been legally prosecuted yet. Last year, the Aviation and Railway Accident Investigation Board had planned to announce initial investigation results showing both of the plane’s engines sustained bird strikes and the pilots turned off the less damaged one just before the crash landing. The initial finding, which implied human errors, drew vehement protests from bereaved families and fellow pilots who accused authorities of trying to shift responsibility to the dead pilots. The investigation board later cancelled the announcement.

title: Chip sell-off helps boost China’s private funds as US$83.3b is pulled out of mutual funds
description: Mutual funds’ net assets under management shrank by 1.4 per cent in July, while private funds grew 8.7 per cent to record high.
content: The assets managed by China’s private funds grew last month as those of its mutual funds shrank, with investors diversifying their portfolios amid a sell-off of semiconductor shares. The net assets under management (AUM) of domestic mutual funds shrank by 560 billion yuan (US$83.3 billion), or 1.4 per cent month on month, in July to 39.11 trillion yuan, according to data released by the Asset Management Association of China on Wednesday. The decrease ended a four-month run of mutual fund growth, with net AUM hitting a record high 39.67 trillion yuan by the end of June, data from the association, which is backed by the China Securities Regulatory Commission, showed. By contrast, China’s domestic private funds managed a record 25.73 trillion yuan of assets by the end of July, up 2.07 trillion yuan, or 8.7 per cent, in a month, according to the association’s data. The July increase marked the 10th consecutive month of expansion of private offered funds in China. Mainland China’s markets and their global peers witnessed a slump in semiconductor shares in July amid growing concerns over the monetisation of artificial intelligence. Shanghai’s chip-heavy Star 50 Index plunged nearly 26 per cent in July, deeper than the 8 per cent fall in the broader CSI 300 Index, which tracks leading companies on the main boards in Shanghai and Shenzhen. However, thanks to a second-quarter boom, the Star 50 Index remains up 24.36 per cent so far this year, while the CSI 300 Index has fallen 2.68 per cent. Among private funds, those investing in unlisted equities expanded by 570 billion yuan, or 0.5 per cent month on month, to 11.93 trillion yuan by the end of last month. Meanwhile, the total net worth of domestic mutual equity funds declined 0.9 per cent month on month to 4.99 trillion yuan. The AUM of mixed-asset funds fell 18 per cent in July to 3.8 trillion yuan.

title: Japan fast-tracks anti-drone system amid China’s military build-up
description: Ukraine conflict shows the value of nimble procurement, which experts say could help Tokyo respond to Beijing’s expanding capabilities.
content: Tokyo is experimenting with a radically faster way of buying new weapons – picking a domestically built interceptor drone less than three months after launching the procurement process. Analysts say this shift could help Japan respond more quickly to China’s expanding military capabilities. The defence ministry’s Acquisition, Technology and Logistics Agency (ATLA) announced on Tuesday that it had signed a contract to buy Terra Drone’s Terra B1 system following competitive trials. The decision marks the first time the ministry has used its rapid-acquisition approach to acquire drones. ATLA described the roughly three-month process as “unprecedented”. Terra Drone said the B1 was the only system to pass the trials and that it would begin mass production. Delivery is planned for around September, with the Maritime Self-Defence Force expected to receive the system first. The Tokyo-based company has drawn on experience from Ukraine, where other systems in its portfolio have been used to counter long-range attack drones. It has also acquired stakes in two Ukrainian interceptor-drone companies. The Japanese authorities are seeking a more economical way of countering long-range, one-way attack drones than relying on conventional interceptor missiles. In pursuit of this capability, ATLA evaluated proposals from 38 companies before selecting four finalists for trials in July: the Terra B1, Beyond Vision’s BVQ404, Quantum Systems’ QS Interceptor and DZYNE Technologies’ IonStrike. While the value of the Terra B1 contract and number of units have not been disclosed, Masashi Murano, a senior fellow at the Hudson Institute, said he understood the ministry would initially acquire and operationally test a limited number. The speed of the process was striking, according to Jeffrey Hornung, Japan lead at the Rand Corporation’s National Security Research Division. “I am astonished by how quickly this has all transpired,” Hornung said, adding that in more than two decades following Japanese acquisitions, he could not recall a system moving through the process so quickly. Hornung said Japan had lacked a cost-effective interceptor for unmanned systems. The Terra B1 would not “level the playing field” on its own, he said, but could help counter new threats posed by China. Tokyo is drawing broader lessons from the war in Ukraine, where inexpensive drones and rapidly evolving counter-drone technologies have become central to high-intensity warfare. Japan’s latest defence white paper placed greater emphasis on unmanned systems as part of the “new ways of warfare” for which Tokyo must prepare. It also described China’s external stance and military activities as the country’s “greatest strategic challenge” while highlighting Beijing’s accelerating development of AI-enabled unmanned systems. In this context, Murano called the new rapid acquisition process a “groundbreaking step”, saying modern forces needed systems that could be produced at scale while remaining adaptable as adversaries developed countermeasures. The ability to quickly incorporate battlefield lessons into weapons, tactics and operational concepts – sustaining a “rapid innovation cycle” – would be “critical to victory”, he added. The circumstances surrounding the Terra B1 selection, however, make it unclear how readily the three-month timeline can be applied to future acquisitions. A source familiar with the procurement process said the solicitation requirements had been narrowly defined, creating the impression that the competition had been designed around the domestically produced Terra B1 from the outset. Meanwhile, Murano said questions remained over whether the ministry could move as quickly when confronted with a “genuinely new and unforeseen challenge”. That caution was shared by Yoshihiro Inaba, a defence expert and Japan correspondent for the Naval News website, who said the rapid approach was particularly suited to counter-drone systems and relatively inexpensive unmanned aircraft. More sophisticated weapons, however, required greater engineering expertise, technology, manpower and funding. “As a result, it is unlikely that every type of weapon system can be developed and manufactured within a short time frame,” Inaba said. Hornung also cautioned against treating the B1 process as a model for all future acquisitions, but said it set an important precedent for newer technologies and Japan’s willingness to accept greater risk. Tokyo was increasingly turning lessons from Ukraine into tangible capabilities for a potential conflict in Northeast Asia, he said, making it harder for Chinese military planners to be confident of success should hostilities involve Japan and the United States.

title: Can Singapore’s new anti-scam rules help stop online fraud before it occurs?
description: The new rules shift more responsibility to messaging platforms, in a move analysts say could become a regional model.
content: Singapore’s new rules for messaging platforms mark a significant shift in the country’s fight against scams, placing greater responsibility on digital services to help stop fraudsters before they reach potential victims, as the government seeks stronger penalties for non-compliance. Analysts said the requirements could reduce the number of people exposed to scams and offer a potential model for other Southeast Asian countries, while cautioning that sophisticated fraudsters could adapt and seek ways around the new safeguards. Singapore police announced earlier this month that online messaging platforms must implement measures to make it more difficult for unknown contacts to engage users and to alert people to potential scam risks. The rules build on the Online Criminal Harms Act (Ocha), which gives authorities powers to issue directions, codes of practice and implementation directives aimed at disrupting online criminal activity, including scams. Singapore authorities have framed the measures as part of a wider effort to reduce scam exposure before victims are drawn into conversations with fraudsters. The stakes are high: scam victims in Singapore lost about S$410.6 million (US$323 million) in the first half of this year, despite an overall fall in scam cases and losses from the same period previous year, according to the police’s midyear scam and cybercrime brief, issued on Wednesday. Authorities said messaging platforms were the top contact method used to reach victims in 27.6 per cent out of 16,821 scam cases. The new requirements include displaying warnings or signs of risk – such as country of origin or date of creation of an unknown account – and requiring users to give consent before being added to chat groups or channels by unfamiliar contacts. Platforms will also have to allow users to silence, filter or block messages or calls from numbers not saved in their contacts. The requirements will apply to seven platforms and services – WhatsApp, Telegram, WeChat, Apple iMessage, Apple FaceTime, Google Message and Google Meet – which must comply with the broader code by January 31, 2027. Measures relating to spoofing the Singapore government must be in place by September 30. The new requirements were a “wise” move likely to reduce scam cases, said David Lam, an associate fellow at ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute. “Online scamming is a dynamic threat landscape with scammers constantly evolving their methods and tactics to exploit victims,” he said, adding that messaging platforms had a critical role in stemming communication between fraudsters and potential victims. Failure to comply with Ocha directives without a reasonable excuse currently carries a fine of up to S$1 million, a figure the Ministry of Home Affairs has proposed raising to S$10 million as the city state battles a scam scourge. Chew Han Ei, an adjunct senior research fellow at the Institute of Policy Studies, said the new measures were a part of a significant shift to increase platform-level responsibility. “People text quickly, often under distraction or time pressure, and malicious actors deliberately exploit those opportunities. Good platform design should therefore help users make safer choices by default,” he said. Limits of prevention Analysts said the requirements could make it harder for scammers to reach potential victims, but warned against viewing them as a way to eradicate scams altogether. “Scams are a multibillion-dollar industry. The actors are constantly innovating at the same time as the companies, and they would probably find ways to circumvent these technical features,” said Shahzeb Mahmood, head of research at Tech Global Institute. Fraudsters could easily move to other platforms to conduct operations, he said. “A lot of people in Singapore, especially migrant workers, use platforms other than the seven mentioned and those are falling through the cracks.” Nuurrianti Jalli, a visiting fellow at the ISEAS – Yusof Ishak Institute, said scammers could take control of accounts in potential victims’ contact lists, or use a local number or established account to appear less suspicious. She also warned of user fatigue, whereby people become accustomed to dismissing warnings that are too vague or frequent. “Ultimately, these measures should reduce the number of people entering the scam funnel, but they will not eliminate scams,” Nuurrianti said. “I would describe them as friction rather than a firewall.” Analysts said non-compliance by major technology companies was less likely to be the main obstacle. Ocha took effect in February 2024, with its first directive issued last year to Meta Platforms – which owns Facebook and WhatsApp – to implement measures curbing Facebook impersonation scams. Similar directives were also issued to Apple and Google.
